📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that with the 2026 TV schedule heading into the holiday season, many are likely preparing for their favorite yuletide programming and getting ready for other festivities. We can reportedly count Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce amongst such people, as they are reportedly figuring out their first Christmas as a married couple. And apparently, deciding where to spend the holiday has become a little complicated. Per a newly introduced report, the newlyweds want to celebrate with both families without making either set of parents feel left out.

The Grammy winner and her Kansas City Chiefs tight end husband on married July 3 at Madison Square Garden, an event Kelce later described as one of the best nights of his life. Now, Rob Shuter alleges in his Naughty But Nice substack that the newlyweds have been discussing their first Christmas together. Per Shuter, an insider claims:.

Industry observers note that neither wants to disappoint their parents, but they also don’t want their first Christmas as a married couple to become a tug-of-war. They want everyone to feel included.

According to recent reports, it's a familiar holiday scheduling problem, although the families involved are rather more recognizable than most. Swift's parents, Andrea and Scott, have long been central to her Christmas celebrations, while Kelce remains close to his mother, Donna, and father, Ed. Swift even grew up on a Christmas tree farm in Pennsylvania, an experience she later turned into a holiday song. With both sets of traditions to consider, choosing where to spend the holiday allegedly hasn't been straightforward.

In a recent development, the Kelces already have some well-established food traditions. Kylie Kelce has praised Swift's baking alongside Donna Kelce's famous dinner rolls, so there would apparently be no shortage of people willing to contribute to Christmas dinner.

Also, the couple may already have a solution in mind. Instead of traveling between family gatherings or deciding which parents to visit, Shuter's sources notes Swift and Kelce are considering hosting Christmas themselves. The idea would bring their relatives to one celebration, although no final plans have been publicly declared. A second source told Shuter:.

They think bringing everyone together is the perfect answer. They get to start their own traditions without making either family feel they’ve lost out. It’s about creating one significant family Christmas.

It has been revealed that there's at least one reason a gathering away from a football stadium might be easier this year. As it so happens, the Chiefs don't have a game scheduled on Christmas Day in 2026, according to the team's published schedule. Kansas City is set to host the Newly introduced England Patriots on Dec. 21 and the San Francisco 49ers on Dec. 27, leaving Christmas Day free of a game-day obligation.

Sources indicate that last Christmas looked a little different for the couple. The Chiefs played the Denver Broncos at Arrowhead Stadium on Dec. 25, with Swift and her parents in attendance. She and Kelce also surprised several stadium employees with Christmas gifts.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

It has been revealed that kelce has already talked about looking forward to his first Christmas as a married man. Earlier this month, while promoting Tommy Hilfiger's winter collection, he told Women's Wear Daily he was excited to start newly introduced traditions with Swift. Although there's at least one he's apparently keeping: his mom Donna's homemade blueberry muffins.

It has been revealed that the families have spent Christmas together before. Back in 2023, the “Shake it Off” performer's brother Austin demonstrated up at a Chiefs game dressed as Santa Claus and surprised Kelce with a Christmas present. Both families also played a part in the couple's July wedding, with Austin serving as Swift's man of honor and Jason Kelce standing beside his brother as best man. The newlyweds even asked guests to make charitable donations instead of bringing wedding gifts. So, getting everyone together for Christmas wouldn't exactly be a first for the newlyweds.

Neither Swift nor Kelce has confirmed Shuter's report, so where they'll spend Christmas and whether both families will be there remains to be seen. But with the holiday just a few weeks away, they still have time to figure things out. However they end up celebrating, might I suggest checking out our list of the best Christmas movies? At least that'll give everyone something to watch once the presents are opened.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The video game research company Sensor Tower has updated its GTA 6 sales tracker to reveal the latest, albeit unofficial, sales data for the open-world crime game.
  • The report noted PS5 sales are dominating the mix, with GTA 6 selling 11.13 million units on PS5 so far, compared to 3.81 million on Xbox Series X|S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the video game research company Sensor Tower has updated its GTA 6 sales tracker to reveal the latest, albeit unofficial, sales data for the open-world crime game. According to Sensor Tower, GTA 6 has now sold 14.94 million total units via pre-purchases, which works out to about $1.45 billion in gross revenue. The report mentioned PS5 sales are dominating the mix, with GTA 6 selling 11.13 million units on PS5 so far, compared to 3.81 million on Xbox Series X|S. That means of the 14.94 million GTA 6 sales so far, 74% are on PS5 and 26% on Xbox Series X|S. In total, GTA 6 sales for PS5 have so far reached $1.08 billion in revenue, compared to $3.81 million for Xbox Series X|S. Sony and Microsoft keep about 30% of revenue due to their platform fees, so GTA 6 being a huge success directly benefits both of those companies. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wmKu9Uow-os The huge gap in sales between platforms is not surprising because the PS5 is dominating Xbox Series X|S in terms of console sales. In fact, GTA 6 is breaking records on Xbox, Microsoft has said, and the sales numbers for GTA 6 on Xbox line up with Xbox's share of the console market. Sensor Tower is projecting as many as 25 million total pre-purchases for GTA 6 by launch, and if the 75/25 split holds, that would be about 18.5 million units on PS5 and 6.5 million on Xbox Series X|S. GTA 6 is the most preordered game of all time for PlayStation and Xbox. If the 10 million pre-purchase number is real, that would break a record for most preorders set by Cyberpunk 2077 (8 million). Sony holds the marketing rights for GTA 6 on PS5, but that doesn't mean that Microsoft is doing nothing to try to promote the game. Just recently, Microsoft announced a GTA 6-inspired custom Xbox console that sits inside an alligator. Circana has released newly introduced data that shows that GTA 6 holds 29% purchase intent among US console and PC gamers. That means nearly 1 in 3 console and PC gamers in the US proposal to buy GTA 6–this is the highest purchase intent that Circana has ever measured for any game. GTA 6 may indeed be a gigantic hit commercially, and one that helps lift the entire industry with increased sales of hardware and accessories. But anyone looking to buy a new console to play GTA 6 is set for major sticker shock, as consoles today are more expensive than ever. Not only that, but GTA 6 is not going to save the industry’s many serious and deep-rooted complications, experts believe. GTA 6 rolls out on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game's file size is about 212GB, and thankfully, preloading is already underway. The game unlocks on November 19 at midnight local time, and that means US players will be among the last in the world to get in. People in New Zealand, meanwhile, will be the first in the world to play GTA 6. If you're thinking about booking a flight to the land of Hobbits, here are some tips for packing your PS5 safely.

As MAGA Melts Down, MAHA Is Also Breaking Apart—Starting With the Moms

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2392 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • suspended his presidential campaign and endorsed Donald Trump, bringing his ragtag bunch of supporters—crunchy mamas, anti-vaxxers, and conspiracy theorists; testosterone bros, peptide enthusiasts, and people who put a “COEXIST” bumper sticker on their car in the 1990s—along for the ride.
  • “I think we are seeing a fracturing of the MAHA movement as those concerns start pulling people in different directions,” says Sandro Galea, dean of the Bursky School of Public Health at Washington University in St.
  • In a recent development, the crack-up didn’t start with the midterms, though the fact that most MAHA-backed candidates lost certainly accelerated it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In August 2024, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. suspended his presidential campaign and endorsed Donald Trump, bringing his ragtag bunch of supporters—crunchy mamas, anti-vaxxers, and conspiracy theorists; testosterone bros, peptide enthusiasts, and people who put a “COEXIST” bumper sticker on their car in the 1990s—along for the ride. But now that the blue wave or tsunami—pick your tortured water metaphor—has come to pass, the fractures within MAHA threaten to break the movement apart, driven by bitter disappointment with the Trump administration.

“I think we are seeing a fracturing of the MAHA movement as those concerns start pulling people in different directions,” says Sandro Galea, dean of the Bursky School of Public Health at Washington University in St. Louis. Groups that are interested in healthier food are not necessarily the same as groups opposed to vaccines, he points out; it’s not a sure thing that those groups will continue to find common cause.

In a recent development, the crack-up didn’t start with the midterms, though the fact that most MAHA-backed candidates lost certainly accelerated it. Earlier this year, Trump had to withdraw his nomination of MAHA darling Casey Means for surgeon general after her stance on vaccines made it impossible for Republicans to get enough votes to support her confirmation. In May, MAHA ally Marty Makary, the commissioner of the Food and Drug Administration, resigned, reportedly because of pressure from the administration to authorize fruit-flavored vapes. And in October, Calley Means—Casey’s brother—resigned from his high-level post under Secretary Kennedy at Health and Human Services, with MAHA outrage on unmet promises growing.

Three days after the midterms, Joe Rogan released a bomb-throwing, names-naming, two-plus-hour interview with Calley Means, in which the former Kennedy adviser used the word “demonic,” possibly in the literal sense, eight times.

Sources indicate that the massive takeaway was that Susie Wiles seemed to have told Kennedy to go sit in a corner and play by himself. All roads to Trump went through her office, and according to Means, she slow-walked, watered down, or outright quashed many MAHA priorities. According to Means, she did this primarily because of her and her family’s financial ties to lobbying on behalf of big business.

Wiles did not respond to a request for comment, but a spokesperson for Wiles previously told Axios that these allegations were “outrageous, defamatory, and provably false.”.

Industry observers note that means argued that MAHA managed some wins: Trump signed an executive order to boost research on the use of psychedelics for treating mental health conditions. The newly introduced food pyramid instructs Americans to eat more steak than oatmeal. (In this economy?) There have been other MAHA victories too: The administration made it easier for Americans to get a handful of unproven injectable peptides, including the “Wolverine stack.” Trump signed an executive order in support of regenerative farming. The administration requested changes to the labels on testosterone products in an effort to make the hormone easier to prescribe—good news for Pete Hegseth’s promise of a “high-T Department of War.” It asked food manufacturers to voluntarily phase out some food dyes. It has sought to reduce the number of recommended childhood vaccines.

Means did not cite the United States recently losing its measles-elimination status as a win, though that was also a result of MAHA talking points.

According to recent reports, the MAGA-MAHA mind meld provided plenty for the wellness bros, but precious little of what MAHA moms were expecting from their alliance with Trump. Tiffany Cianci, a high-profile MAHA advocate who goes by @thevinomom on Instagram, states the results were “small things,” not the massive systemic changes that had been promised.

In an emailed statement, a spokesperson for HHS pushed back on this narrative, writing, in part, “HHS has delivered the most sweeping public health reforms in modern history…Across the federal government, the administration has transformed food and nutrition policy, invested more than $1 billion in regenerative agriculture and farm modernization, and taken action to address harmful chemical exposures.”.

In a recent development, health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. delivers remarks during an event at HHS in August. The event highlighted a series of 'landmark actions' to improve the nation's food.

In a recent development, for the MAHA moms, there are two original sins of Trump 2.0. The first is the administration’s outright support for glyphosate, an herbicide that has been classified as a probable carcinogen by a World Health Organization agency. The second is its failure to put out a definition of ultra-processed foods, which the movement sees as the first step toward curbing those foods, particularly in school lunches. One was never released; Means alleged to Rogan that ultra-processed-food initiatives such as this were stymied by White House officials including Wiles, who he said told him, “I need sugar money.” Reporting found that food CEOs leaned on the White House to make the definition go away.

A White House official noted on background that the definition for ultra-processed food remains a priority and is actively being worked on by relevant agencies. White House spokeswoman Allison Schuster said that “the MAHA coalition has found a champion in President Trump…The administration has already secured extensive victories for the MAHA agenda, including overhauling the dietary guidelines for Americans, axing artificial ingredients in our food supply, and investing in regenerative farming.”.

According to recent reports, however, the Trump administration has arguably hindered research on ultra-processed foods in other ways. A leading scientist who was studying ultra-processed food’s link to diabetes and obesity took early retirement from the National Institutes of Health last year after NIH officials, he said, censored the reporting of some of his study results because the study didn’t prove the hypothesis of ultra-processed-food addiction as they had hoped it would. If he’s to be believed, one of our best hopes for understanding the health risks of ultra-processed foods exited due to the actions of MAHA officials. (Vanity Fair has reached out to HHS for comment on the allegations of censorship; an HHS spokesperson previously told The Upcoming York Times, “NIH scientists have, and will, continue to conduct interviews regarding their research through written responses or other means. We remain committed to promoting gold-standard research and advancing public health priorities.”).

According to recent reports, “We do have a food supply that’s nearly 70% ultra-processed food,” indicates Jessica Knurick, a registered dietitian and science communicator on social media. She counters that many of MAHA’s alleged priorities are aligned with the hopes of public health workers and nutritionists—yet the movement writ large has eroded trust in the very professionals who do that work. “They really want fewer environmental toxins. If you want that, you need strong regulation on corporations,” she says. “They voted in an administration that is decisively deregulatory.”.

“All of the things that the MAHA movement claimed to have wanted,” she adds, “this administration has legislated in the exact opposite direction.”.

See, for instance, the glyphosate debacle. Instead of curbing the herbicide, something for which he’d long been an advocate, Kennedy got on board with Trump’s support of it, including an executive order that actually prioritized production of the chemical under the bizarre guise of national security. Then the administration supported Roundup weed killer manufacturer Monsanto, now owned by Bayer, in a case before the Supreme Court, which resulted in a decision shielding the tech giant from state-level lawsuits brought by those who believed they’d been harmed by the glyphosate-containing product. (Glyphosate-based Roundup products are no longer produced for the US residential market.).

This flew in the face of everything MAHA believed about Kennedy’s priorities. Vani Hari, a MAHA influencer who goes by the Food Babe, has been called both the Jenny McCarthy of food and a Democratic infiltrator. She thinks that the last nearly two years resulted in some positive change. She also tells me that she’s become somewhat disillusioned: “There have also been deeply disappointing decisions, particularly when it comes to glyphosate and pesticides.”.

Despite it all, the HHS secretary continues to be deified by the vast majority of MAHA leaders, who don’t blame Kennedy for these setbacks. Cianci, however, blames just about everyone involved. “What I see within MAHA right now is a fracturing into one very, very small sliver that loves the proximity to power and the fundraising. They unfortunately tied their hitch to the wrong horse, which is partisanship,” she claims. “And you have the rest of us that actually want our kids to be healthy.”.

Supporters of the Make America Healthy Again movement are seen at a news conference on removing synthetic dyes from America's food supply, at the Health and Human Services Headquarters in Washington, DC, 2025.

If there is a road forward for MAHA, it might be best exemplified by Elizabeth Frost, a community health advocate and the leader of MAHA Ohio. She comes by her skepticism of the pharmaceutical industry honestly, after growing up in Appalachian Ohio during the height of the opioid epidemic. She now runs a political consultancy in the state, which she indicates works with both parties.

Beginning last year, Frost partnered with epidemiologists from Yale to find out how the people of East Palestine, Ohio, were still being affected by toxic exposures after the 2023 derailment of a train filled with hazardous materials. Frost went to bat for the scientists, lending her local grassroots credibility to their study on water quality in the town.

In a recent development, “I think there is a broader anti-corporate movement in America that hasn’t really been given a home with either established party because both parties have their own pet corporate interests,” she tells me. After Kennedy’s ascent, she had hoped for a focus on the MAHA issues that enjoy broad support. “Vaccines are not the most popular issue even for MAHA. Most people in MAHA would prefer for the majority of time to be spent talking about issues that are a little bit more unifying”—rather than something like Steak ’n Shake’s now using beef tallow for its french fries. “It’s just not where people’s hearts are.”.

In a recent development, speaking of no heart: Stephen Miller has been promoted to chief of staff after Wiles was forced out in the wake of the midterms. Both Calley Means and Secretary Kennedy have celebrated the move. “Stephen Miller is the strongest MAHA supporter in the administration. It’s time to unleash the Kraken,” Kennedy wrote on X.

But some MAHA moms are not so sure about the kraken. Cianci notes that within MAHA, “people are very, very, very uncomfortable” with Miller. “If you’re just going to do what you’ve been told to do and take it to the extreme—he’s like the human embodiment of the paper clip problem,” she says.

Frost is similarly concerned about how things might go under Miller. “I don’t expect that on environmental exposures, industrial contamination, a strong streak against corporate influence—I doubt we’re going to get those things,” she notes. She is also dismayed by MAHA leadership’s embrace of convicted rapist Russell Brand. “What the hell are we doing?” she wonders.

A person familiar with MAHA thinking who spoke on background counters that while it’s fair to say that Miller might be polarizing, he is also not beholden to corporate interests the way Wiles was, making him far less likely to block the scrutiny of pesticides and healthy food policies.

It has been revealed that cianci, Frost, and Hari all hope that MAHA will survive by focusing on policy over partisanship. “I also believe MAHA’s future must be bipartisan,” Hari wrote in an email.

According to recent reports, cianci sees opposition to data centers as the next big problem on which MAHA can lead. And she hopes that the anti-corporate tilt she sees in MAHA will spread. “We had a record number of candidates get elected to Congress this year that turned down all corporate PAC money. That is indicative of the MAHA movement. That is indicative of anti-corruption. And I think they’re going hand in glove.”.

Industry observers note that frost would like to see Republicans work with progressives like Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez on shared goals, like getting pesticides out of the food supply. She wants legislators to realize that “the way to hold their seat is to work across aisles on problems that their constituents care about.”.

In a recent development, perhaps MAHA can reinvent itself by leveraging some of its most popular issues to make common cause with Democrats. After all, 30% of midterm voters told pollsters that they support the MAHA movement, while many more—the vast majority of Americans—say that food additives and pesticide use should be more regulated. A plurality of Americans do not want data centers in their communities. The movement’s best hope for staying relevant is probably the (right now very pissed) MAHA moms, whose concerns about food and pollution were always the most broadly resonant parts of the MAHA platform—rather than a yen for peptides, beef tallow, or testosterone.

Recent findings suggest that most people want to be able to afford healthy food and effective health care. Trump’s rule has not made those things more accessible, with high cost of living, massive cuts to Medicaid, the ending of certain Affordable Care Act subsidies, and reductions in federal funding for SNAP benefits.

In a recent development, the challenge with a rebrand is that the connection to MAGA is right there in the name. But Trump’s presidency clearly has a shelf life, and MAHA wants to outlast him. “If anyone has any ideas on how to change the name of a political movement,” Frost says, “let me know.”.

According to recent reports, no one knows yet exactly what the next-gen Xbox console, Project Helix, will be, but most people are convinced it won't be cheap. The ongoing memory shortage has driven current-gen console prices skyward since 2024, with the Xbox Series X rising from $500 in 2020 to $800 in 2026. Project Helix is projected to cost as much as $1,800 at launch, but Microsoft aims to keep the price down when it eventually releases the device. According to VP of next-gen Jason Ronald, techniques like neural rendering could help manage costs. "It's definitely a challenging time, but as a system and a platform designer, it's also one of the most exciting times, because we have to invent entirely fresh technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable," Ronald noted in the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine. "This is a substantial reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering, because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years." In a nutshell, neural rendering uses AI to predict and generate high-quality video game frames while using only a portion of hardware power, similar to upscaling technoligies like PSSR, DLSS, and FSR. This could enable next-generation visual leaps while keeping the console accessible and reasonably priced for consumers. The other benefit is that the AI software models can improve over time through updates, as console hardware remains fixed over its lifespan, hence Ronald's quote about improvements reaching Project Helix over a few years into its run. It remains to be seen how these breakthroughs will be spread across Project Helix, which Ronald teased as a family of devices that can address home, mobile, and cloud gaming needs. Xbox suggesting that it's working smarter to deliver an affordable gaming experience is an idea that Shawn Layden touched on recently, as the former PlayStation boss spoke about how Sony should be less concerned with chasing improved graphics and rather focus on making a cheaper PS5-level console instead. Meanwhile, Sony is squeezing more life out of the PS5 generation with AI-guided upscaling technology, and the base model PS5 got its own version of this in the form of Quick Spectral Super Resolution. Originally available for only two games, QSSR is coming to more titles in the future, like Control Resonant, Arc Raiders, and No Man's Sky.

Garmin Cyclists Can Now Make Themselves Appear on Waze in Real Time

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (469 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cyclists who ride with Garmin gear can now appear as live, moving icons on the Waze driving app, and nearby drivers will receive an alert to slow down and watch for them on the road.
  • For riders already using Garmin devices, opting in costs nothing and adds a new layer of safety, particularly on roads where drivers may not expect cyclists.
  • Recent findings suggest that riders can simply opt in once through Garmin Connect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cyclists who ride with Garmin gear can now appear as live, moving icons on the Waze driving app, and nearby drivers will receive an alert to slow down and watch for them on the road.

For riders already using Garmin devices, opting in costs nothing and adds a new layer of safety, particularly on roads where drivers may not expect cyclists. The feature is rolling out now, but you should be aware of its limitations.

Recent findings suggest that riders can simply opt in once through Garmin Connect. After that, sharing starts automatically when an outdoor cycling activity begins and stops when the ride ends. While a ride is underway, Waze consumers near the cyclist see a cyclist icon move along the road and receive a Live Cycling Alert reminding them to slow down and stay aware.

The feature runs on LiveTrack, Garmin's existing live location-sharing tool, which lets friends and family follow a rider's real-time location, speed, course, and more. Garmin notes this collaboration extends that peace of mind to motorists, giving them greater awareness of their surroundings.

In a recent development, garmin notes its location sharing is temporary and session-based. The rider's name, identity, and route are hidden, and no personal information is shared or displayed in Waze. Drivers see only an anonymous icon and the alert.

You'll need a few things to get this feature up and running:.

A compatible Garmin Edge bike computer or Garmin watch.

A phone running Garmin Connect with a data connection.

An outdoor cycling activity (the feature doesn't apply to indoor rides).

The good news is using the feature is free: LiveTrack costs nothing on compatible Garmin bike computers and watches, and Waze is free for drivers.

This new feature is a great safety perk, but there are real-world caveats worth considering:.

Industry observers note that this feature is for Waze only. Alerts reach drivers only when Waze is open on their phone. Google Maps, which has far more customers, is excluded, so a large portion of the drivers you share the road with won't see you this way.

It depends on your phone's signal. Your position travels from the Garmin to your phone, then to Garmin's servers, then to Waze, and finally to the driver's phone. On a patchy rural signal, a few seconds of lag could put the icon on the wrong side of a bend from where you actually are. A rider who leaves their phone at home or whose phone loses signal simply won't show up on a Waze map, as a ride without a data connection is invisible to Waze.

Finally, remember to treat this safety feature as an extra perk, not a guarantee. At the end of the day, it isn't a replacement for bike lights, bright clothing, and defensive riding.

  • To catch you up in case you haven’t seen the original series, Jen Affleck, a 20-something Mormon wife and mother, joined MomTok in Utah to fight against the typical social norms and stereotypes that are common within the religion.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that if you’ve ever watched The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, you know there’s no shortage of drama. Just look at Taylor Frankie Paul, who’s had a swingers scandal, the cancellation of her season of The Bachelorette, custody concerns with her children, and chaos surrounding production. But the Hulu reality series was popular and created a lot of buzz, so I was not surprised when they revealed the spinoff, The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County, currently on the 2026 TV schedule. However, the fact that it feels like the majority of the women in the newly introduced show are not Mormon and that some aren’t even wives is a bit weird and an interesting choice, considering the title, and viewers (including myself) have taken notice.

To catch you up in case you haven’t seen the original series, Jen Affleck, a 20-something Mormon wife and mother, joined MomTok in Utah to fight against the typical social norms and stereotypes that are common within the religion. After appearing in Season 34 of Dancing with the Stars as a celebrity contestant alongside fellow Mormon Wives star Whitney Leavitt, the mother of three with a fourth on the way decided to stay in Southern California, citing the fracturing of MomTok and the need for therapy to recover from everything that happened.

Seeming to instead have decided to jump right into another reality series, which again is an interesting choice, Jen has brought together a new group of friends, all of whom are mothers with their own drama and secrets, but who are not all Mormon, despite the show’s name. One has even admitted to signing on for the heightened visibility reality TV brings.

According to recent reports, it’s hard not to notice that The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County is a cast divided into two groups, with the women who are Mormons being outnumbered by the women who are not. In the season premiere, cast member Aspyn Ovard (who's got a memorable storyline about being part of a throuple) says, “We’ve all been shaped by Mormonism in one way or another,” which is a bit of a vague statement when we don’t know all the details of the backgrounds of many of these women, and even she makes it clear that she’s very closed off to the church and its teachings.

I'm not the only one who has noticed this either, as this conversation has popped up all over social media, including places like Reddit, where fans have asked why non-Mormons are "even on the show." I get it's weird to call out someone's religious preferences, but when your show is called Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, I do think that leads to a certain expectation.

Industry observers note that when you’re in the business of entertainment, building a franchise off of something successful and popular makes sense. But it’s hard to escape the weirdness of not really delivering on what your show’s title promises. All of this is not to say that the women who make up the OC spinoff cast don’t have compelling lives of their own, because they do, but the religious branding doesn’t entirely fit and feels like more of a subplot than a main focus, like it is in the original series.

And it all makes me wonder if the title should have just been something more reflective of Jen Affleck specifically? Just spitballing here.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

In a recent development, for a reality show that’s supposed to be centered around Mormons, The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County actually positions them to be the villains of the season. McCall DaPron, the older sister of the OG series’ Mayci Neeley, exhibits confrontational behavior. She gets into frequent clashes with other cast members, often leaving them to wonder whether it’s possible to keep this friend group together.

In a recent development, her strong commitment to her faith and her efforts to share it with others, including best friend and co-star Jordan McClanahan (whom she successfully converted), rubs anyone not as devoted the wrong way. This is especially true when her need to influence others’ opinions and actions creates conflict.

It has been revealed that the Secret Lives of Mormon Wives has had a seemingly endless amount of drama and scandals over four seasons, which are streaming with a Hulu subscription, but Mayci always came across like the most supportive one of the group on that show, where McCall seems less inclined to stay neutral. It’s hard to know how much of the drama is manipulated with editing, but it’s another interesting choice on a series that already seems to be trying to break its own formula.

All of this noted, if there ends up being a second season of the OC spinoff, I will still definitely be tuning in!

Between Jen being pregnant with her fourth child at the same time she decides she wants a divorce, Aspyn trying to get her ex-husband to spend time with her current throuple, and Salomé Andrea figuring out if she can reconcile with a man she began dating in ninth grade and couldn’t marry in the Mormon church before she ultimately walked away from both, it is all definitely weird, but just weird enough to make me want to see what happens next.

Industry News: 10 Movies Like ‘Interstellar’ You Should Watch Next

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1264 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Christopher Nolan’s 2014 megahit Interstellar has it all: massive sci-fi ideas, cool robots, ugly crying, and a Matt Damon character in need of rescuing.
  • It has been revealed that if you loved both the special effects in Interstellar that make space travel feel viscerally thrilling (and terrifying) and the mind-blowing concepts, this is the film for you.
  • If you’re looking for more existential missions with somewhat reluctant heroes in space, Project Hail Mary is your next stop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Christopher Nolan’s 2014 megahit Interstellar has it all: massive sci-fi ideas, cool robots, ugly crying, and a Matt Damon character in need of rescuing. Grounded in the intensity of the human experience, this story of humanity’s potential extinction and the sacrifice of one man to save it doesn’t just deliver exotic planets and thrilling spaceship maneuvers; it also provides all the feels as Joseph Cooper (Matthew McConaughey) sacrifices everything he has in an effort to save the entire human race. It’s one of the best science fiction films ever made, with Nolan’s signature complexity, time manipulations, and emotional wallop. If you love this movie, here are ten more that offer a similar viewing experience.

It has been revealed that if you loved both the special effects in Interstellar that make space travel feel viscerally thrilling (and terrifying) and the mind-blowing concepts, this is the film for you. Stanley Kubrick’s 1968 epic (written by sci-fi master Arthur C. Clarke) traces humanity’s development from mildly smart apes to spacefaring capitalists who discover a mysterious obelisk on the Moon that sparks a mission to Jupiter. While it operates in a colder emotional key than Nolan’s film, 2001: A Space Odyssey absolutely delivers on the epic side of things (and the cool—if slightly deranged and deadly—artificial intelligences). Stream 2001: A Space Odyssey on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

If you’re looking for more existential missions with somewhat reluctant heroes in space, Project Hail Mary is your next stop. When the Sun begins to dim due to the interference of an alien entity, scientists identify the one nearby star that isn’t being similarly affected. Brilliant molecular biologist Ryland Grace (Ryan Gosling) winds up forced to go on what is assumed to be a fatal, one-way mission into deep space to try to find a way to save humanity, unexpectedly assisted by a charming alien he names Rocky. It’s got the same emotional volume and massive ideas as Interstellar, and fans of Nolan’s film will love it. Stream Project Hail Mary on MGM+ or Philo, or rent it on Prime Video.

In a recent development, part of what makes Interstellar so compelling is the stakes: The human race is slowly dying, and a handful of people must make incredible sacrifices to save it. That’s the vibe of Sunshine, set in a future where the Sun is dimming and a spacecraft is dispatched to deliver an enormous bomb designed to reignite the Sun’s fusion cycle. But the mission is the second attempt after the first ship vanished mysteriously seven years earlier, and when the latest crew stumbles on the derelict wreck of the first mission, things swiftly descend into violence and madness—but the crew remains determined to save the world, no matter the cost. Rent Sunshine on Prime Video.

Interstellar works in large part because of the emotional dynamics at play. McConaughey’s character leaves his children behind and is forced to witness them growing up without him, missing out on their lives and saddled with the knowledge that they resent him despite the necessity of his mission. Arrival is a First Contact story focused on language—linguist Louise Banks (Amy Adams) is drafted into an effort to understand the strange, complex language of the aliens. As she slowly builds to an understanding of how the aliens communicate and perceive time itself, her own heartbreak and loss come into play, giving this film a similarly devastating emotional punch. Stream Arrival on Kanopy or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

Family dynamics and the toll of lonely space missions fuel Ad Astra, a film with the same emotional core as Interstellar. Twenty-nine years ago, famed astronaut Clifford McBride (Tommy Lee Jones) led the Lima Project, a space station around Neptune searching for intelligent life. Thirteen years ago, Earth lost contact with him. When bursts of energy emanating from Neptune threaten to end life on Earth, his son, Roy (Brad Pitt), is dispatched to try to make contact with his father. It’s an epic journey with a powerful climax that will satisfy fans of Interstellar in every way. Stream Ad Astra on Netflix or rent it on Prime Video.

Ridley Scott’s prequel to Alien has its flaws, but if you’re looking for a sense of epic spacefaring adventure in the same key as Interstellar, it’s perfect. When two scientists discover a star map apparently left behind by ancient aliens, they secure funding from the Wayland Corporation to organize a space expedition to the indicated planet. Accompanied by a colorful crew and the android David, they discover an apparently abandoned outpost of the species dubbed the Engineers. The story wrestles with questions about humanity’s origins, purpose, and potential—but this being an Alien film, things swiftly turn horrifying. Rent Prometheus on Prime Video.

Adapted from Carl Sagan’s 1985 novel, Contact follows astronomer Dr. Ellie Arroway (Jodie Foster), who becomes involved with an effort to decipher a signal originating from the star Vega. The signal turns out to be a set of instructions for constructing a one-person spacecraft of some kind, and Arroway is eventually selected as the candidate to take the journey. There’s a sense of courage in the face of the unknown that’s similar to Interstellar, as well as the thrill of strapping into a spaceship and pressing the ignition. Plus, there’s the added bonus of seeing one of the greatest trick shots in cinematic history. Rent Contact on Prime Video.

Stanislaw Lem’s 1961 novel Solaris explores what Lem saw as the impossibility of ever understanding a truly alien life. The two major adaptations—Andrei Tarkovsky's 1972 version and Steven Soderbergh’s 2002 take starring George Clooney—are both worth watching, but Tarkovsky’s film is a masterpiece of psychological horror. The story is set mainly aboard a space station orbiting a planet covered in what appears to be a sentient "ocean" and chronicles the strange haunting and inexplicable experiences of the humans living on the station. If your favorite part of Interstellar is the ending when things get trippy and weird, you’ll probably love Solaris. Stream Solaris on HBO Max, Plex, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

Industry observers note that the story of a mission to Jupiter’s moon Europa to search for intelligent life, Europa Report has the same sense of terrifying excitement that accompanies Interstellar’s missions to the different candidate planets. Leaning into the fragility of life in an environment not designed to support it, the mission crew face a steady stream of loss and danger as they work to catch sight of alien life on the frozen, deadly moon, ultimately faced with making terrifying sacrifices in order to provide humanity with the answers that it seeks. Stream Europa Report on Netflix, Kanopy, or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

A film based on a 1956 epic science fiction poem written by a Swedish Nobel Laureate might seem like an unlikely match for fans of Interstellar, but it’s actually perfect. As the Earth becomes uninhabitable, humanity begins launching ships to colonize Mars. When one such ship, the Aniara, is damaged and veers irreversibly off course, the passengers and crew are faced with the knowledge that they will sail off into the void without hope of rescue. Within a few years, despair has driven some to suicide and madness, while others cling to the possibility that they might yet find a way back. The film offers a different perspective on the existential crisis of humanity’s extinction, exploring the worst-case scenario to its bitter, bleak end. Stream Aniara on Kanopy or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

One beneficiary of that was Disney Plus' Percy Jackson and the Olympians, which got a much-needed boost prior to the premiere of its third season.

Recent findings suggest that the Rick Riordan adaptation's co-showrunner, Dan Shotz told IGN that the Percy Jackson team had "heard that there was a huge boost in viewers during that period because everybody obviously was searching for The Odyssey." That came at the perfect time for the series, as its second season had concluded in July, ahead of the third season's premiere on Nov. 20. "Anybody who didn't know about Sea of Monsters found it," said Shotz. He's referencing the second book in the original series of novels, which was adapted in the show's second season and largely plays with the narrative structure and characters of The Odyssey.

It has been revealed that shotz added that it was surreal to see Nolan's vision of the story versus the show's. While Percy Jackson is obviously based on a story inspired by The Odyssey, the two pieces still share a lot of the same themes and plot beats because of the shared source material of Homer's original epic. His favorite part of the Odysseus-versus-Percy discussion was the memes joking about how Percy did the same journey in seven days and was far more efficient. The Odyssey isn't the only thing that has boosted interest in the excellent Disney adaptation. Recently, the first two seasons were added to Netflix, and it quickly became one of the streaming services' top performers.

According to recent reports, if The Odyssey got you into Percy Jackson, then the imminent release of season 3 is sure to be exciting. The newly introduced season will adapt the third book, The Titan's Curse, which is something of a tonal shift for the series into darker territory. With five books in total, it also means the show is over the hump. Unfortunately, Disney has yet to announce a fourth season, which is starting to worry fans.

Season 3 will see the return of Percy, Annabeth, and Grover as the trio embark on a new quest that puts them in the middle of a battle between the gods and titans. They'll also meet new faces along the way, such as the Di Angelo siblings, the goddess Artemis, and her hunters. Walker Scobell, Aryan Simhadri, and Leah Sava Jeffries will reprise their roles as Percy, Grover, and Annabeth respectively. Newcomers to the cast include Levi Chrisopulos as Nico di Angelo, Dafne Keen as Artemis, Kate McKinnon as Aphrodite, Ming-Na Wen as Hera, and Holt McCallany as Atlas.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A drive-by shooting in Southern California ended with no injuries and an arrest after the gunman reportedly opened fire near a business and office campus that houses Xbox subsidiary InXile Entertainment. According to Aftermath and local affiliate KTLA5, the shooting occurred on November 11 at an office building on the former Marine Corps Air Station in Tustin, California. The police department posted on Facebook that, after uncovering "multiple shell casings in the area," local detectives worked "around the clock" to locate the suspect. Sergeant Christopher Peterson told Aftermath on November 13 that although the investigation is still ongoing, an unnamed suspect had been apprehended "less than 48 hours" after the shooting. "Officers got there [on November 11]," Sergeant Peterson remarked. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt. Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why." An InXile Entertainment spokesperson corroborated the incident with Aftermath, expressing relief about the situation. "We're relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office,” the spokesperson said. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate." Founded in 2002, InXile Entertainment has been under the Xbox Game Studios umbrella since 2018. Since its founding, the studio has developed several games, from the 2004 ARPG The Bard's Tale to the 2011 action-adventure Hunted: The Demon's Forge to the 2014 post-apocalyptic RPG Wasteland 2. Right now, the team is working on Clockwork Revolution, a steampunk ARPG not too dissimilar from immersive sims like BioShock and Dishonored. It has no release date right now, but InXile Entertainment is targeting a 2027 window for PC and Xbox Series X|S.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the “Siri Recap” feature that Apple announced in September is finally available in a developer beta, and I’ve spent the last 24 hours with the feature turned on.
  • It has been revealed that I have a button in the watch’s Control Center that can turn the recapping abilities off, but if I forget to do so, Siri listens to everything.
  • The recaps somberly mention silly memes my kids were laughing about, and make major bullet points out of offhand remarks from brief conversations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the “Siri Recap” feature that Apple announced in September is finally available in a developer beta, and I’ve spent the last 24 hours with the feature turned on. It’s even more unsettling than the “Live Rewind” feature that rolled out at the same time. It listens to all my conversations, and produces summaries that are both helpful and deeply creepy.

It has been revealed that I have a button in the watch’s Control Center that can turn the recapping abilities off, but if I forget to do so, Siri listens to everything. I’ll get a recap of my entire evening, presented in roughly hour-long chunks, including things I would have completely forgotten I had even heard about.

The recaps somberly mention silly memes my kids were laughing about, and make major bullet points out of offhand remarks from brief conversations. If a conversation sticks to a single topic, I’ll often get a reasonably good summary of it, with specific facts and numbers highlighted; but just as often, Siri will get confused and mix up several topics or completely mishear a name or phrase.

Apple has four features that it considers part of “audio intelligence":.

Music recognition, better known as Shazam. We’ve had a version of this on the Apple Watch for a long time now, although it has some improvements and now identifies music automatically.

According to recent reports, sound recognition, which can notify you about doorbells and babies crying. A version of this debuted in 2020 as an accessibility feature.

Live Rewind, which gives you an on-wrist transcript of the last 15 seconds of detected speech.

Siri Recaps, which summarizes entire conversations for you to read on your phone.

According to recent reports, live Rewind had the flashiest demo from the Apple event: A server rattled off the day’s specials at a restaurant, and then the Apple Watch-wearing diner checked his watch to see a readout of exactly which dishes had just been mentioned. The utility is both obvious and kind of unnecessary: Why wouldn’t you just ask the server to repeat the list while they’re standing right there?

I haven’t found myself using Live Rewind, except out of curiosity about how the feature works. I discovered that it doesn’t pick up song lyrics very well, and also that by the time I think to check what was just noted in a conversation, more than 15 seconds has passed since the part I was unsure about. I haven’t yet found a reason to use it for real.

Recent findings suggest that but Siri Recaps? Those are both useful and unsettling. I enabled the feature, and decided to test it out later. But since it was on, it dutifully listened in as I picked up my son from school and gave him an patch on an ailing family member’s health. We stopped by the library, and along the way we chatted about a variety of things: holiday travel intends, library policies, and the possibility of humans living in space in the future. Siri was listening to it all.

Recent findings suggest that after you're updated to 27.3, go into the Watch app, tap Siri, and turn on Siri Recap. You can set a schedule for when it should listen (for example, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., if you want it on for the work day but off for the evening). You'll need to set a passcode on your watch, and you'll be guided through a step to upgrade your audio connection. The control center on the watch will have a button you can use to turn Siri recaps on and off at will. To read your recaps, go to the Siri app on your phone.

It has been revealed that as promised, the recaps do not identify speakers. They do not contain an exact transcript, and there is no way to listen to a recording to check what exactly was mentioned. This is probably good for privacy and for relationships; there’s no way to prove that your spouse said such-and-such exact thing. I can also tell people I am not recording them, and technically be correct.

But still: I feel weird publishing the contents of these recaps, because they do contain things that people noted to me in what they assumed was a private setting. I had the feature on when I attended a choir practice, and Siri recapped the brief chats I had with other choir members before and after practice. (Interestingly, it did not recap any of the quiet conversations I had with fellow sopranos while the tenors were rehearsing their part. I’m not sure if the watch was unable to hear us over the music, or if Siri is programmed not to listen when music is being played.).

Because speakers aren’t identified, it seems Siri doesn’t know what to do when there is a disagreement. A human note-taker would jot down that Person A made a point in favor of something, and person B made a point against. But when my son and I disagreed about how likely space colonization might be in the future, the recap didn’t reflect the separate positions that were put forth. It summarized the conversation as including “debating the feasibility and timeline of human space colonization and asteroid mining,” which isn’t exactly accurate, but close enough.

When it comes to the content of the discussion, the recap notes a bullet point of “skepticism regarding permanent space colonies within the next 100 years.” It didn’t include my reasons for being skeptical, and didn’t mention my son’s opposing viewpoint at all. If I were using this recap to jog my memory of the conversation, it wouldn’t be all that helpful.

Details are sometimes egregiously incorrect. After a discussion about a family member’s health, the recap had notes on the prognosis of “father.” The family member we discussed is not anybody’s father. Names in general seem to be a problem; I recommended a book to my son, and the recap includes notes about the content of the book, but not its title. The book’s author appears in the introduction to the recap (sort of a summary of a summary), but not in the content of the recap itself where the book is mentioned.

I should probably turn Siri recaps off. It seems wrong to let people chat with me without letting them know that their conversation is being ... well, not technically recorded, but basically recorded.

Sources indicate that but it’s so tempting to leave it on so that I can review my day. Some of the details in the recaps are useful, like the dates that were discussed as options for a holiday party. The recaps will be deleted in about a week (unless I save them to the notes app), so if I want to remind myself of a conversation a few days ago, I should be able to scroll back through my recaps and find it.

I would be a fool to rely on the recaps, though. The most key points of a conversation are often left out; Siri doesn’t know what’s actually important, and there’s no way to guide it as to what to pay attention to. Specific details can be wrong, as I mentioned. There’s also no way to control when a “conversation” starts or stops, unless you are turning the recap feature on and off from the watch.

Sources indicate that and there’s more: Not only are names usually omitted (wait, who did she say I should ask about that project?), the few identifiers that make it into the recap, like names of events, are often wrong. Subjects of discussion are often conflated in really unhelpful ways: My husband mentioned paying for certain course registrations for one of our children, and later I talked to that child about an unrelated exam. The recap got all of these things mixed up with each other and was wrong about pretty much every detail. About all the recap could usefully do is to remind me that something about AP U.S. History was discussed. Reading the recaps can be like reliving your day entirely in the passive voice.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ahead of the GTA 6 release this week, publisher Take-Two Interactive and 2K Sports have announced an NBA 2K27 crossover with the game.
  • Ahead of the GTA 6 release this week, publisher Take-Two Interactive and 2K Sports have revealed an NBA 2K27 crossover with the game.
  • Industry observers note that the $80 digital-only NBA 2K27 Vice City Edition features Miami Heat player Bam Adebayo on the cover, and for that GTA 6 touch, the art also includes the signature Vice City neon glow.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ahead of the GTA 6 release this week, publisher Take-Two Interactive and 2K Sports have announced an NBA 2K27 crossover with the game. Starting November 27, Vice City will take over the digital basketball courts, and a special-edition NBA 2K27 Vice City Edition will also be released to promote GTA 6. The $80 digital-only NBA 2K27 Vice City Edition features Miami Heat player Bam Adebayo on the cover, and for that GTA 6 touch, the art also includes the signature Vice City neon glow. This is something of a first for Take-Two Interactive--and possibly, the rest of the industry--as releasing a special edition of a game that promotes another game isn't something that we've seen before. This version also includes bonus Vice City-themed content and several benefits for GTA+ subscribers. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=93W0zh7ThBo For Season 3 of NBA 2K27's live-service league, Vice City-themed content and rewards across The City social hub and MyTeam mode will be available to unlock. This three-week promotion will include bonuses and access for GTA+ Members, and Take-Two says players can expect themed apparel, including Vice City and Los Santos jerseys, Burger Shot and Cluckin' Bell Employee Outfits, and more. Vice City-themed limited-time events will run throughout the season, with players competing in Conquer Leonida and Vice Run. Wednesdays will offer a chance to earn extra reputation by wearing Rockstar Games collaboration gear in Wear & Earn events, and one of the fresh modes is Neon vs. Noir, a 5v5 full-court clash pitting a Vice City team against a Los Santos lineup. MyTeam will also feature Vice City-themed cards, a powerful new Premier Exchange card, and limited-time modes. The new gear will cost you some bucks, as the Season 3 Pro Pass--which offers access to the premium track with Vice City rewards like the Burger Shot gear, Cluckin' Bell outfit, Cactus Jack jersey, and Macca the Gator--will cost $10. The Hall of Fame Pass, which includes everything from the Pro Pass, 10 instant Level Skips, an extra 15% XP booster, and 15,000 VC, is priced at $20, and to get all the GTA-themed cosmetics, you have to grind through the 40-level season track. If you purchase the Vice City edition, the Season 3 Pro Pass is bundled with your copy. GTA+ members on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S can also play the standard edition of NBA 2K27 for free from November 27 to January 15, 2027. If they like what they see, they'll get 20% off the game if they choose to purchase. GTA 6 preorders also include a one-month trial of GTA+. Finally, GTA+ members can also download a Vice City bonus content pack featuring a Vice City-styled blue boat hat and oversized T-shirt, 30 skill boosts for five games, and 15 Gatorade boosts for five games. GTA 6 marketing has been heating up as the game gets closer to launch, and this isn't the only basketball promotion on the table. For one night only, the NBA's Miami Heat will wear GTA 6-inspired jerseys when they host the Milwaukee Bucks on November 18, and the match will take place on a court inspired by Vice City.

Robert Pattinson Is the Fresh James Bond

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It looks like Robert Pattinson is trading in his Batmobile for an Aston Martin.
  • Industry observers note that “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” stated Pattinson in a statement.
  • Industry observers note that created by Ian Fleming for his 1953 novel Casino Royale, James Bond, the British intelligence officer who lends his immense talents to MI6, is one of the most recognizable characters in the modern world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It looks like Robert Pattinson is trading in his Batmobile for an Aston Martin. After a highly scrutinized and lengthy audition process involving some of Hollywood’s most sought-after leading men, it was the Batman star who emerged at the eleventh hour to nab the highly sought after role of MI6 agent James Bond.

Industry observers note that “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” stated Pattinson in a statement. “I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”.

Industry observers note that created by Ian Fleming for his 1953 novel Casino Royale, James Bond, the British intelligence officer who lends his immense talents to MI6, is one of the most recognizable characters in the modern world. Figuring prominently in 12 of Fleming’s novels and two collections of short stories, Bond is both tall, dark, and handsome and calm, cool, and collected—the platonic ideal of a world-class spy. Bond leapt from page to screen in 1962 with the Eon-produced Dr. No, spawning one of the biggest media franchises in history. Since its inception, the 27 Bond films have grossed more than $7 billion dollars worldwide.

Pattinson follows in the suave footsteps of Daniel Craig, who played James Bond for five films, from 2006’s Casino Royale until 2021’s No Time to Die where (spoiler alert) Craig’s 007 dies while protecting the world from a global terrorist organization. Around No Time to Die, there was another shake up in Bond ownership when Amazon acquired Bond’s parent studio, MGM, in an $8.5 billion deal. Barbara Broccoli—whose father, Eon founder Albert R. “Cubby” Broccoli, produced the first Bond film—and her half brother, Michael G. Wilson, held the rights to the franchise for almost 30 years, and pledged to work with Amazon after founder Jeff Bezos. However, in February 2025, the Broccolis confirmed that they’d be stepping back from the franchise and ceding complete creative control to Amazon MGM. At the Oscars a month later, the Broccoli family was honored with a bizarre musical tribute to James Bond, starring Margaret Qualley, Doja Cat, and Lisa, unofficially ushering in a upcoming era in the Bond Cinematic Universe.

Industry observers note that although a latest era of Bond loomed, Amazon MGM had one major problem: they needed a new Bond. Ahead of No Time to Die, Craig had confirmed that he was stepping away from the franchise, leaving the producers with a 007 sized hole to fill. Before she stepped away, Broccoli insinuated that this new era of Bond was looking for a younger actor, in their 30s, to take over the reins from Craig, who was 51 when he retired from MI6.

It has been revealed that technically, they landed on someone slightly outside their preferred age range; Pattinson is 40 years old. Just don't tell him that. During Vanity Fair's lie detector test with Jennifer Lawrence while promoting their film Die My Love, Pattinson insisted he was from a different generation. I am Gen Z," he said to Lawrence. "I am." Hey, you're only as old as you feel. In the same video, Pattinson said he “loves taking jobs of younger actors," which he managed to do with his Bond casting. Good for Pattinson.

According to recent reports, almost every leading man in Hollywood's name came up as a potential predecessor to Craig—except for Pattinson, who the masses assumed was out of contention due to the fact that he locked into playing another beloved fictional character with massive IP: Batman. Pattinson's take on the caped crusader in Matt Reeve's The Batman (2022) was a major success, but several production delays on The Batman Part II, and a shakeup at Batman's studio DC—last week, it was declared that co-CEO's of DC James Gunn and Peter Safran were ousted from the studio—meant that there might be time in Pattinson's schedule for some sexy espionage.

Still, it was far from a done deal that Pattinson would land 007. In recent years, some fans have advocated for a twist on the classic Bond formula. Lashawna Lynch made history as Nomi, the first Black person or woman to ever to hold the 007 moniker in No Time to Die. But Nomi is not James Bond. There was a seemingly endless period when the world was convinced that Idris Elba—arguably the most tall, dark, and handsome man to ever exist—would take on the mantle at some point, but while Elba auditioned, it wasn’t meant to be. Now, at 53, Elba has seemingly aged out of the role. (For the record, Elba thought the next Bond should be a woman.) Elba wasn’t the only name bandied about in recent years. It was reported that Aaron Taylor Johnson was close to signing a contract to take over the role in 2023, but those reports turned out to be false.

Recent findings suggest that although a favorite at the beginning, Jacob Elordi reportedly didn't screen test for the role. Riz Ahmed made an Emmy-nominated television show, Bait, inspired by the idea of a British Pakastani actor getting cast as Bond. Other actors rumored to be in the mix over the course of the process include, but are not limited to Tom Francis, Harris Dickinson and apparently Harry Styles. At the end of the day five actors screen tested for the role: Slow Horse's Jack Lowden, One Night Only's Callum Turner, Disclosure Day's Josh O'Connor, Superman's Nicholas Hoult, and Pattison. Hoult and Pattinson were the last two to screen test for the role, implying that the powers that be at Amazon MGM may not have been happy with the three options presented and sent a hail mary. When Puck reported that Pattinson was able to negotiate a 3 picture deal rather than a 4 picture deal despite the fact that he commanded a much higher salary then the other options, it looked like the writing was on the wall that Pattinson would be the next Bond.

In a recent development, it also helps that Pattinson is having a career high at the moment, having starred in a handful of the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful films of 2026. He began the year by turning his controversial A24 comedy The Drama with Zendaya into a box office success, generating $134 million worldwide on a budget of $28 million. He then followed that up with a deliciously sniveling turn in Christopher Nolan's epic The Odyssey, an Oscar front-runner which earned $1.8 billion at the box office. Then there's Primetime, Lance Oppenheim's To Catch A Predator drama which stars Pattinson as host Chris Hansen. (Yes, in a way Chris Hansen is now one degree from being James Bond. Let that sink in). Primetime hit significant with $61 million globally on an $18 million budget, and is earning Pattinson leading actor buzz. On top of it all, he's still got Dune: Part 3 with Villeneuve coming down the pipeline in December.

It has been revealed that ultimately, the Twilight star was handpicked by the powers that be at Amazon MGM, producers Amy Pascal, David Heyman, executive producer Tanya Lapointe, and director Denis Villeneuve, who is helming the next iteration of the series based on a script from screenwriter Steven Knight. Given the fact that Pattinson is starring in Villeneuve's highly-anticipated Dune: Part 3 it might not be that much of a surprise that the director chose Pattinson as his next Bond. “Before anything else, I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey," said Villeneuve in a statement. "We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007. I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our upcoming James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin.”.

According to recent reports, pattinson enters a long lineage of spectacularly suave spies—some who lasted longer than others in Bond’s impeccably tailored suits. The first ever James Bond was, of course, Sean Connery, who went on to star in seven Bond films, including From Russia with Love (1963), Goldfinger (1964), and Diamonds Are Forever (1971). Connery was followed by George Lazenby, who starred in a single Bond film, On Her Majesty’s Secret Service (1969), before passing the reins back to Connery. The third Bond was Roger Moore, who took over for 1973’s Live and Let Die, and appeared in a total of seven Bond films, most notably The Spy Who Loved Me (1977) and Octopussy (1983).

After Moore came Timothy Dalton, who became 007 with 1987’s The Living Daylights, then threw in the towel after 1989’s License to Kill. Millennials will fondly remember the next Bond: Pierce Brosnan, who starred as the sexy spy in four films from 1995’s Golden Eye to 2002’s Die Another Day, until Craig took over in 2006.

Sources indicate that will Pattison's Bond be more debonair like Brosnan, who told VF he was “eagerly” awaiting the Bond casting news, or brooding like Craig? Will he be remembered as a rightful heir to Connery's throne, or will his Bond feel closer to Austin Powers in The Spy who Shagged Me? In any case, lets hope Pattinson prefers his martinis shaken not stirred. He's going to be drinking a lot of them for the foreseeable future.

10 Hacks Every Reddit User Should Know

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (841 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that if you're looking for discussions, recommendations, or advice online, it's hard to avoid Reddit.
  • Reddit used to let everyone view your post and comment history, but in recent years, you can make your profile private.
  • Old Reddit lets you use the site's classic design, and I prefer it to the more modern UI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that if you're looking for discussions, recommendations, or advice online, it's hard to avoid Reddit. From mainstream sports to niche crafts, it does seem that there's some kind of Reddit community for everyone. (And if there's not one, you can make one yourself.) If you're using Reddit, here are 10 hacks you should know about to improve your experience on the site.

Reddit used to let everyone view your post and comment history, but in recent years, you can make your profile private. You can hide your posts, comments, and the subreddits you're a part of. If you want to do this, click your profile icon once you've logged in to Reddit, and go to Settings > Profile. Alternatively, you can follow the direct link to Reddit's profile settings page. Click the drop-down menu next to Content & Activity, and select Hide all. You should also turn off Online Status on the same page to stop people from seeing when you're using Reddit.

Old Reddit lets you use the site's classic design, and I prefer it to the more modern UI. Old Reddit looks dated, but it doesn't have infinite scrolling, distracting animations, and a bunch of features designed to increase the time you spend on the platform. It's no wonder that Reddit is making it harder to access this version of the site. As long as it's around, you should switch to Old Reddit for a cleaner reading experience. You can do that by going to Reddit Settings > Preferences and enabling Default to Old Reddit. You can also visit old.reddit.com, though you'll need to sign in for access.

Many subreddits use custom themes that range from beautiful to borderline unusable. If you want a more consistent UI across the site, you should disable these custom subreddit styles. Go to Reddit Settings > Preferences and turn off Use community themes. If you're using Old Reddit, click the preferences button in the top-right corner, and under "display options," disable allow subreddits to show me custom themes.

Sources indicate that reddit's social features are useful if you have friends on the site, but in most cases, those features are annoying at best. If your post or comment goes viral, be prepared to deal with waves of weirdos who find it entertaining to send unsolicited advice or opinions. To keep all of this at bay, you should disable the site's social features. Go to Reddit Settings > Privacy, and turn off Allow people to follow you. On the same page, click Who can send you chat requests, and pick Nobody. You can also turn off Show up in search results to remove your profile from Google searches.

A multireddit is a feed that shows posts from a customized group of subreddits. You can think of it as a way to break out of Reddit's algorithms, and create your own Reddit feed. I use multireddits to follow all sports-related subs I'm interested in. I even have one for gaming, and one for fountain pens. It's a great way to create interest-specific feeds, and if you make them private, no one else can see them. To create one, click the Create custom feed button in the left pane in new Reddit. In the Old Reddit design, click the Create button in the left pane. Be sure to select the Private button to keep it from showing up for others. You can add as many subreddits as you like to the list, and bookmark the feed to access it whenever you wish to.

If you want to reduce Reddit's tracking, you should turn off ad personalization. Go to Reddit Settings > Privacy, and turn off Personalize ads. To block Reddit's ads altogether, you can use any ad blocker you like. I recommend uBlock Origin, which is one of the best ad blockers you can install, though most can hide Reddit's ads on desktop. On mobile, you can try using AdGuard or Wipr to hide in-app ads in Reddit.

Reddit has recently adopted an Instagram-like experience for its feeds. It removed the ability to sort posts by latest, controversial, best, etc., and instead offers "For You" and "Following." If you dislike this change, you can bypass it. I use Reddit on mobile Safari, and I recommend an extension called Sink It for Reddit. It can automatically redirect you to Old Reddit, and there's a feature that optimizes it for mobile, which brings back the old sorting options. You can also use third-party apps such as RedReader for Android, or RDX for Reddit on an iPhone or iPad to restore the old sorting options for Reddit posts.

In a recent development, after all these years, Reddit's built-in search still leaves something to be desired—at least, on the surface. To find posts on Reddit faster, use search filters on the site. For instance, adding "title:" to your search will limit the results to post titles, and boolean operators such as AND, OR, and NOT also work for advanced searches on the site.

At the same time, Zelnick isn't worried about the impact on GTA 6, in part because he believes the game is so good that people will find a way to pay for a fresh console.

Matt Damon’s Odysseus consults with Zendaya’s Athena in The Odyssey.

I’m in front of these people who I’ve admired, but I’m just like, I don’t want to mess this up.”.

While she admitted that these emotions might have worked for her character, they were not so good for her state of mind: “I was incredibly nervous, which I guess is helpful for the scene, but there’s so many other background actors as well who are performing their hearts out—so many—stunt performers who are performing and giving the most beautiful performances.”.

Tom Holland in a scene from The Odyssey.

#4241. WoW: Forever’s Dungeons Have Gotten Yet Another Big Change

WoW: Forever’s Dungeons Have Gotten Yet Another Big Change

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1036 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • World of Warcraft: Forever's dungeons have changed once again, with developer Blizzard's most recent adjustment requiring an emergency hotfix to address players' outcry.
  • World of Warcraft: Forever's dungeons have changed once again, with developer Blizzard's most recent adjustment requiring an emergency hotfix to address players' outcry.
  • Dungeons, specifically how much experience points players earn from them, have been one of Forever's most debated topics going back to the game's beta.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever's dungeons have changed once again, with developer Blizzard's most recent adjustment requiring an emergency hotfix to address players' outcry. Dungeons, specifically how much experience points players earn from them, have been one of Forever's most debated topics going back to the game's beta. Make them too lucrative, and players will just stay inside dungeons instead of questing out in the world. At the same time, Blizzard doesn't want dungeons to be one-time affairs, with players completing all their quests in a single run and never going back. Blizzard opened a new front in the dungeon wars on November 13, making a change so that nobody in a dungeon group would receive any experience if enemies were considered "trivial" to to any player in the group. The idea behind this appeared to be an effort to prevent high-level players from running low-level ones through dungeons, in the process curtailing players from selling character "boosting" services to lowbies. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9AlEQvn4dlc Unfortunately, far too many players playing the game normally were caught in the crossfire. Many of Forever's dungeons have double-digit level ranges, meaning even if a player might find enemies early on in the dungeon trivial, enemies and bosses later on won't be. It also created a scenario where players were leveling up mid-dungeon, only to suddenly find themselves fighting trivial enemies and bricking the experience gains for everyone in the group. As it turns out, committing to a multi-hour adventure, only to suddenly find nobody is earning experience points and everyone is mad at you because you happened to level up, is not a great social experience. Blizzard was at least quick to admit the change "missed the mark" and made adjustments a day later on November 14. "With hotfixes that are now live, we've just deployed a further change to this restriction, making it so the XP nullification only kicks in when the high-level player is more than 12 levels above the level of the enemies," Blizzard said in a forum post. At least judging from forum comments, that seems to be a more reasonable compromise, even if it still does prevent higher-level players from coming to help their lower-level friends. It's just the latest chapter in what has become one of the biggest ongoing discussions in the Forever community. During the Forever beta, Blizzard made changes to experience earned from dungeon quests, nerfing them significantly. Come launch day, it became apparent Forever's dungeons weren't worth running more than once, as after completing quests, experience earned from kills was extremely low. Blizzard agreed, and issued a change on November 8 to increase the amount of kill experience earned in dungeons by 50%. It was a sizable increase, but is still lower than the experience amount players earned from doing dungeons in WoW Classic. Forever's launch broke WoW concurrent-player records, and after one week of adventuring through Azeroth once more, classic WoW feels fresh again. Despite the record-breaking launch, Blizzard hasn't released official stats, but fansites have already pieced together the game's most popular class, race, and faction.
