  • The Criterion release of Guillermo del Toro's "Frankenstein" includes a newly introduced "Reborn Cut" that reinserts eight minutes of footage.
  • In a recent development, now, how much can eight minutes really change a movie, especially one that's already 150 minutes long?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

The Criterion release of Guillermo del Toro's "Frankenstein" includes a newly introduced "Reborn Cut" that reinserts eight minutes of footage.

In a recent development, now, how much can eight minutes really change a movie, especially one that's already 150 minutes long? Quite a lot, it turns out. "Frankenstein: The Reborn Cut" completely recontextualizes Victor Frankenstein (Oscar Isaac) by featuring a young Victor (Christian Convery) secretly murdering his abusive father, Baron Leopold Frankenstein (Charles Dance).

According to recent reports, in both versions, Victor comes to suspect Leopold let his mother Claire (Mia Goth) die in childbirth. This suspicion doesn't come to much in the theatrical cut; Victor confronts his father about it, who answers no one can conquer death, and Victor counters that he will. That night, Victor dreams of a "Dark Angel" promising him that craved knowledge. Victor's story of his childhood still ends with his father's death, but by seemingly natural causes.

Recent findings suggest that the "Reborn Cut" includes additional dialogue; Victor says, to secure the Dark Angel's deal and protect his little brother William from "the Beast," he decided to kill his father. Victor mixes a poison recipe from Leopold's own medical library and drops it in his father's ear as he sleeps, like Claudius killing Hamlet's father.

Recent findings suggest that victor Frankenstein of the theatrical cut already demonstrated an Oedipus complex, or a boy who sexually desires his mother and wants to kill his father. Goth plays Victor's mother and his coveted Elizabeth Harlander, and Victor's drink of choice is milk. Victor literally killing his father in the "Reborn Cut" completes the character's psychology. It also deepens his character in the rest of the movie as he becomes a father himself to the Creature (Jacob Elordi), whose violent revenge against Victor for abusing him now even more closely mirrors Victor and Leopold.

Nothing of this sort happens in Mary Shelley's "Frankenstein" book. Victor's childhood was already one of the biggest changes from the "Frankenstein" novel, where he indicates that "no youth could have passed more happily than mine." Victor's father dies at the end of the novel in grief from the Creature killing all of his and Victor's loved ones.

In a recent development, in del Toro's movie, Victor adores his mother, but his father is cold, concerned only that Victor carries on his legacy as a master surgeon — he strikes Victor with a cane when he fails in his studies. Del Toro refashions Frankenstein Sr. like his villain Captain Vidal (Sergi López) in "Pan's Labyrinth." Both men only see their wives as brood mares and dislike the child she already has. Both men's wives die in childbirth, and with the suggestion Vidal/Leopold allowed that because he only cared about the child's life.

In a recent development, leopold's abuse infects how Victor treats his creation. Victor tries to rear the Creature, but it goes horribly wrong because he's echoing his father's parenting. In his arrogance, Victor also doesn't conceive of his creation as a child. Take his anger when the Creature cuts his hand grabbing a razor blade — is that parental concern or anger that the monster damaged his [Victor's] artistic work of surgically sculpting the Creature's body?

Industry observers note that in another scene, the Creature recoils when Victor gets angry at him for not speaking, and Victor reacts in exasperated disbelief: "I'm not going to hurt you. I made you." It seems like he genuinely wants to be different from his father but doesn't know how to be, which is even more gutting in the "Reborn Cut" since we know that Victor hated his father enough to kill him.

Sources indicate that if Leopold's death felt abrupt in the "Frankenstein" theatrical cut, now we know why. Victor making an explicit Faustian deal with the "Dark Angel" also makes Victor's later rage against it for supposedly betraying him more coherent, and that deal essentially extracting Victor's soul fits the Angel's Satanic visage.

According to recent reports, the theatrical cut, though, reveals Victor as the villain more gradually. The Creature initially attacks like a "monster" but then the movie tells his side. Victor being a murderer undercuts the bait and switch; poisoning your own father, even an abusive one, as a child is an undeniable sign of a bad seed.

According to recent reports, the sequence of events still flows either way. In both versions, Victor recounting his deal with the Dark Angel cuts to the Creature breaking free from the ice. In the theatrical cut, Victor asks "but how [will I conquer death]?" The Creature demonstrates he found the answer. In the "Reborn Cut," Victor claims he realized he had to kill his father as the Creature is coming to kill Victor, his father.

In a "Frankenstein" audio commentary, del Toro reveals he cut the sequence on the advice of his longtime pal, James Cameron. Victor killing his father doesn't just make him less sympathetic, Cameron argued, it weakens his character: "If Victor kills his father [...] he has completed his task. He avenged his mother. Why would he then embark on the quest for immortality?".

Leopold's last scene in the theatrical cut, Victor grabbing his father's cane and boasting he'll surpass him, emphasizes that quest will be Victor's revenge. I'm split on if the "Reborn Cut" is superior, but Victor killing his father is a clarifying change which makes the story and themes of "Frankenstein" hang together a little better.

As his eyesight fades, Hesse races against time to rescue more than 1,000 films capturing the continent’s struggle for independence in the 1950s and 60s. Hidden for decades after Nkrumah’s overthrow in a 1966 coup, the archive becomes a bridge between generations to fill in their lost history. Five years ago, after a chance encounter, Hesse asked fellow documentarian Proudfoot to tell his story.

According to recent reports, “Over six decades ago Chris Hesse picked up a camera and documented one of the most pivotal moments in world history,” notes Ethan Lewis, Head of Non-Fiction at Higher Ground. “Now, thanks to iShowSpeed and this historic, precedent setting partnership, this history will be shared for all to see for free.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that every James Bond casting announcement marks the start of a fresh era.
  • The first Bond of the Amazon MGM era was destined to be even more of a turning point than usual, no matter who landed the role.
  • According to recent reports, when Robert Pattinson was officially declared as the seventh actor to play 007 on Monday morning, the latest era of the Bond franchise officially took shape.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that every James Bond casting announcement marks the start of a fresh era. The fictional MI6 agent has been one of pop culture’s few constants over the past seven decades; and each time a new actor steps into the role, it tells us something about the entertainment landscape we at the moment inhabit. Bonds can be intensely serious or silly and self-deprecating, and actors have entered the franchise at ages ranging from their late 20s to mid 40s. The role always goes to a member of the Commonwealth, but the variation that’s possible within those parameters has turned the franchise into a vertical wine tasting that illustrates what male movie stardom looks like in each decade. Related Stories Fall Festival Movies Sold: ‘Edward Said: Between Worlds’ About Palestinian-American Author Lands at Kino Lorber The Stop-Motion Tool That’s a Constant in This Crazy, AI-Mixed-Up World.

The first Bond of the Amazon MGM era was destined to be even more of a turning point than usual, no matter who landed the role. The next film in the franchise will be the first one ever produced without the involvement of the Broccoli family, who have carefully guarded each iteration of the character since “Dr. No” came out in 1962. It marks the biggest movie investment that Amazon has ever made, as the tech giant spent nearly $10 billion to acquire MGM (of which Bond was the clear crown jewel) and then wrestle full control away from the Broccolis. With Denis Villeneuve at the helm, it arguably marks the first time that Bond has been rebooted by a true auteur director with a distinct preexisting style and fan base. And it follows a Daniel Craig era that many feel took the idea of a dark, realistic James Bond to its logical endpoint with no obvious direction to go next.

According to recent reports, when Robert Pattinson was officially declared as the seventh actor to play 007 on Monday morning, the latest era of the Bond franchise officially took shape. But it also marked the end of a larger Hollywood era in which blue chip legacy characters were seen as infinitely more crucial than the people playing them. We spent much of the past decade declaring that IP are the upcoming movie stars. But casting the current Batman actor as James Bond proves that is no longer the case.

According to recent reports, that line of thinking began to take shape in the 2010s, an era of Hollywood that will forever be defined by the phrase “cinematic universe.” As moviegoing became less of a consistent consumer habit and more of an event-driven hobby, the industry found that putting an A-list movie star or two in a fresh film was no longer enough to guarantee a massive opening weekend. What did work, though, was slapping a Marvel logo in front of something and watching the box office dollars flow in.

Sources indicate that top-tier franchises were places where you went to build your star power, not cash it in. A latest Bond or Spider-Man announcement was often the mainstream world’s introduction to a rising star that would be a household name within a few years. The approach was certainly better for the producers who steward these franchises: it ensured that the real value was contained in the stories and iconography that they controlled, making it relatively easy to bring in massive box office hauls with interchangeable actors who often moved onto bigger things before they became too expensive or demanding.

As that formula becomes less workable, it’s fair to wonder where we’ll start going to find our new stars. If you were casting a new Spider-Man in this environment, you probably wouldn’t pick an obscure theater actor like Tom Holland. We’re already seeing more stars come out of independent genre films, one of the few niches that can still be profitable without star power. “Obsession” gave the world its biggest breakout star of 2026 in Inde Navarette, and now she’s heading to the Marvel Cinematic Universe to help lead the “X-Men” franchise. But legacy franchises were once Hollywood’s most reliable path to minting new stars, and the industry will have to get creative if it doesn’t want the pipeline of bankable stars to fizzle out.

According to recent reports, from an artistic standpoint, there’s every reason to believe Pattinson will make an excellent Bond. He has already worked with Villeneuve on the upcoming “Dune: Part Three” and has proven himself to be one of his generation’s most versatile leading men. He’s equally capable of playing brooding heroes and sniveling villains; a 2026 slate that includes “The Drama,” “The Odyssey,” and “Primetime” is evidence of both his range and consistent box office appeal. But from a business standpoint, it’s a decision that you wouldn’t make if you didn’t have to.

It has been revealed that his deal reportedly costs more money for less commitment than any of the other finalists who screen tested. You’ll be juggling a production and promotion schedule that also includes “The Batman” franchise and other major films. In the run-up to the movie, more eyes will be on the man himself than the timelessness of the brand. And when the time eventually comes to replace him, expectations for the level of actor you need to land will be higher than ever before. It’s the kind of move you make when you simply cannot afford to fail. Nobody would deny that that’s the exact situation Amazon MGM finds itself in, but the mere fact that something as reliable as a newly introduced James Bond movie could place a studio in such a position is notable in and of itself.

In a recent development, it would be reductive to say that the pendulum has entirely swung back towards favoring movie stars. The old model where you could regularly deliver hits by putting George Clooney and Julia Roberts on a poster is certainly nowhere to be found. It might be more accurate to say that we’re in a “more is more” era of Hollywood, where no film is ever guaranteed to become the kind of cultural event that’s required to turn a profit on these massive tentpole budgets. With more competition for audience attention spans than ever before, you need to pair the power of Bond and the power of Pattinson and Villeneuve to feel truly comfortable with your investment.

#4140. These Are the Best Ways to Encrypt Your Email

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (702 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

These Are the Best Ways to Encrypt Your Email

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (702 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You probably already know that your email isn't actually all that private, especially if you have a free account with a major service provider like Gmail (Google) or Outlook (Microsoft).
  • Industry observers note that as this in-depth explainer from Adaptive Security describes, most emails are encrypted in transit via Transport Layer Security (TLS), which prevents anyone from reading your message as it travels from server to server.
  • According to recent reports, emails are also typically encrypted at rest—for example, while sitting on Google's servers and in a Gmail recipient's inbox.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You probably already know that your email isn't actually all that private, especially if you have a free account with a major service provider like Gmail (Google) or Outlook (Microsoft). But if you are sending sensitive information via email, you can minimize what can be snooped on and by whom using end-to-end encryption, which generally ensures that only the recipient can read your message. Here's what you need to know about email encryption and how to set up an extra layer of privacy.

Industry observers note that as this in-depth explainer from Adaptive Security describes, most emails are encrypted in transit via Transport Layer Security (TLS), which prevents anyone from reading your message as it travels from server to server. However, encryption is temporarily stripped at each server: content is received and processed in plaintext and then re-encrypted when it leaves, meaning it could be read, logged, and distributed by the server provider.

According to recent reports, emails are also typically encrypted at rest—for example, while sitting on Google's servers and in a Gmail recipient's inbox. But this only prevents someone with physical access to the server hardware from reading messages, as Google still holds the encryption key and can access stored data. And, as PCMag points out, Google is scanning your messages to a degree, and it (along with other email providers) can and will hand emails over to law enforcement and government agencies in some cases.

By contrast, with end-to-end encryption (E2EE), emails are readable only on the sender's and recipient's devices, and can be decrypted only with the recipient's private key. They're never translated into plaintext as they pass between and through servers to their destination, meaning that no one—including server providers, hackers, or law enforcement—can view the content. It's worth noting, though, that E2EE is not impenetrable nor a total guarantee of privacy. For example, metadata like subject lines and email addresses may remain in plaintext, and encrypted messages are still susceptible to phishing. Plus, forwarding an encrypted message breaks the encryption.

Still, end-to-end encryption is especially useful when sending sensitive information that may be valuable to bad actors, though if security and privacy are a high priority, you may want to consider it for all of your emails. How you deploy encryption depends on whether you are adding it to your current email or switching to a dedicated provider.

If you have an account with a major email provider like Gmail, Outlook, or Apple Mail, you can add a third-party tool that layers an encryption protocol like OpenPGP on top of your existing account. PCMag recommends PreVeil, SecureMyEmail, and Virtru (which is limited to Gmail owners in Chrome) for those who want to keep their current emails. Mailvelope is a browser add-on (and therefore a desktop-only tool) available in Chrome, Firefox, and Edge, though it can also be installed on other browsers, like Brave, that are built on the same architecture. FlowCrypt integrates with Gmail and Google Workspace on desktop and mobile.

Note that enterprise users of Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 have access to true end-to-end encryption without third-party add-ons. Gmail's Confidential mode and Outlook's Encrypt feature, available to all users, are not E2EE equivalents, as Google and Microsoft, respectively, still manage the keys.

For those who are willing to start fresh with a latest email address (or who have a custom domain), providers like Proton Mail or Tuta offer native end-to-end encryption. The caveat: by default, this is only between consumers on the same service, so from one Proton user to another. If you want to send an end-to-end encrypted email from Proton to a Gmail user, for example, you have to set up password protection (and share the password via another secure channel) or use a PGP-compatible tool like those listed above. You can also Proton's Gmail integration does allow for end-to-end encryption, but only if both Gmail parties are using the Proton integration.

The bottom line here is that email wasn't designed to be a highly secure form of communication. End-to-end encryption does add a layer of privacy and security if you jump through hoops to set it up, but it's still susceptible to human error and social engineering.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that dragons are the most iconic fantasy creatures, and for a good reason. These mighty serpents appear in some form across all cultures, ranging from vicious weapons of death and destruction to powerful beings of wisdom and grace. This unique duality allows storytellers to go wild with their depictions of dragons, and, theoretically, no two are the same.

According to recent reports, it's no surprise that there are plenty of great dragon books out there that feature these mighty beasts. However, some of them stand out a bit better than others thanks to how they present the dragons and their use in the narrative. Note that there are tens of thousands of fictional dragons, so this list can be viewed as a snapshot of some of the greatest.

Michael Ende's The NeverEnding Story is best known for its 1982 film adaptation, widely regarded as one of the darkest fantasy movies for families. However, the movie only covered the first half of the book, which wouldn't be adapted until 1990 in The NeverEnding Story 2. Dragons have a few small but very important roles in the narrative, and come with lots of thematic significance.

Industry observers note that the most obvious one is Falcor the Luck Dragon, who resembles a lion-headed beast with pinkish skin and the ability to fly without wings. He represents wisdom and optimism, encouraging the heroes to keep faith in their quests, and that good luck always comes to those most deserving of it. Later, the protagonist, Bastian, impulsively wishes the dragon Smerg into existence—a grotesque, chimeric abomination that represents how reckless abuse of power can have disastrous consequences on the world at large.

C. S. Lewis' The Chronicles of Narnia is among the first fantasy series people get into, and remains very popular and beloved to this day. For the third book, The Voyage of the Dawn Treader, Lewis created his own odyssey as the characters go looking for seven missing lords and then try to find the end of the world and the country of Aslan, the great lion and creator of Narnia. During their stop on one isle, Eustace Scrubb discovers an elderly dragon as it dies among its hoarded treasure, and, when he sleeps among it, transforms into a dragon himself.

Lewis uses Eustace's transformation to explore themes of human greed and how selfish desires can turn us into something monstrous. It also has ties to Norse mythology through Fafnir, who was originally a dwarf but transformed into a dragon after killing his father and stealing his treasures. Of course, since Lewis was a staunch Christian, he has Eustace change back after he uses his draconic abilities to help the crew of the Dawn Treader, before allowing Aslan to tear away his dragon skin as a symbolic representation of divine redemption.

In a recent development, few series have had the level of effect on modern fantasy as George R. R. Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire. Thanks to the success of the HBO adaptation, Game of Thrones, it spawned a latest wave of fantasy media based on political intrigue with reserved levels of magic, for better or for worse. Martin himself also produced a number of spin-off works, such as The World of Ice and Fire, which gives greater details about Westeros, Essos, and continents never visited in the main series.

In a recent development, the book also gives a wider impression of the dragons tamed by House Targaryen, who are all but extinct in the main series. Beautiful artwork depicts Targaryen dragons in all their glory, and detail is also given of the Valyrian Empire that the Targaryens originated from, which could field thousands of dragons in their wars of conquest. And once you're done with the dragon history, there's plenty more lore to immerse yourself in thanks to Martin's unique skill in writing such an engaging secondary world.

While dragons appear in plenty of stories, very few are told from their perspective. Enter E. E. Knight's Age of Fire series, which follows a trio of dragon siblings right from birth as they interact with a complex world of humans, dwarves, elves, and others. The first book, Dragon Champion, is told from the perspective of the eldest dragon sibling, AuRon, who is a rare scaleless dragon, meaning he doesn't need to eat metal to keep them strong.

Knight has a lot of fun going into the biology of his dragons, from the use of a flammable fatty liquid for their fire breath to the detail that they don't grow their wings until they reach maturity. He also does a good job demonstrating how dragons view the passing of time, as AuRon meets multiple characters along his journey, only for them to age drastically between chapters while AuRon feels like only a week has passed. Later books would get caught up in geopolitics as the siblings end up shaping the fate of the world, but Dragon Champion keeps things to the life of a dragon in the wild, which makes it stand out the most.

Speculative history is a fun genre that sees writers try to imagine how the world might change if history had gone a different way or included a fantastical element. Naomi Novik asked a very interesting question: what if the Napoleonic Wars had dragons? The result is His Majesty's Dragons, the first book in her Temeraire series.

Sources indicate that the book uses dragons as an aerial equivalent to warships. They bond to a human upon hatching, and, once trained and grown, carry entire squadrons of human soldiers with them into combat. Meanwhile, the dragons are still fully sentient creatures, and there are multiple different breeds that grow to different sizes and exhibit different powers.

It has been revealed that given that every culture in the world has its own creature that fits into the broad idea of what a dragon is, it's common to wonder if they might all be related, or what their biology might be like. Dugald Steer, author of the speculative Ology series, decided to tackle it with Dragonology: The Complete Book of Dragons. Authored in text by Dr. Ernest Drake, the book goes into a deep dive regarding dragon biology and how they interact with humans.

In a recent development, the detail put into this book is fantastic, down to the book containing small letters meant to be opened and read alongside the main text, and "samples" of dragon scales and dust that readers can interact with. Dr. Drake also assigns Latin names to each dragon species featured, making the book truly feel like a scientific journal meant to be taken seriously. Combined with the gorgeous illustrations, this book is a must-have for any dragon lover, or aspiring world-builders looking to develop their own.

Industry observers note that the idea of dragon riders is one of the coolest in fiction. Who doesn't want to have a draconic companion of their own with whom they can fly through the sky or even just converse with on a deep level? Modern audiences might think of the How to Train Your Dragon movies when imagining dragon riders, but the concept arguably first exploded in pop culture thanks to Dragonflight, the first book in Anne McCaffrey's Dragonriders of Pern series.

Sources indicate that set in the far future when humans have been able to colonize other planets, the dragons of Pern are telepathic beings who imprint on their riders at birth. They're not magical creatures, but rather came to be through years of selective breeding, and have plenty of sci-fi abilities like the ability to access a form of hyperspace called "going between." By chewing on special stones, the dragons are able to breathe fire, which the people of Pern use to protect them from regular attacks by voracious organisms called Thread.

It has been revealed that ursula K. Le Guin's Earthsea books take readers to a fantastical archipelago where magic is commonplace and learning something's true name gives you power over it. The first book, A Wizard of Earthsea, follows a young man named Ged as he learns the ways of magic. So, naturally, his travels bring him into contact with dragons.

Industry observers note that the dragons of Earthsea vary in size and power, but at their apex, they are every bit the ancient and powerful creatures you would expect them to be. While most dragons are wise and deeply tied to magic, they also look down on humans and are more likely to kill them than converse. That remarked, it is possible for a human to win a dragon's respect enough to have a conversation with them, especially if they're able to decipher the dragon's true name.

While grading papers one day, Professor J. R. R. Tolkien found a blank sheet and wrote down: "In a hole in the ground, there lived a hobbit." From there, he worked backwards to figure out what a hobbit was, and before long, The Hobbit was published. Widely regarded as one of the greatest fantasy books ever made, it has never been out of print since its release, eventually leading to The Lord of the Rings.

Industry observers note that the story is a classic hero's journey centered on a quest to reclaim treasure stolen by the dragon Smaug, and draws heavily from Germanic mythology. Though Smaug himself only appears in two chapters near the end of the book, he leaves quite the impression, thanks in large part to Tolkien's decision to let him speak, something that was not common at the time. It not only made Smaug a representation of avarice and greed, but also a cunning and intelligent foe capable of manipulating anyone he talks to thanks to eloquent words and sharp questions that plant seeds of doubt in a person's mind.

The oldest surviving epic poem in the English language is Beowulf; it has long been a source of inspiration for fantasy writers, including Tolkien, who wrote an entire essay about the poem's importance. Namely, he focused on its monsters and argued that they represented man's fears and our struggles against adversity and strife. This is best represented by Beowulf's third and final opponent: a dragon who awakens in wrath when its hoard is plundered.

According to recent reports, beowulf's dragon can be interpreted in many ways, but many of them boil down to the inevitable end. There are some forces that simply cannot be fully conquered, represented by Beowulf slaying the dragon but dying in the process. The fact that it came from beneath the earth and guarded treasure from the ancient past also represents the passage of time and how all empires will inevitably come to an end.

Sony Pictures Television is bringing back game show The Joker’s Wild as a half-hour syndicated program hosted by comedian and television personality Howie Mandel.

Sources indicate that the reboot, which combines the gameplay of the original with upcoming twists and a high-stakes Jackpot bonus round, will launch in broadcast syndication in fall 2027 on the CBS Owned Stations. It is unclear yet what the stations will drop for next fall to make room for The Joker’s Wild.

Industry observers note that mandel has gameshow credentials with his long stint as the host of Deal or No Deal, for which he has Emmy nominations. He has also served as a judge on America’s Got Talent for more than 17 seasons and is the new host of The Price Is Right Tonight.

In a recent development, on The Joker’s Wild, two contestants compete by taking spins on the High Roller slot machine, using their luck and knowledge to win big. The contestants answer questions based on categories that come up in their spins, and Jokers are wild, increasing the points up for grabs. After three rounds, the contestant with the most points wins the game. That winner moves on to the latest Joker’s Jackpot bonus round where they’ll face tempting deals with the Devil as they try to take home up to $50,000.

“The Joker’s Wild is one of the most recognizable brands in game show history, with a format that combines trivia, unpredictability and significant-money stakes,” mentioned Suzanne Prete, President, Game Reveals, Sony Pictures Television. “Howie brings exactly the kind of wit, energy and spontaneity that this game demands.”.

Created and originally hosted by Jack Barry, The Joker’s Wild has gone through a number of incarnations, including syndication runs, since first launching in 1971. The most recent revival with host Snoop Dogg wan on TBS and TNT for two seasons.

The Joker’s Wild is produced by Sony Pictures Television and executive produced by showrunner Mashawn Nix, whose credits include Deal or No Deal, Match Game and Red Table Talk. Ad sales for the series will be handled by CBS Media Ventures.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Star Trek: Picard didn't give fans the same old Borg, and all three seasons featured new and distinctive spins on Star Trek's most feared cybernetic villains. Star Trek: Picard's three seasons each had different showrunners, and the presentation of the Borg reflected the sensibilities of the creative minds behind Patrick Stewart's Paramount+ series.

Introduced in Star Trek: The Next Generation season 2's "Q Who?", many fans feel the apex of the Borg was TNG's two-parter, "The Best of Both Worlds." Star Trek: First Contact brought the Borg to the significant screen in spectacular fashion, turning them into epic movie villains and introducing the Borg Queen (Alice Krige). The Borg returned multiple times afterward, most significantly in Star Trek: Voyager, which expanded the Borg's mythology in their place of origin, the Delta Quadrant.

The Borg are so inextricably linked to Admiral Jean-Luc Picard (Patrick Stewart) that it's no surprise that they factored into every season of Star Trek: Picard. Season 1's showrunner, Michael Chabon, was interested in world-building and explored the state of the Borg post-TNG. Season 2's co-showrunners Akiva Goldsman and Terry Matalas took surprising chances with the Borg from an alternate timeline. Running season 3 alone, Matalas then closed the book on the Borg from TNG by first letting them win.

In a recent development, star Trek: Picard season 1 followed up Star Trek: The Next Generation's ideas of the Borg being restored after assimilation. Picard season 1 introduced the Artifact, a Borg Cube cut off from the Collective that was salvaged by the Romulans. Working with United Federation scientists like Dr. Soji Asha (Isa Briones), the ex-Borg who were "reclaimed" are mentally and emotionally damaged, and face a challenging path back to their individuality.

Hugh (Jonathan Del Arco), the USS Enterprise-D's first successful reclamation other than Captain Picard himself, returned for a brief reunion. Tragically, the Romulan Zhat Vash expelled thousands of Borg drones into space, while Seven of Nine (Jeri Ryan) allowed herself to be briefly assimilated to take command of the Artifact. The Borg were seen as what they largely are withot the Collective: victims-turned-refugees who deserved the Federation's help.

Recent findings suggest that star Trek: Picard season 2 revealed that the Borg were completely annihilated in a dark alternate timeline ruled by the authoritarian Confederation of Earth. The Borg Queen (Annie Wersching) was her Collective's lone survivor, awaiting public execution by the evil General Picard. Yet the Borg Queen found a kindred spirit in Dr. Agnes Jurati (Allison Pill), whom she assimilated to create a newly introduced hybrid version of the Queen.

The Jurati Borg Queen led a benevolent upcoming Collective that gained provisional Federation membership.

Industry observers note that although the Borg Queen and the diabolical Dr. Adam Soong (Brent Spiner) created a 21st-century proto-Borg army, Star Trek: Picard season 2's ultimate twist was Jurati gaining controlling influence as the hybrid Borg Queen. By the end of Picard season 2, the Jurati Borg Queen led a benevolent new Collective that gained provisional Federation membership. This bizarre turn of events came with an open ending, as Jurati's Borg stood guard against a mysterious new enemy that may never be revealed.

It has been revealed that star Trek: Picard season 3 created an alliance long theorized by fans between the Dominion's Changelings and the Borg. Meanwhile, the Borg Queen implemented her revenge against Picard decades in the making: to assimilate Jean-Luc's son, Jack Crusher (Ed Speleers). As the Borg's new Vox, Jack sent the signal that gave the Queen the triumph she longed for by assimilating every Starfleet Officer under 25.

Industry observers note that the Borg Queen's victory was brief, as the crew of the USS Enterprise-D penetrated her Cube hiding in Jupiter to save Jack. In turn, Admiral Picard discovered the Borg and the Queen were shells of themselves, suffering the deteriorating effects of a virus implanted by Admiral Kathryn Janeway (Kate Mulgrew) in Star Trek: Voyager's series finale.

It has been revealed that star Trek: Picard season 3 saw the final destruction of the original Borg that menaced the Federation since Star Trek: The Next Generation. Sadly, the compelling fresh concepts of the Borg from Picard's first two seasons were left unfinished, and are likely to remain that way.

Star Trek: Picard is streaming on Paramount+.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Whether it's fantasy masterpieces like Game of Thrones, sci-fi epics like Dune: Prophecy, or even high-class dramas like Succession, HBO has already found a winning formula when it comes to TV indicates. Through its streaming service, HBO Max, the studio continues to release some of the most-watched shows on TV year after year across various genres, and the empire is only growing as time ticks by. Last year in January, HBO took one of its biggest risks in platform history with the launch of The Pitt, the medical drama starring Noah Wyle, who spent years recurring as Dr. John Carter on ER. It didn't take long for it to become clear that HBO's gamble has paid off, and with billions of minutes watched through its first two seasons, The Pitt is officially one of the most popular shows in the world.

Industry observers note that after the success of The Pitt Season 1, HBO renewed the show for Season 2, but the studio didn't wait nearly as long to double down on the future of The Pitt beyond its second season. HBO announced mere days before The Pitt Season 2 premiere that the show had already been picked up for Season 3, and cameras on the third season began rolling earlier in the year, assuring that it would once again come back on a swift timeline. Collider's Taylor Gates recently attended a FYC (For Your Consideration) event with the cast of The Pitt, and when asked how things were going in production for Season 3, Noah Wyle shared an in-depth upgrade, revealing how many episodes are fully cut and even which episode the team is filming right now:.

Industry observers note that "We're shooting Episode 12 right now. I think I'm the only one working tomorrow... It's going really, really well. We've got nine episodes cut and locked, and we're really, really proud of this season. It's not easy to come back after a first season and deliver a strong second [season]. It's especially hard in the third year because you really have picked all the low-hanging fruit, and you have to dig a little bit deeper to find who your characters are, even deeper than you've explored them before, and everyone was up for the challenge this year.".

The cast of The Pitt was also asked to give one word to describe their characters in Season 3 during the FYC event that took place. Gerran Howell, who plays Dr. Dennis Whitaker, said "faith" is the apt word to describe Whitaker's journey in Season 3, while Dr. Trinity Santos actress Isa Briones used two words, describing Santos' journey as "cracked open" in Season 3. Noah Wyle followed behind, saying that Dr. Robby is "climbing" in Season 3, while Dr. Mel King actress Taylor Dearden states that her character will be "processing.".

It has been revealed that as for Sepideh Moafi, who was a newcomer in Season 2 as Dr. Baran Al-Hashimi, she mentioned that her Season 3 journey will be "porous," and Dr. Langdon star Patrick Ball teased a "tumbling" journey for Dr. Langdon in Season 3. Katherine LaNasa, who plays the glue in the Pittsburgh Trauma ER, Dana Evans, said that she will be "teetering" in Season 3, while Fiona Dourif notes Dr. Cassie McKay will be "outraged" in the third season. Creator R. Scott Gemill jokingly teased that he's "tired" while working on Season 3.

Check out the first two seasons of The Pitt on HBO Max and stay tuned to Collider for more updates and coverage of Season 3.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Harlan Coben has been on a tear at Netflix with his most recent, I Will Find You, becoming the streamer’s fifth most popular series of all time.

Coben is back with limited series The Innocent, marking his 15th adaptation for Netflix. The streamer has greenlit the project, after Deadline revealed it was in development earlier this year.

The Innocent reunites Coben with Robert Hull, showrunner of I Will Find You, which starred Sam Worthington, and Bryan Wynbrandt and Steven Lilien, who served as writers and exec producers.

Hull launched production tech giant StoryMath earlier this year with Wynbrandt and Lilien, who created CBS’ God Friended Me, and the company has now signed a fresh overall deal with Netflix. Watch on Deadline.

Interestingly, The Innocent has already been adapted by Netflix as Spanish series El Inocente in 2021.

Recent findings suggest that the book follows Matt Hunter, who served nine years in prison after innocently trying to break up a fight-and ending up a killer. Now nine years after his release from prison, his innocence long forgotten, he’s an ex-con who takes nothing for granted. With his wife Olivia pregnant and the two of them closing on a house in his hometown, things are looking up. Until the day Matt gets a shocking, inexplicable video call from Olivia’s phone. And in an instant, the unraveling begins.

A mysterious man who begins tailing Matt turns up dead. A beloved nun is murdered. And local and federal authorities–including homicide investigator, Loren Muse, a childhood schoolmate of Matt’s with a troubled past of her own–see all signs pointing to a former criminal with one murder already under his belt… Matt Hunter. Unwilling to lose everything for a second time, Matt and Olivia are forced outside the law in a desperate attempt to save their future together.

Hull, Wynbrandt and Lilien will serve as showrunners, writers and exec producers with Coben and Ben Coben serving as exec producers through Final Twist Productions.

Elsewhere, The Whisper Man, which starred Robert DeNiro, saw a similar increase in sales, Remarkably Bright Creatures saw sales across all formats rise 560% from its first-look launch to its peak in May, East of Eden, published by Penguin Classics, hit the number one on Amazon’s best sellers list some 74 years after publication with a 200% rise in sales and Little House on the Prairie helped drive 110% more sales for the Storytide and HarperCollins-published book.

On screen, book adaptations account for nearly 20% of total view hours and over 13B global views since 2025, per the streamer.

The company was at the Texas Book Festival this weekend for the first time with a panel featuring The Hunting Wives author May Cobb and Guarding Stars author Katherine Center as well as Virgin River showrunner Patrick Sean Smith and exec Cole Galvin.

“People come to comfort and heartland stories for connection and optimism—the kind of story you put on to unwind. From Virgin River to Little House on the Prairie to Guarding Stars, our job is to give audiences more of what they love.”.

The Country Grammys’ Odd Gender Split: Women Are ‘Contemporary,’ Men Are ‘Traditional’

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (742 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollingstone

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • First, the exciting news: It’s going to be a record-setting year for female country artists at the 2027 Grammy Awards.
  • At the 69th Grammy Awards, Kelsea Ballerini’s Mount Pleasant, Carter Faith’s Cherry Valley, Megan Moroney’s Cloud 9, Kacey Musgraves’ Middle of Nowhere, and Ella Langley’s Dandelion are the contenders for Contemporary Country album, making for an incredible group of nominees where, no matter who wins, a woman will take top honors.
  • It has been revealed that country’s women have often found recognition from Grammy voters when country-radio playlists fail.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

First, the exciting news: It’s going to be a record-setting year for female country artists at the 2027 Grammy Awards. For the first time in history, the entire Best Contemporary Country Album category is dominated by solo women artists. The last run to come close was 2021’s pool, but that also included the mixed-gender band Little Major Town, when the category was known as Best Country Album.

At the 69th Grammy Awards, Kelsea Ballerini’s Mount Pleasant, Carter Faith’s Cherry Valley, Megan Moroney’s Cloud 9, Kacey Musgraves’ Middle of Nowhere, and Ella Langley’s Dandelion are the contenders for Contemporary Country album, making for an incredible group of nominees where, no matter who wins, a woman will take top honors. But there’s a clear division when the Contemporary field is compared with that of Best Traditional Country Album.

It has been revealed that country’s women have often found recognition from Grammy voters when country-radio playlists fail. Despite Langley’s success this year, women still are played on the airwaves a small proportion of the time compared with their male counterparts. From Musgraves’ 2019 win for Golden Hour to the Chicks in 2007, the awards are often a corrective for the industry’s deeply endemic gender imbalance and reluctance to embrace left-of-center artists of any gender. It’s hard to say if these nominations will ever push programmers to shift their thinking: Musgraves’ sweep wasn’t enough to put the now-classic “Rainbow” into heavy rotation. But it does provide a boost that can help level the playing field when Music Row won’t come to bat.

According to recent reports, that remarked, there’s something strange afoot among this year’s country album Grammy nominations. While the Contemporary Country Album category is entirely women, the Best Traditional Country Album category is … all men. Last year marked the first awards for the Contemporary-versus-Traditional split, and it resulted in a win for Jelly Roll in Contemporary and Zach Top in Traditional (where Margo Price was the only female nominee). Allowing for more opportunities to recognize great music is always welcome, and the albums here are excellent — we are particularly ecstatic to see Charlie Worsham’s Once Upon a Second Time Around in contention in a year where he’s also up for a CMA Award and is about to become a Grand Ole Opry member. Charley Crockett’s Clovis, Vince Gill’s 50 Years From Home: Down at the Borderline, Cody Johnson’s Banks of the Trinity, and Willie Nelson’s Workin’ Man: Willie Sings Merle round out the group. Trending Stories Raye, Rosalía, and Ella Langley Lead 2027 Grammy Nominees Jennifer Lopez Teases Upcoming Music on ‘Fallon’: ‘This Does Feel Like a Happy Era’ Robert Pattinson Is the Next James Bond Watch Buffalo Springfield Come Together for the First Time in Many Years Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

But the gender split illuminates an problem many feared would happen when the Best Traditional Country Album category was introduced — that a “traditional” label (as opposed to “alternative” or similar) would go on to reinforce the patriarchal, and white, ideal of what “real” country music sounds and looks like. Carly Pearce’s truly excellent Honest Woman, for example, was submitted in the Traditional category but didn’t make the cut. Despite the sonics of the record (a lot of classic-country and bluegrass influences), would she have had a better shot in Contemporary? It’s hard to say, but based on the past two years of nominations, women can barely get in contention for Traditional album, while Nelson and Crockett are up for the second year in a row. None of this should diminish any of the artists’ achievements, but it’s concerning to see women, who are often policed for not being “country enough,” and non-white artists of any gender not make the “Traditional” cut at all.

Make no mistake, it will be a great year for country music at this year’s Grammys: women breaking records, Langley and Lambert snagging seven nominations each and in the main categories (including a much-deserved Producer nod for Lambert), and artists like Worsham and Faith getting recognized for truly superb albums. We just hope that siloing by gender isn’t a trend that continues in years to come, because the last thing the genre needs is an award that reinforces that division even further.

#4128. 10 Privacy Hacks Every Mac User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1060 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

10 Privacy Hacks Every Mac User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1060 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple has a pretty good track record on privacy.
  • It has been revealed that enabling the macOS Firewall (which is off by default) adds a layer of protection against external devices on your wifi network, as well as unauthorized apps from initiating a connection to your device.
  • In a recent development, another hack for maintaining privacy on public networks is to enable rotating MAC addresses, which randomizes the identifier your device broadcasts when scanning for and connecting to wifi.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple has a pretty good track record on privacy. The company bakes a number of protections into its OSes to keep your data from being shared or stolen. That said, you can make your Apple devices even more secure. There are plenty of opt-in settings that make it even harder for anyone to snoop on your device and activity. These are the best privacy hacks for your Mac.

It has been revealed that enabling the macOS Firewall (which is off by default) adds a layer of protection against external devices on your wifi network, as well as unauthorized apps from initiating a connection to your device. Turning on Stealth Mode prevents your Mac from even responding to these requests, essentially making it invisible to anything that's scanning a network you're connected to. This makes it more difficult for hackers and malware to know your device exists, much less attack it. This can interfere with certain essential activity when you're on your home network, but it's a valuable security setting when on public wifi. You can leave Firewall on all the time and enable Stealth Mode only as needed. Go to Settings > Network > Firewall, flip the toggle, then hit Options to manage Stealth Mode.

In a recent development, another hack for maintaining privacy on public networks is to enable rotating MAC addresses, which randomizes the identifier your device broadcasts when scanning for and connecting to wifi. If you use either your real MAC address or a fixed one (random but unchanging), it's easier to track your activity on that network, including when you arrive, how long you stay, and when you leave. Rotating addresses are best for public, shared networks you temporarily connect to, and don't require a login via a captive portal (like hotel wifi). You can turn this on for specific networks via Settings > Wi-Fi > [Network Name] > Details and change Private Wi-Fi address to Rotating.

Industry observers note that images and screenshots contain metadata, such as timestamps, device and hardware details, and, in the case of photos, physical location. Much of this information is stripped automatically when you share files to social media or via encrypted messaging apps, but if you're sending them via text or email, posting to forums, or sharing over AirDrop, metadata remains intact. You can easily remove metadata from your images right on your desktop. Select the file and hit control + click to bring up an options menu, then go to Quick Actions > Convert Image. Uncheck the box next to Preserve Metadata, then hit Convert. (This is also useful for quickly converting HEIC to JPEG without opening a separate app.).

Industry observers note that apple collects information about your device for diagnostic purposes or to improve apps and services, some of which is shared with third-party app developers. This may include crash and usage data as well as recordings and transcripts of Siri interactions and iCloud analytics. You can disable sharing for some or all of these categories under Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements.

In a recent development, you may be surprised by the number of apps and system services that use your device's location in the background. You should definitely disable location services for third-party apps that don't require location to function. You can find these toggles under Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services. You can also turn off location permissions for some Apple apps and services if you're not using them on your device, like Weather and Maps. Finally, tap System Services and disable location for any non-essential features—at the very least, disable "Mac Analytics" and "Significant Locations & routes" (which lets your Mac and other iCloud devices learn locations and routes you use often).

In a recent development, third-party apps on your Mac that need access to your device's camera and microphone have to request permission, and it's easy to grant this in the moment and then forget that you've allowed it. You should regularly audit which apps have these permissions and revoke access from those that don't need them on a day-to-day basis. Disabling them forces the app to ask again. Go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone or Camera to see the allowed apps and flip the toggle to disable permissions.

Sources indicate that another permission type you may have granted without much thought is local network access. This allows third-party apps to discover and communicate with other devices—printers, smart speakers, and IoT devices—on your home wifi. While this may be useful for services like Spotify that cast to connected hardware, other utilities, media apps, and games probably don't need to be mapping your network in the background. Go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Local Network to audit permissions and disable those that aren't needed.

Another important permission to check concerns third-party apps that have access to your Mac's full disk, which includes data from Mail, Messages, Safari, Home, Time Machine, and admin settings. If an app only works with files you explicitly open and save, it doesn't need full disk access. Legitimate use cases may include antivirus and malware scanners, productivity tools, or backup utilities that you trust. You can also audit which apps have access to specific files and folders. This is under Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access or Files & Folders.

If you're using iCloud to store photos, files, and device backups, your data is encrypted on Apple's servers and in transit. Apple still holds the decryption key, which is useful if you somehow get locked out of your account and need help recovering it, but for sensitive data—including device backups—end-to-end encryption is the most secure way to ensure no one but you can gain access. Advanced Data Protection is an opt-in setting for iCloud that encrypts your information end to end. You'll need to set up an alternative recovery method, such as your device passcode with two-factor authentication, a recovery contact, or a recovery key. Be careful, though: If you lose access to this recovery method, you will lose your data. You can enable Advanced Data Protection on your Mac under System Settings > [Your Name] > iCloud > Advanced Data Protection > Turn On. Note that some iCloud data, including passwords and payment methods, are already end-to-end encrypted by default.

If Your Google Pixel's Camera Is Suddenly Broken, Here's the Fix

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sadly, updates aren't all perfect, as Google Pixel users are discovering this week.
  • In a recent development, here's the situation: Following the November revision, some users are opening their Pixel Camera apps to find an error that reads, "Something went wrong.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that updates are generally good for your devices. The latest Chrome enhancement, for example, patches an actively exploited security vulnerability, while Apple's latest updates stop people from seeing iMessages they shouldn't have access to. In most cases, it's beneficial to update your tech to the latest software version whenever possible.

Sadly, updates aren't all perfect, as Google Pixel users are discovering this week. As reported by Android Authority, Google's November upgrade apparently shipped with a bug that breaks some Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 cameras. Seeing as Pixels are rather famous for their shooters, this is a decidedly unfortunate glitch.

In a recent development, here's the situation: Following the November revision, some users are opening their Pixel Camera apps to find an error that reads, "Something went wrong. Close and open the Camera app again," with a "Learn More" link to, well, learn more. Others aren't receiving the error, but are instead running into a blank Camera viewfinder, as if the lens is totally covered. What's more, some users are reportedly saying that the concern is present on third-party camera apps, not just the Pixel Camera app. That would imply this is an issue with the camera system-wide, not just the Pixel Camera app itself.

To be clear, it doesn't seem like this is a universal problem. It's not like all Pixel users are now running with broken cameras. But based on the forum complaints Android Authority discovered, it seems reasonable to assume that this glitch isn't limited to just a handful of unlucky Pixel owners.

Recent findings suggest that luckily, there is an apparent workaround here, though it's not totally obvious. Some users are having no luck restarting their Pixels, while others report that a factory reset wasn't enough to restore camera functionality.

According to recent reports, what does appear to work, however, is shutting your Pixel down and waiting five minutes or so. It's not clear why, but giving your Pixel a chance to "breathe" seems to shake the glitch and bring back your camera. As Android Authority reports, that fix comes from "Diamond and Gold product experts" on Google's Support forum.

If your Pixel's camera is giving you grief following the November upgrade, this workaround is definitely worth a try—especially since more drastic measures don't actually seem to do anything. As the glitch does seem to be rather widespread, I wouldn't be surprised to see Google issue a patch in the coming days. But until then, turning your phone off for five minutes may be a decent compromise.

Latest Update: Five Hacks Every Apple Watch Series 12 User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (813 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the latest Apple Watches have a lot of new features that older watches don't, so I figured it was time for a new list of hacks.
  • In a recent development, the Series 12 can finally count steps natively, a task that for some reason is only arriving now, and is restricted to just the newest Apple Watch models.
  • Recent findings suggest that you don’t need this creepy feature listening in to everything, but it can be nice to have it as a backup on occasion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the latest Apple Watches have a lot of new features that older watches don't, so I figured it was time for a new list of hacks. While our general Apple Watch and fitness tracking hacks are still golden, Series 12 devices offer new features like native step counting, a Readiness app, an upgraded heart rate sensor, an AI-based version of Siri, and "audio intelligence" that can replay and summarize real-life conversations, within limits. Here's how to get the most out of them.

In a recent development, the Series 12 can finally count steps natively, a task that for some reason is only arriving now, and is restricted to just the newest Apple Watch models. Enjoy it! To add a step counter to your watch face, long-press on the clock screen to edit it, tap on a complication (that’s what Apple calls those little icons and numbers that appear on some watch faces), choose Activity, and then tap Steps.

Recent findings suggest that you don’t need this creepy feature listening in to everything, but it can be nice to have it as a backup on occasion. A button in your Apple Watch’s Control Center can turn the feature on and off. Keep it off except when you have a structured conversation that you’ll want to refer to later. This feature is currently in beta (which you can try now if you want to), but is expected to be available to everyone later this year.

Sources indicate that it's worth turning off the default setting not just because of the creepiness factor, but also because the recaps work best when there is a single subject of conversation, with a clear start and end, and just one context. If you leave recaps running all the time, your doctor’s appointment will get mixed in with your grocery shopping, YouTube watching, and everyday chatter.

To finish off a recap and make it useful, take a look at the recap shortly after the conversation, tap the three-dots menu, and hit Edit. You’ll be able to adjust the notes and add your own crucial details. Siri won’t identify speakers and seems to shy away from including certain details, like people’s names. You can add in what it missed and also create your own bullet points so that everything gets noted down while it’s still fresh in your mind.

This one isn’t specific to the Series 12, but if you haven’t gotten on board with the pinch and wrist flick gestures yet, now is a great time.

It has been revealed that first, the wrist flick: If a notification is on your screen, or you’re otherwise looking at something you’d rather be done with, just flick your wrist away from you and then back toward you, as if there were a crumb on the watch face and you wanted to knock it off. This will bring you back to the watch face and close whatever you were looking at.

It has been revealed that the double pinch is another useful one, although Apple calls it double tap. This is confusing because you aren’t double tapping the watch, you’re tapping your thumb and forefinger together while wearing the watch. You don’t need to touch the watch face at all. So, when you get a notification or a call, look at it on your watch, and pinch your thumb and forefinger (of the watch hand) together twice. The watch detects the pinch from subtle movements in your wrist, and it will open the notification. You can then use the wrist flick to close the notification. Performing a double pinch when no notification is on screen will bring up your smart stack. You can then double-pinch to move to the next card in the smart stack, or single-pinch to open that card and see its details.

If you want to learn even more gestures, go into the Watch app, and select Accessibility and then Hand gestures. You can remap a whole-fist “clench” to do the same thing as pressing the digital crown, for example, or to open the control center or Siri.

In a recent development, A little rude, perhaps, but helpful: With the new AI-based Siri, sometimes answers to questions can be long-winded. If Siri launches into a novel-length response and you’re not interested in hearing all that, just put your palm over the screen. You’ll instantly be transported back to your watch face, and the Siri response will stop.

If you still want to see those longer responses without having Siri read the whole thing to you, you can set this up on your phone, and the settings will carry over to your watch. On your iPhone, go to Settings and tap Siri, then Responses. Select Silent responses instead of Spoken responses. You can then read through her answers, or skim them, as you prefer.

#4121. 10 Hacks Every watchOS 27 User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1356 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

10 Hacks Every watchOS 27 User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1356 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that watchOS 27 introduces a solid set of upgrades to your wrist—assuming your Apple Watch supports it.
  • With watchOS 27, Apple changed what double-pressing the Digital Crown does.
  • It seems Apple realized the mistake, however, as evidenced by watchOS 27.2.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that watchOS 27 introduces a solid set of upgrades to your wrist—assuming your Apple Watch supports it. While the newest update isn't Apple's most feature-filled, it does include a number of changes that improve the way you exercise, track your health, and locate missing items. That's especially true for anyone with the latest Series 12 or Ultra 4. If your Apple Watch supports watchOS 27, you should know about these 10 hacks:.

With watchOS 27, Apple changed what double-pressing the Digital Crown does. Instead of opening the app switcher, it now triggers Audio Intelligence—if you have an Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4. If you don't have access to those features, the gesture now does nothing.

It seems Apple realized the mistake, however, as evidenced by watchOS 27.2. When you're using an app while running this latest upgrade, press and hold the bottom part of the watch's screen, and you'll trigger the app switcher. You can now jump to a different app, or close an app that isn't working. Sadly, this only works when you're already in an app, and not when you're on the Home Screen, but it's certainly better than nothing.

While you can load up multiple complications on your Apple Watch, they aren't exactly dynamic. That's why I'm a massive fan of the Smart Stack widgets on the Apple Watch, which update dynamically to show contextual information. Now, with the fresh Siri Modular Face, you can access dynamic widgets on the Home Screen. If you've just parked your car, for example, you'll see a widget showing its location; likewise, if you have an upcoming calendar appointment, it will be front and center.

To use the Siri Modular watch face, tap and hold on the screen, go to the end of the list, tap the Plus button, and find and add the Siri Modular watch face. Once you do, you'll start seeing dynamic widgets when you wake up your watch. Don't expect much personalization from this watch face, however. You can customize the colors and add three small complications, but that's it.

Recent findings suggest that the double-tap gesture is one of my favorite Apple Watch features. By tapping your thumb and index finger together twice, you can do things like answer a call or reply to a message. In watchOS 27, Apple took the gesture one step forward. You can now use the double-tap gesture to scroll through your widgets; if you perform a single tap, it then opens the highlighted widget or the shortcut. This means you can open and browse the weather app, or start a workout, without ever touching your Apple Watch's screen.

Sources indicate that your Apple Watch's fresh Music Recognition app has native Shazam integration. What's more, Shazam will record your request even when you're offline and away from your iPhone. The moment you reconnect, the service will identify the songs, which you can see in the Shazam app on your iPhone or Apple Watch.

Industry observers note that it seems like Apple has a library of songs it uses for offline recognition, because in my testing, it was able to recognize a Coldplay song instantly, even when in Airplane mode. To use it, you can either open the Music Recognition app, or you can add the widget for faster access. Scroll up on the Home Screen, go to the bottom of the screen, tap the Edit button, then the Plus button, and add the Music Recognition widget.

It has been revealed that apple Watches have traditionally lacked a live step count widget or complication. To find your step count, you had to go to the bottom of the Activity app, or rely on third-party apps. But even still, these apps never showed live data. You’d always have to wait a couple of seconds to see the updated stats.

According to recent reports, now, if you own the latest Apple Watch Series 12 or the Ultra 4, you can add a live step count widget or complication to the Apple Watch face or the Smart Stack. This will show you your precise step count at all times. To use it, go to the bottom of the Smart Stack, tap the Edit button, then tap the Plus button. Here, find and add the new Step count widget.

Recent findings suggest that siri is no longer a voice assistant that you use for one-off tasks. With Siri AI, you can now carry on multiple conversations with context and memory. It's not as robust as ChatGPT or Claude, but you can use Siri AI for brainstorming, researching, and jotting down ideas for later.

Sources indicate that the Siri AI app on the iPhone indicates all your conversations, and so does the Apple Watch. This means you can continue your Siri AI conversations and view past chats on your Apple Watch. To use it, press the Digital Crown once, then tap the Siri app icon in the center. This will open up all your conversations instead of calling upon Siri. Tap a conversation to continue your chat on the Apple Watch. Of course, anything you do here will be reflected in the Siri app on your iPhone.

The new Find My app on the Apple Watch reveals a single map for finding people, devices, and items. This means you can now locate your family members who are sharing their location with you, as well as AirTags or other Find My items from the watchOS app.

Sources indicate that after opening the app, you can use the Digital Crown to zoom in or out of the map. Use touch to pan around. The map doesn't show all items and people at once, though. Tap the Menu button at the bottom-right corner, and then switch between People, Items, or Devices. If you have multiple items, you can scroll through them using the Digital Crown.

In a recent development, while it's not a Whoop-level feature, the Apple Watch now includes a Readiness score. Instead of individually looking at your training load, sleep score, and vitals, you now have one number that gives you the whole picture.

In a recent development, the Readiness score ranges from 0 to 10 and is based on your recent fitness activity, sleep data, and background health monitoring. If you have a score of 8 to 10, your Apple Watch thinks you can push yourself, or "go for it," as it says; if it's below 5, the watch thinks you should consider lighter activity. This feature, though, is only available on Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. You can use the upcoming Readiness app on your Apple Watch to see this data, but you can also access it on your iPhone in the Fitness app's new Readiness section.

Low Power Mode isn't your only option when it comes to extending the battery life for your Apple Watch. watchOS 27 offers a special Max Extended Workout mode just for long workouts. With it, your Apple Watch disables some features, like splits and alerts, and reduces the frequency of GPS and heart rate readings, in the hopes of extending your battery throughout your entire exercise. To use it, go to the Workout app and select the workout you want. Tap the Goals button in the top-right corner, and choose the Extended option. Then, switch to the Max Extended option and start your workout.

The Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 come with a set of Audio Intelligence features that use the microphones on the Apple Watch, paired with AI models (both local and cloud-based), to identify sounds, music, and record conversation. Thanks to this upcoming feature, one of the iPhone's accessibility features also makes its way to the Apple Watch.

Sound Recognition can alert you when it hears sirens, alarms, doorbells, and more, even when your iPhone isn’t around. To set this up, go to the Settings app on your iPhone and navigate to Accessibility > Sound & Name Recognition > Sound Recognition. Here, enable the sounds you want to monitor, and make sure to turn on the Detect using Apple Watch toggle.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that when Richie Furay was first approached with the idea of creating a documentary about his life, the founding member of Buffalo Springfield and Poco was very skeptical.
  • This is exactly what makes Through It All: The Life and Influence of Richie Furay so compelling.
  • Recent findings suggest that through It All, directed by Denny Klein, has been completed, and will be submitted to festivals in the near future.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that when Richie Furay was first approached with the idea of creating a documentary about his life, the founding member of Buffalo Springfield and Poco was very skeptical. It was nearly a decade ago that his late manager, David Stone, proposed the idea. “I was like, ‘Really?’” the 82-year-old musician remembers over a recent Zoom call from his home in Boulder, Colorado. “‘[But] I’m just the guy in the middle.’”.

This is exactly what makes Through It All: The Life and Influence of Richie Furay so compelling. Furay was a country-rock pioneer who played in two groundbreaking bands (as well as the supergroup Souther-Hillman-Furay Band), but he never became a household name like many of his peers. In the mid-1970s, he converted to Christianity, and devoted his life to faith and his family. “I have to stop and say, ‘Look, it’s not about my name being written in lights at Carnegie Hall,’” Furay claims. “For me, it’s my name being written in the Lamb’s Book of Life that’s really crucial.”.

Recent findings suggest that through It All, directed by Denny Klein, has been completed, and will be submitted to festivals in the near future. The film features narration by Cameron Crowe, and includes interviews with David Geffen, Clive Davis, J.D. Souther, and more. You can also watch Furay meeting up with his Buffalo Springfield bandmates Neil Young and Stephen Stills, in a clip shared exclusively with Rolling Stone.

Below, Furay looks back on his career and discusses what it’s like to watch his life on film, and the legacy he wants to leave behind. “What can I say? It’s been an interesting journey,” he notes. “When I left Yellow Springs, Ohio, to be a folk singer in Upcoming York, who knew what it was going to lead to all these years later, to us talking today?”.

Industry observers note that I imagine it’s surreal to watch a film about yourself. It must be like watching your life flash before your eyes.I know. I was hoping I’d still be around when it came out, so at least I got to see it now.

Industry observers note that nine years in the making is a long time. At any point, did you worry It might not get released?Yeah. With Covid and David passing away, and other things that they have to do to get everything working right… It’s taken a long time. But Denny’s been persistent, and when David was here, he was persistent, too. I knew they were going to go to the finish line as far as they could go. And Denny has certainly picked up the ball and he ran with it. He remarked, “We’re going to make this documentary.”  Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

In a recent development, have you seen the film yet?I did. I saw it over the weekend, on Friday night. That’s the first I’ve seen it. I’ve been the subject, but it’s been their project. So it was kind of all new to me, too. Although we did hours and hours of interviews. And then to break all of that down is like, oh, my gosh. How in the world do you do that?

I’m curious what it’s like to work with Cameron, because this is someone who interviewed you several decades ago.Well, I was Cameron’s first interview for Rolling Stone [in 1973]. And that was years and years ago. He was a kid, and I was a kid. And I had not seen or talked to Cameron for the longest time. And somehow on my social media [in 2017], a Cameron Crowe appeared, and I wrote behind the scenes and said, “If this is really you, I want to talk to you. Because I want to invite you to a show that I’m doing at the Saban Theatre in Los Angeles with my friend Timothy B. Schmit, and I want you to come.” And he wrote back and said, “It’s me, I’ll be there.” And that’s how we reconnected. And then to have Cameron actually be a part of what’s going on here is just more than I could have ever thought of or asked. It’s been really wonderful. He’s such a great guy. I love him.

In the film, he expresses a lot of guilt over his Rolling Stone headline, “Poor Poco: They Were ‘The Next Substantial Thing’ Four Years Ago.” He didn’t write that headline, but I have no idea who did.I have no idea, either. And had it not even been brought up, it was in distant memory to me [laughs].
