Sources indicate that have you seen Almost Famous?A long time ago. It reminded me of Poco to a certain degree, but Poco didn’t really ever attain the success when I was in the band that the movie had the group making at the time. But that’s part of movie-making, and that’s why he is a great filmmaker.

Recent findings suggest that this documentary is emotional at times to watch, because it has interviews with people who are no longer with us: David, Clive Davis, and the great J.D. Souther.As I was watching this, it certainly put a bump in my stomach as well. I mean, from Clive to J.D. to Steve Cropper that I worked with and others. Wow, it just goes to show you how short life is, and you never know how long you’re going to be here.

Recent findings suggest that when I was recording [2022’s] In the Country, J.D. came to the studio to do the interview. We hadn’t seen each other for a while. And people try to make things up. I can’t believe how much people try to talk about, “Oh man, these guys couldn’t get together. They didn’t like each other.” It was all nonsense.

They don’t know what’s going on in the background of people’s lives. J.D. and I never had any difficulties at all. I will say that when David Geffen put the band together, it looked good on paper, but not always what looks good on paper translates into reality. Because David’s thing was, “Hey, we’ll just put together another Crosby, Stills, and Nash.” It’s like, “Really? It’s that easy, David? I’ve been at this for six years now.” And yeah, great songwriters, great singers, great band, great musicians. But like I noted, what looks good on paper sometimes doesn’t translate into reality.

And then, who knows what’s going on in the background? I was in the middle of a personal and family crisis when that whole band got together. That took its toll, but it had nothing to do with how we got together. When J.D. came and did the interview, it was just so good to see him. I mean, the hugs that we had and the pictures that we took. It was just wonderful.

It has been revealed that when was the last time you had seen him prior to that?I guess I went to one of his concerts, and I think it was in Cleveland, and I can’t even remember the year. It was one of his solo concerts, and I was back there with a friend, and we went to see the concert. When J.D. played here in Denver, I would see him, and if I happened to be in the town where he was playing, we’d make the time and go see him.

It has been revealed that do you remember your last conversation with him?It was when we were doing In the Country. There was so much going on there, sometimes it just comes and goes, and I can’t remember. But I remember the feeling that I had after he had left. It was like, “Wow, man, I’m really glad I got a chance to see and talk to you.”.

It has been revealed that let’s talk about this Buffalo Springfield conversation that takes place in the film. When did that happen?About two years ago. So it was very recent. We were actually going to get together before we got together in California, but there were some worldly circumstances that got involved, and Neil said, “I can’t do it now.” It was interesting though, because Stephen and I had a relationship before Stephen and Neil or Stephen and Neil and I had a relationship. So Stephen and I went on to do an interview together, which was our part of the being together. And then we had the three of us together, which is a whole other dynamic.

I love that no matter how many years pass, you guys are still laughing and enjoying each other’s company.Isn’t that cool?

When did you last see Neil before that?Oh, before that, I guess it would’ve been when we did the [Buffalo Springfield] concerts [in 2011]. That would’ve been the last time that I actually saw Neil.

You seem to not have any hard feelings about that reunion falling apart.No. It all worked out typically, as it usually did. I think we did seven demonstrates, and then Bonnaroo was the very last one. And after every show, we’d always get together and we’d decompress and go, and then everybody would go their [separate ways]. After Bonnaroo, I never saw anybody. It was crazy. It was like, “Well, this must be over now.”.

Would you ever play with them again? I’ve seen Stephen’s Light Up the Blues benefit, and he and Neil have both played Buffalo Springfield songs. I’d love to see you on the stage with them.Well, David offered my services for the one about, I don’t know, maybe two years ago, and we never heard back. And I understand. The question hasn’t come up, so I haven’t had to deal with whether I would or not. I love those guys, and a lot’s just passed. We’re getting older and older as we go. I’m getting ready to do my last two concerts starting on Friday and Saturday.

The last ever?Well, unless there’s something that comes of the documentary. I’ve made a commitment to go out if there is something. Sundance is coming to Boulder, and if Sundance picks it up for whatever reason, there’s a possibility that I could do a short concert here for that as well.

Other than that, it’s just time. It’s just getting harder and harder to get out on the road. I’m not working at the Sphere every weekend, [like the Eagles]. I love those guys, man. I’ve been out there a couple times now, and I love what they do. I’m so happy for them, but it’s harder and harder for me just to get out and travel around.

What did you think of the Eagles at the Sphere? It’s such an amazing show.Oh, I loved it. My wife Nancy and I saw it, and then I came back and I noted, “My daughter has to see this.” And it took us another, I don’t know, probably eight or nine months to get her out there. But I just had to go, because it was so dynamic. I loved it. I loved every bit of it.

It has been revealed that I mean, Timothy and I have been very good friends for a long time, and we walked backstage and I’m seeing the whole setup that they have out there, and I just love what they’re doing. I think for whatever impact I had on that band or Poco had on the band … well, they had two of my bass players in Poco. So, we must have had some influence on them. But yeah, I love them. The music, you just sit back and you just smile. And plus, the presentation at the Sphere is just absolutely overwhelming.

Industry observers note that what was that like for you when you started hearing songs like ”Take It Easy” on the radio?When I first heard “Take It Easy” it was a heartbreaker, because we had just released “A Good Feelin’ to Know.” We were in the New York area. I’ve played every SUNY there is, every gymnasium. And we had just released it and we’re driving into one of the other state universities in New York, and all of a sudden it was, “Well, I’m traveling down the road trying to loosen my load.” And it’s like, “Oh, boy.” That’s when I got a hold of David Geffen and he convinced me [to form Hillman-Souther-Furay].

I love that David is in the film. He doesn’t do that for a lot of people.No, I know he doesn’t. And David, I feel that both of us have respect for one another. He stayed in my house before. My car broke down and I was bringing him home. That was probably, oh golly, 30 years ago. It was during the Poco time.

I haven’t seen David in a long time, but at one point in time I wrote him a letter. This was probably about 20 years ago, if not more. And I wrote him a letter just appreciating him and our relationship. And you know what? Within a week, I had another letter written back. So we haven’t really seen each other, but I’m very thankful for the relationship that we had over the years.

It has been revealed that your vocals are remarkably preserved. You sound incredible.Well, it’s been by God’s grace, there’s no doubt about it. Because now I feel like I’m one and done, maybe two [shows]. If I try to do three, man, it’s kind of really difficult. I did three in July. We went from Kent, Ohio, down to Cincinnati and then down to Nashville. And by the time we got to Nashville, it was like, “Oh my goodness, this is not the place I don’t want my best voice.” It holds up, and I’m very thankful for that. I’m just hoping it holds up for two more shows.

How did you feel about your later life being portrayed? It’s not something many people know about. You have a very special story.Right. And it was presented in that way. Denny was insistent, and that was the only way I think that this was going to be anything different than any other documentary. Here’s where this guy’s life has led him, and I think they certainly covered that and portrayed that well.

Do you ever think about what your life would’ve been like had Al Perkins not joined the band, and you hadn’t become a Christian? Or if Souther-Hillman-Furay had taken off and you became stars?Yeah, it probably would’ve been different. I don’t know that Nancy and I would’ve made 60 years. So I wouldn’t go back and trade my life today for any of the success that music might have brought me for what I have in almost 60 years of marriage and four daughters and 13 grandkids. There’s not even any way to compare that.

Industry observers note that I’ve been very thankful that the journey has allowed me, even doing 35 years of pastoring a church, to continue to be able to play music. I mean, the two reveals that I’m doing in California, they’re not huge venues, but they’re sold out. And so it makes you feel good that my whole life still is having an impact in touching people’s lives.

According to recent reports, you obviously have very different political views from Neil and Stephen. Does that ever get in the way of your conversations?No, because we’re adults. And that’s how it has with some, and I’ve reconciled with some. For others, they’re respectful of me and I’m respectful of them, and that’s where it stands. And that’s how my relationship with Stephen and Neil has always been.

Yeah, we’ve been different. We’ve been as far apart, probably, as you mentioned, politically as one can be. And it doesn’t matter when we get together. When we hug each other, you can tell that it’s real, that our friendships that we established years and years ago are meaningful. They weren’t just fleeting. They were real, and that’s how it should be.

You can have your opinions about things, and I can have my opinions about things, and you know what? Then let’s move on. When we did a band, it was like a marriage. And if that marriage breaks up, it can be a crisis, but it also can be a workable situation, and we’ve decided to make it a workable situation.

In the film, Neil jokes that he should have gone to Monterey. What are your memories of the festival?I was actually struggling with tonsillitis. I’d just gone through a tonsillectomy or whatever, and it was difficult. But not having Neil there was certainly very difficult. I mean, I loved David [Crosby], and he was a sweet guy. But he did not fill the bill. And even Buffalo Springfield had nine people in and out of the band in two years. It was a Canadian band, and those Canadians, I don’t know what to tell you [laughs], but the original band for me was the band with Dewey [Martin] and Bruce [Palmer], and then Stephen and Neil and myself. And everything else was just trying to patch it together, and it was difficult to do. And Monterey didn’t have the original band, and it made it difficult. But I sure loved watching Otis Redding and Jimi Hendrix. I mean, it was incredible.

It has been revealed that it’s a tragedy that it’s the only known concert footage of the band, and Neil isn’t even in it.Isn’t that incredible? I mean, there’s footage of Bob Dylan. It’s like, “Where did this come from?” And yet you go here and there’s nothing on Buffalo Springfield, nothing. I mean, very, very rare footage of anything.

According to recent reports, how often do you listen to Buffalo Springfield?Not very often. It’s interesting, Nancy and I get in the car and we’re driving someplace. We don’t even put music on the radio usually. It’s just like, let’s just have some peace and quiet in this little cubicle that’s going across the country or going to the next town.

Recent findings suggest that nancy is pretty funny in the film. She’s very candid about how she was going to leave you, but then you told her you became a Christian. She was disappointed you wanted to make it work.I know. There was dead silence. I thought she would be happy, and little did I know she was already making plans for another life. Oh gosh, it broke my heart at the time. It was a very difficult time. That was what was going on in the background during Souther-Hillman-Furay. She was hoping to get out of it and felt, “Oh, I can’t do this now.”.

Recent findings suggest that what was it like for your grandkids to watch their grandfather getting this movie about his life?We’ve tried to make it that I’m just a normal guy that just happened to have a different life than others. We go to all the sporting and dancing events, and they’ve grown up with me knowing me more just like this, than trying to put on a rock & roll show or something. They all sat and they watched it. We had to watch it in different rooms because I think there were 20 of us by the time we got everybody together. And I think they were very touched. I had to go home and I had to digest everything that I saw, and I think they were doing the same thing. Now, if it makes it onto some other stages or something, I think it’ll have a whole different impact on them, and on me.

According to recent reports, you stopped being a pastor in 2017. What brought on that decision?Nancy and I were sitting at a restaurant on Christmas Eve. We usually have our Christmas Eve services. And she mentioned, “Are you OK? The whole left side of your face is drooping.” And we went over to the doctor and I had Bell’s palsy. I’d never even heard of Bell’s palsy.

And at that particular time, I just got to thinking how fast things can happen, how fast things can change. So I made the decision then. I think it’s time after all these years that we spend more time together focusing on ourselves rather than having other things dictate what we do and why we’re doing it. And that was the decision that I made to step away from the pulpit ministry.

In a recent development, so I don’t have a church today. I’m not going to tell somebody how to believe, but I will tell people why I believe. I’ll say that God gave us the gift to sing these songs to you. So it’s a different kind of lifestyle now. It’s not getting up and preparing and doing things for a Sunday morning service or whatever. It’s just life now. What do you want your legacy to be?[Quoting the Bible]: “Well done, good and faithful servant.” On all regards. I have a precious love for the people that have come out and still support me in a musical way. And I’m humbled and gracious that people would still pay money to come to hear me play the songs. And yet on the other side, I want people to know that I have a very strong faith in Jesus Christ, and I want the Lord, when I finally cross that line into eternity, to say, “Well done, good and faithful servant.”.

It has been revealed that if there is one thing you could tell a young Richie, what would it be?Stay focused. And I’m sorry, Angie, but don’t believe all the press you get. Whether good or bad. Because if it’s good for a while, it’s all about to blow your ego up, and if it’s bad, you’re going to just kick the can down the road and be discouraged and disgusted. And you just gotta stay focused, and you gotta stay true to yourself.

Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.
  • Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.
  • There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

Even Chelsea’s in-house streaming had given up the ghost by the end. Consecutive pre-season defeats for Chelsea, but worth remembering that Colwill and Palmer sat out this fitness exercise and Enzo Fernandez is still to return. Palestra’s performances a real positive but the team is still finding its way.

It has been revealed that juventus win a corner late on, but Yildiz’s delivery is too close to Penders. Just two minutes for Chelsea to find an equaliser.

In a recent development, mudryk does well to dig out a cross from the left but the goalkeeper Perin gathers. There will be four minutes of added time to play.

Chelsea not really threatening an equaliser as the game meanders towards a conclusion. Should they score a goal, we will have a penalty shoot-out.

Estevao looked for Mudryk with a reverse pass between full-back and centre-back but there was too much weight on the ball.

Estevao’s free-kick is saved but the bigger news for Chelsea fans is that Mykhailo Mudryk has been introduced from the bench, replacing Nicolas Jackson for the closing stages.

Industry observers note that lavia and Liam Delap involved in some handbags with the Juventus players, Bremer the centre-back in the thick of things too and has been shown a yellow card. Chelsea have a free-kick, Estevao over it from 35 yards out.

Just the one goal scored for Chelsea against top level opponents in pre-season, but I doubt Alonso will be panicking just yet. Chelsea play Milan this weekend before hosting Real Sociedad on August 15th in their final pre season friendly.

According to recent reports, juventus goalkeeper Perin sells Nicolas Jackson a dummy so he can pick a pass into midfield. The Italian side controlling the game quite well since the goal, against a weaker Chelsea team.

Recent findings suggest that chelsea’s younger players will have to dig them out of trouble in the last 20 minutes. There has not been much in the game, Chelsea have shaded it in general play without quite creating enough.

The Kosovan winger with a first-time, left-footed hit from almost 25 yards, curled into the top corner. Nothing Penders could do about it.

More changes from Chelsea: Anselmino, Acheampong, Satpaev, Assugo and Delap the players on, replacing Hato, Palestra, Gittens, Caicedo and Pedro. Alonso finishing the team with his younger players on the pitch.

Jonathan David slides a pass across the Chelsea six-yard box when there was a chance to shoot, but the flag was up for offside in any case.

It has been revealed that penders does well to palm away an inswinging cross from Zhegrova, before Estevao picks out the run of Palestra on the break with a brilliant forward pass. Chelsea corner, cleared. Now Caicedo has been booked for a cynical challenge to stop a break, much like Douglas Luiz.

In a recent development, nicolas Jackson hacked down by Douglas Luiz after he turned on halfway with three or four Chelsea runners in support. Painful one for Jackson, and a yellow card for the former Aston Villa midfielder. Chelsea players not happy with that challenge in a pre-season game.

Chelsea certainly have the upper hand in the game, quick feet from Joao Pedro to win a free-kick in midfield. If either team is going to score the game’s first goal, you fancy it will be them.

This time Chelsea find Palestra with a ball over the top, but his shot at goal is at a comfortable height for the goalkeeper.

Palestra popping up in a centre-forward position again, but his shot towards goal is not struck cleanly. The right-back at the heart of Chelsea’s attacking again.

Two very different XIs out there for the second half.

Penders replaces Sanchez in goal, Sarr on for Tosin, Estevao on for Quenda and Jackson on for Welbeck.

For Juventus: Bremer, Perin, Zhegrova, Owusu and David are on.

Not much to write/phone/WhatsApp home about, so far. The combination between Quenda and Palestra down Chelsea’s right has been the best feature of their football, am sure we will see Estevao on that flank in the second half among other changes. The bumpy pitch and a hydration break has not helped the spectacle.

There will be four minutes of stoppage time, simply a result of the hydration break.

Far too much space opens up between Chelsea’s defence and midfield, with Meritti turning and carrying the ball forward. Boga tests Sanchez with a strike from the edge of the box. That was probably Juventus’s most threatening attack.

Palestra defends well as the last man up against Milik, Chelsea almost undone by Locatelli’s outside of the foot pass.

Sources indicate that robert Sanchez caught under a cross swung to the back post, very unconvincing goalkeeping, but Juventus could not get their shot away in the box. Nicoll-Jazuli then did well to bring the ball away for Chelsea at the edge of the box.

Recent findings suggest that chelsea have another corner, and yet again it comes from a right-sided attack. Chelsea are in ascendancy now after a slow start, but it is a very low intensity contest.

Caicedo with a couple of threatening crosses from a centre-right position, but no Chelsea player can connect with them cleanly. Gittens’s dribbling down the left causing problems for Cambiaso, and he was the one attacking Caicedo’s cross at the back post.

According to recent reports, play has now resumed after the drinks break. No changes from either team, those will come at half time. Chelsea have 21 players sitting on their bench, albeit a number of academy players are on tour.

Time for a hydration break, even though the game is being played under a closed roof.

Sources indicate that chelsea’s right side is their most dangerous, by a distance. Quenda does well to slip Palestra in on the overlap, and his low cross into the six-yard box is cleared for a corner. Juventus clear. Boga with a burst through the Chelsea midfield but the Juventus man then gets his pass wrong.

According to recent reports, kelly with a left-to-right switch to Cambiaso, and his cross deflects off the toe of Miretti in the middle and trickles just wide of the far post. Sanchez was scrambling but I think the goalkeeper had it covered.

Chelsea enjoying their most sustained spell of possession in Juventus’s half so far, without quite carving out a clear cut chance. Juventus defending their penalty area with a back five, but they do not have Bonucci, Chiellini and Barzagli back there anymore.

Quenda with a threatening inswinging cross from the right flank, but Welbeck could not quite rise high enough to direct his header towards the far corner. Quenda was keeping the width for Chelsea with Palestra inside the winger in the box. Quenda then slices a shot over from long range.

Recent findings suggest that welbeck and Caicedo involved in some good combination play, with Nicoll-Jazuli’s outside of the foot pass finding Gittens. Chelsea’s left-winger runs into traffic, but he has been one of the bright spots of the pre-season campaign thus far.

Having watched a couple of Chelsea’s friendlies, there is a lot to like about Palestra at right-back. Tall, long stride, lots of composure on the ball. Will be interesting to see if they can find a way for him and Reece James to start games. Chelsea as a team yet to find much rhythm in the game so far.

Tosin could well find himself down the pecking order this season among Chelsea’s raft of centre-backs, but he makes an key block in the area before Locatelli drags a shot wide from the edge of the box.

In a recent development, former Bournemouth defender Lloyd Kelly is in the Juventus team. The Italian team are looking to press high in the early minutes whenever Chelsea try to play out from the back. Quenda with an early dart at the Juventus defence but he gets the pass all wrong with Palestra overlapping.

Recent findings suggest that palestra with a loose first touch but he recovers and defends well. Like in Sydney, this looks another very bumpy pitch, you can see the join marks between the pieces of turf that have been freshly laid. Coming out of these games without any injuries will be a priority for Alonso.

Juventus get the game started in their pale pink away kit.

Juventus XI: Di Gregorio, Kalulu, Gatti, Kelly, Cambiaso, Douglas Luiz, Locatelli, Miretti, Boga, Milik, Celik.

Subs: Perrin, Pinsoglio, Nava, Bremmer, Rugani, Koopmeiners, Arthur Melo, Cabal, Owusu, Gil Puche, Oboavwoduo, Licina, Durmisi, Yildiz, Zhegrova, David.

Sources indicate that welbeck starts against Juventus, but no Jordan Henderson with the group just yet. As Sam Dean writes here: “Last season, especially, provided evidence that the balance of their squad was not right, and they are now trying to change the internal dynamic by adding more leadership and experience to the team.”.

Recent findings suggest that how long will he stay there? Will he play his way back into Alonso’s team, be shipped out on loan or sold for a fee? Sam Dean assesses the options for player and club in this piece. Out of sight, out of mind could well be the most likely outcome for a player who has missed almost two years of football, and looked extremely raw before his ban.

In a recent development, looks like a back four once again for Alonso, and Danny Welbeck makes his first Chelsea appearance. Pedro will play off Welbeck as a second striker. Geovany Quenda was signed last year from Sporting CP, but joined up with Chelsea this summer. Another wide forward in their collection.

Chelsea XI: Sanchez; Palestra, Fofana, Tosin, Hato; Caicedo, Nicoll-Jazuli; Quenda, Joao Pedro, Gittens; Welbeck.

Chelsea subs: Penders, Sharman-Lowe, Curd, Slonina, Acheampong, Subuloye, Sarr, Diakite, Anselmino, Lavia, Essugo, Watson, Walsh, Kellyman, Mudryk, Estevao Willian, Kavuma-McQueen, Neto, Satpayev, Jackson, Delap.

The wheels of commerce continue to turn for Chelsea in the transfer market but this afternoon Xabi Alonso’s team continue their preparations for the new season against Juventus in Hong Kong.

They have the chance to recover from the ignominy of losing to 10-man Tottenham Hotspur in Sydney on Saturday, but with 19 days until Chelsea’s Premier League opener against Fulham these matches are still a fitness building exercise. The positive from the Spurs game was Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill, Cole Palmer completing 80 minutes – three players who endured injury problems last season.

Another fresh arrival is expected to follow Morgan Rogers, Marco Palesta, Maxence Lacroix, Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck to Stamford Bridge, with the club nearing a deal for Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria.

It wouldn’t be Chelsea without talk of some eye-catching outgoings, with Spurs reportedly interested in Nicolas Jackson and Enzo Maresca eyeing a reunion with Pedro Neto at Manchester City.

Sources indicate that alonso’s team promise to be flexible in their tactical approach this season, but so far he has set up with a back four rather than the 3-4-2-1 system he used to such great effect at Bayer Leverkusen. That could change as availability increases closer to the start of the season, but Palestra’s bursts forward from right-back in tandem with Estevao have caught the eye.

Sources indicate that juventus finished sixth in Serie A last season under Luciano Spalletti, the former Roma and Napoli coach who usually guarantees expansive and attractive football. Turkey left-winger Kenan Yildiz was their top goalscorer last season, and it looks like they will make it through the summer without the left-winger being picked off by one of the Premier League’s elite. Yildiz scored 11 goals in all competitions, and Dusan Vlahovic was the only other player to reach double figures so scoring goals is a problem to address. Lois Openda and Randal Kolo Muani have been signed this summer to strengthen the forward line.

I Analyzed the Seven Biggest AI Chatbots to Determine How Safe They Are for Kids

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1841 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • AI safety for both adults and children is under greater scrutiny than ever before, with a growing number of questions and concerns appearing around how beneficial or otherwise these conversational bots actually are for our mental well-being—even without considering their energy use, ethics, or economic implications.
  • Recent findings suggest that the substantial AI apps, such as ChatGPT and Gemini, are right in the center of these trends, and the companies behind them are taking steps that they promise will keep children safe.
  • OpenAI's ChatGPT has one of the more comprehensive setups in terms of parental controls.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI safety for both adults and children is under greater scrutiny than ever before, with a growing number of questions and concerns appearing around how beneficial or otherwise these conversational bots actually are for our mental well-being—even without considering their energy use, ethics, or economic implications. At the same time, an increasing number of apps and services are becoming age-gated in a growing number of countries around the world, as governments realize that letting kids loose on AI apps, social media platforms, and the web at large might not be the best idea for their ongoing development and prosperity.

Recent findings suggest that the substantial AI apps, such as ChatGPT and Gemini, are right in the center of these trends, and the companies behind them are taking steps that they promise will keep children safe. If you want to know what youngsters in your family may be getting exposed to, and what you can do about it, here's the rundown.

OpenAI's ChatGPT has one of the more comprehensive setups in terms of parental controls. The minimum age for owners is 13, and if you're under 18, you need to have parental consent to open an account—age is predicted via several signals, including what times of day you use ChatGPT and what you talk about.

Sources indicate that accounts for under-18s automatically become ChatGPT for Teens accounts. There's more of a focus on learning and study (with a dedicated study mode), as well as "age-appropriate safeguards to help reduce exposure to sensitive or potentially harmful content." There are built-in protections for "harmful topics," including sexual, romantic, or violent roleplay, graphic violence, and self-harm. These work on top of the safeguards for all users that limit chats about physical harm and illegal activity.

Recent findings suggest that these ChatGPT for Teens accounts can also be linked to a parental account—but while parental consent is required for under-18s to use the service, ChatGPT clearly says that teens do have the option to break the link if they want. If you do persuade your kid to keep your accounts connected, you can set time limits on when the AI bot can be used, and tweak some of the sensitivity settings. However, you can't view any conversations.

Sources indicate that to set up parental controls from ChatGPT on the web, click your profile icon (bottom left), then Settings > Parental controls > Add family member and follow the instructions. It's also worth bearing in mind that ChatGPT app can also be used for free, anonymously, in any web browser, though OpenAI says consumers accessing the AI this way are subject to the default under-18s limits (and can't save chats or access an archive).

According to recent reports, gemini is tied into everything else Google does, and follows the broader rules for Google accounts: No under-13s, unless you're part of a family group and using an account managed by an adult. You can manage your family through the Family Link portal on the web, though as far as parental controls specific to Gemini go, you can only enable or disable access to the AI (settings like screen time apply across all enabled apps).

For all under-18s (partly identified through age estimation), whether or not they're part of a managed family group, Google applies some additional protections. They include preventing the AI from taking on a persona, guarding against emotional dependence on the AI, and discouraging bullying and other forms of harassment. There are also safeguards to limit chats about age-restricted substances like alcohol or vapes, and mental health complications like eating disorders.

These protections for minors are applied in addition to the usual guardrails in Gemini for everyone. The guardrails should lead you away from conversations about self-harm, suicide, violence, and illegal activities, and offer quick links to support in times of crisis. However, Google itself admits that these filters aren't perfect.

According to recent reports, as with ChatGPT, there's a loophole of sorts in that anyone can start chatting with Gemini, for free inside a web browser, with no checks at all. These conversations can't be saved and come up against usage limits fairly quickly, but they're only protected by the general restrictions for all accounts, not the ones specific to minors.

Meta AI will show up in several apps that young people and children are likely to use, including WhatsApp and Instagram, as well as having its own separate app on the web and on phones. The standard restrictions for Meta's social media accounts apply to its AI too: A minimum age of 13, and restrictions for all under-18s. Like many other platforms, it uses some AI magic to flag up accounts being used by minors.

Sources indicate that if you're under 18 and on a Meta Teen account, you'll come up against blocks if you try to get Meta AI to engage in sexual or romantic roleplay, or discuss alcohol or substance misuse. Chats on topics such as eating disorders and self-harm will prompt the AI to offer guidance towards relevant support services.

It has been revealed that meta offers a comprehensive parental control setup for its apps, including Meta AI, but connecting a parent account isn't compulsory for teens. This is handled through the Meta Family Center portal, and parents can get reports on the general topics that kids are chatting about with AI—though they don't get the exact transcripts or prompts. Any self-harm or suicide discussion can trigger an alert to the connected parent account.

All owners, under 18 or over 18, get support and crisis intervention responses when chatting about suicide and self-harm, and there are strict limits on discussing illegal and harmful acts, including drug use and cyberbullying, as well as sexual and adult content.

In a recent development, apple owners have to be 13 or over to have an account, which is required to access Siri AI—anyone younger needs to have an account created for them by an adult, and these accounts can only get at the basic, older Siri. Date of birth must be declared when opening an Apple account, with tighter checks rolling out in many parts of the world.

Recent findings suggest that anyone over the age of 13 can have an Apple account and use the Siri AI app, with or without a connected parent account, as it stands in most U.S. states. This means the well-being safeguards are essentially the same for teens as they are for adults: There are safeguards around self-harm, suicide, sexual and violent content, and illegal commands. It's one of the more conservative AIs when it comes to what it will talk about.

In a recent development, the upcoming and improved Siri AI can be managed to some extent by the new parental controls available in iOS 27 and Apple's other software updates for 2026—Apple has clearly seen the way the wind is blowing—but this is optional for teens. It depends on whether or not you can corral your kids into a Family Sharing group.

If your teens are in your family group of customers, then the standard Screen Time rules apply for controlling app usage limits and device access (in iOS Settings, tap your name, then Family to get at them). There are also options for disabling certain Siri AI features, such as the writing tools or the image creation capabilities.

In a recent development, like Gemini/Google and Apple/Siri, Copilot is tied into the wider Microsoft ecosystem, and access for under-18s can be managed through it. Users must be 13 or older to hold a Microsoft or a Copilot account—and again, there's some underlying tech in place to detect anyone who might be deliberately lying about their age.

According to recent reports, if you've got a teen using Copilot, you can manage their access through the standard Microsoft Family Safety portal. You're able to enable or disable Copilot access, set times during which Copilot can and can't be used, and disable certain features like image generation or voice mode. Parents can't read the Copilot chats of their kids, though.

Parental supervision is optional—a teen aged 13–17 can use Copilot without linking their account to an adult one. Microsoft notes people identified as under 18 won't see personalized results or ads, and will get age-appropriate responses regarding risky or harmful content, though there's not much detail on what that entails.

More generally, content around self-harm, violence, adult content, harassment, and harmful or illegal activity is banned on the AI platform. Any prompts about suicide or drugs will bring up support options rather than answers, whether you're an adult or a young person using the service.

Ultimately that means that minors have the same access to Grok as adults, if they want it—an AI platform that combines "weak safety guardrails" and "a range of extremely harmful content" that includes "explicit sexual content, mental health risks, violent content, and inappropriate responses to... offensive content" (that's the Common Sense Media Report again).

In a recent development, yes, this is the AI chatbot that has previously had a problem with deepfake porn imagery, and which has traditionally taken a rather casual attitude towards safety concerns, led by SpaceXAI CEO Elon Musk. While illegal and harmful content is supposedly banned from Grok, its own FAQs admit that certain chats can result in "dialogue that may involve coarse language, crude humor, sexual situations, or violence.".

There is actually a Grok Kids Mode that limits the kind of content that can be shown and the conversation topics that can be added, but it requires customers to self-declare themselves as minors and is easy to bypass. The advice from Common Sense Media seems to be the way to go with Grok: Do not let your teens access it.

Claude's approach to child safety is straightforward: You can only register for an account if you're over 18. It is possible to lie about your age when signing up, but like the other platforms, Anthropic looks at various "signals" in behavior to spot minors—if your account gets flagged, you have to verify your age using an option like face age estimation or Yoti.

There's no free web access to the chatbot, like there is with ChatGPT and Gemini, so if you're under 18, you're locked out from the service unless you know the behavioral tricks to get past Claude's detection systems.

In terms of more general well-being protections on Claude, any chat around self-harm or suicide will guide people towards helplines and other resources for support. Conversations about illegal activities, disallowed speech, and explicit sexual content are banned from the platform. In recent months, Anthropic says it's also reduced AI sycophancy.

That's something of a whistle-stop tour of the substantial seven AI chatbots, but if you're a parent, it should give you some idea of what's out there and how easy it is to access. Besides the parental controls built into these AIs (or not), you also have the settings available at the platform level—Android, iOS, Windows, macOS—to restrict the use of any potentially harmful apps.

EXCLUSIVE: The resurgence of independent television series continues to grow with Justin Long (Barbarian, You Deserve Each Other) and Kate Bosworth (Still Alice, Along for the Ride) starring in The Renovation, a fully-financed indie comedy series. It hails from Lucas Carter (Summer of ’69), Nick Kreiss (Punk’d) who directs all episodes, Intrigue, Script2Screen and Hammerstone Studios.

In a recent development, production has wrapped in Los Angeles, and EPs Intrigue, Script2Screen and Hammerstone will begin shopping the series to streaming platforms and television networks this month for distribution. Related Stories Acquisitions Hulu Buys Animated TV Comedy Pitch 'Detective Agent Derek' From Nick Kreiss, Trio Big Grey Mass Acquisitions Emile Hirsch, Justin Long & Kevin Connolly Pic 'Lice' Acquired By Bob Yari's Magenta Light Studios - Cannes.

Blending scripted comedy with hidden-camera elements, The Renovation centers on a real, unsuspecting married couple, played by real-life married duo Long and Bosworth, who believe they are participating in a home renovation television show. What they are unaware of is the contractors, fellow contestants, and everyone around them are actors, following a carefully constructed storyline designed to test the couple’s instincts, decision-making and sense of right and wrong. Watch on Deadline.

Conceived by writer and producer Carter, The Renovation takes a fresh approach to the hidden-camera format, combining the storytelling and structure of a scripted comedy with the unpredictable reactions of real people.

The concept for The Renovation was originally developed by Carter, who brought the idea to Tariq Jalil’s Intrigue, Carter’s former employer, where the pair further developed the project. Recognizing the unique nature of the format and the creative freedom required to bring it to life, the team decided to independently finance the series. From there, Script2Screen (By Any Means, Mister) and Hammerstone Studios (Bill & Ted Face the Music, By Any Means) came on board to fully finance the production.

The series is executive produced by Jalil, Carter, Kreiss, Alex Lebovici, Ibrahim Mohammed, Yasmyne Mohammed, Chase Vergari, Michael Mazzarra, along with Long and Bosworth. Dan Swimer, Oscar-nominated screenwriter for Borat Subsequent Moviefilm, also serves as an executive producer.

In a recent development, long and Bosworth are repped by Independent Artist Group and Yorn Levine. Kreiss is repped by Underground and Morris Yorn.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Global stock markets have been volatile as investors continue to assess geopolitical risks in the Middle East, fundamentals and valuations of companies in the artificial intelligence (AI) market and key economic data.

Top Wall Street analysts help investors look past near-term noise and pick attractive stocks with solid long-term growth potential.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

In a recent development, credo Technology (CRDO) provides high-speed connectivity solutions for AI data centers. Robust AI-led demand for the firm's copper and optical interconnects has boosted revenue, driving a solid year-to-date rally.

In his latest research report, Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya raised his price targets on major semiconductor and semiconductor capital equipment stocks, with the price target for CRDO jumping to $340 from $252 with a reiterated a buy rating.

The 5-star analyst noted that Credo is seeing continued strength in the demand for its AECs (active electrical cables) from major and emerging hyperscalers. Moreover, the company has additional growth opportunities in optical DSPs (digital signal processors), ZF optics, ALCs (active LED cables), and PCIe retimers. These products are expected to begin ramping up production and profits in 2027-2028.

Recent findings suggest that following a meeting with the company at the 2026 BofA Global Tech Conference, along with recent channel checks, Arya raised his sales outlook for Credo by 2%-11% for fiscal 2027-2028 and his earnings per share (EPS) outlook by 5%-15%. The improved estimates reflect a strong AEC market outlook over the next five years and the company's "bulletproof reliability and incremental nature of its optical portfolio.".

Arya based his fresh price target on a price-to-earnings multiple of 34x 2028 earnings, compared to the prior valuation of 33x 2027 earnings, saying it reflects contributions from new product adoption in coming years.

Industry observers note that arya ranks No. 84 among more than 12,300 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 62% of the time, delivering an average return of 31.5%. See Credo Technology Statistics on TipRanks.

Sources indicate that next on this week's list is Facebook- and Instagram parent Meta Platforms (META). Recently, Meta introduced consumer and business paid subscription plans for its Family of Apps and a newly introduced suite of Meta One (AI) subscription offerings.

In a recent development, following the launch, Evercore ISI analyst Mark Mahaney reiterated a buy rating on META with a price target of $930. Mahaney views the rollout of the latest subscription plans as a revenue diversification initiative, which could have a modest impact on revenue and eventually an even greater impact on operating income.

The 5-star analyst explained that he doesn't expect these latest offerings to significantly affect near-term revenue growth due to their phased rollout and potentially low initial conversion rates. But he believes that even modest adoption within Meta's massive user base (over 3.6 billion daily owners) could evolve into a significant high-margin revenue stream over the long term.

Mahaney highlighted that META is among Evercore ISI's top three, large-cap long-term picks, alongside Amazon and Spotify. His channel checks remain positive on Meta. Moreover, Mahaney noted that the Mark Zuckerberg-led manufacturer is successfully using AI to enhance user and advertiser satisfaction, reflected in engagement and return on ad spend (ROAS).

"What we now have with Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp Plus subscriptions is another attractive greenfield monetization opportunity for Meta – one that is not captured in Street estimates," concluded Mahaney, adding that his 2028 revenue estimate is 5% above Wall Street's consensus projection.

  • Ultimately, he didn’t hold out, though that’s probably for the better: His self-released debut hour, Thief of Joy, broke out as one of the best reviewed of last year, while being recognized for impressive viewership on YouTube — surpassing a million views within a week, with over 6.4 million all time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Comedian Gianmarco Soresi once mentioned that he procrastinated filming an hour special, “holding on to the most destructive thought a creative can have: I’ll do it when someone pays me for it.”.

Ultimately, he didn’t hold out, though that’s probably for the better: His self-released debut hour, Thief of Joy, broke out as one of the best reviewed of last year, while being recognized for impressive viewership on YouTube — surpassing a million views within a week, with over 6.4 million all time. And now, Soresi has secured the kind of mainstream gatekeeper payday that he originally desired, with his debut Netflix hour God Forbid set to premiere Dec. 3. Related Stories News '3 Body Problem' Sets Season 2 Release Date At Netflix News Harlan Coben's 'The Innocent' Lands Greenlight At Netflix As Streamer Strikes Overall Deal With StoryMath.

In a recent development, named one of Deadline’s Comedians Ready to Break Out In 2025 — and subsequently, one of our Comics Who Won 2025 — Soresi has had one of the swiftest and most impressive rises of any stand-up in recent memory. A performer with roots in musical theater, he spent years chasing acting before deciding to explore stand-up. It took just a decade for him to garner a reputation as one of the art form’s rising stars, through a combo of kinetic live shows, solid social strategy, a hit podcast and popular side projects like the live show, Theater Adult. Watch on Deadline.

For Soresi, a goal consistently at top of mind is to offer fans an “elevated stand-up experience.” He says it took him four to five years to figure out what he could uniquely bring as a stand-up — how to synthesize his strengths as a joke writer with “performance abilities” accrued from his years as an actor. 2022 was a breakthrough year as that in which he was named a JFL Newly introduced Face, garnering industry recognition while showcasing a knack for “play logic and set pieces and movement and musicality” that sets him apart.

Whereas Thief of Joy afforded Soresi the opportunity to introduce himself and his comedic voice to a broad audience, God Forbid may well expand his audience further, as he delves into “the next level of what I’m thinking.”.

For the comedian, 2026 has been a time of connection — a year in which he’s begun to feel “much more connected to the world in a way that I didn’t, whether it be comedically or as a human being.”.

Says Soresi, in today’s episode of Comedy Means Business, “I went to Asia for the first time this year, let alone to do stand-up comedy. And there’s something that feels like it changes when you see just how big the world is. And the fact that I could go somewhere for the first time and sell out a theater and have people who know me, and I don’t know anything about the world, but we’re able to connect through some similarities…And also seeing all these other comedians and these different vibrant comedy communities, some which are much earlier in the trajectory of their stand-up evolution, some of which have taken different paths… I just feel like it’s made me want to expand the way that I think. I see humanity from more vantage points.”.

In conversation with Deadline, Soresi talks about his experiences traveling the world for stand-up in 2026, and the experience of building his career at a time when it’s “really tough to build a sustainable life” as a stand-up without being entrepreneurially minded. He explains how he writes and evolves an act on tour, the difference between the material you’re likely to get from him at an early vs. late show, why it took him a while to find his comedy community, and his experience seeing both great success and great challenges contending with volatile social media platforms. Soresi also discusses why “we miss the gatekeeper,” the brutal nature of touring life, the importance of “sh*t talk” in keeping artists honest, recent Fire Island reveals with comedian friend Jay Jurden, performing for two weeks this summer at the Edinburgh Fringe, his fascination with how the rules governing speech vary from country to country, navigating personal and professional life with girlfriend and manager Tovah Silbermann, and more.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that america’s skies were empty on Friday after the Federal Aviation Administration ordered an emergency ground stop of all flights — the most drastic safety measure the agency can take and only its second invocation since the Sept. 11 attacks. While the nation scrambled to figure out what the hell was happening, it didn’t go unnoticed that the commander-in-chief was nowhere to be found.

In a recent development, donald Trump didn’t address the ground stop — which lasted about four and a half hours and continues to disrupt flight schedules and airport operations — until Sunday, when in a Truth Social post, he called for Congress (which has been controlled by Republicans the past two years) to approve more funding for the FAA. As his Cabinet struggled to provide an explanation and assure the public the nation was not under attack, Trump couldn’t be bothered to provide so much as a post or a call-in to Fox News over what Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin described as a “crisis.”.

So what was the president doing?

Industry observers note that according to a Monday report from The Atlantic, while panic consumed every airport in the country, Trump was in the Oval Office chatting with actor Jon Voight and calling other Hollywood figures, discussing his proposed “Entertainment Revitalization Act.” Sources told The Atlantic that as the crisis began to unfold, the president continued to talk to his celebrity and entertainment contacts, prompting one person he called to gently ask if he shouldn’t be focused on the response to the ground stop. As The Atlantic put it, “Trump demurred.”.

Shortly after the meeting, as millions of American passengers remained stranded in airports and struggled to make accommodations for their disrupted travel, Trump penned a lengthy Truth Social post lauding his efforts to bring “Entertainment back to the United States of America.”.

Sources indicate that “Everyone feels strongly about the Motion Picture and Television Industry — and so do I, and we all want to save it. It was MADE IN AMERICA, and must STAY IN AMERICA,” he wrote. There wasn’t “anything for me to do,” Trump told reporters when pressed about his conspicuous absence on Monday, adding that he wouldn’t take “any responsibility” for the emergency stop.

Recent findings suggest that the administration has not yet provided a coherent explanation of what exactly went wrong on Friday. So far, they have fallen back on their usual cop-out of Blame Joe Biden for their own mismanagement. Mullin claimed an update to the aged communications infrastructure of the FAA overwhelmed the system and caused a major crash. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy suggested the outage was caused by a router failure triggered by the replacement of aged copper wiring.

In a recent development, trump, in his first on-camera statements attempting to explain the cause of the outage, was just as incoherent. It was “very old equipment. Some of it, 55 years. And I hate to blame [anyone], but the Biden administration hooked up a lot of copper into glass,” Trump claimed, blaming his predecessor for systems he readily admitted were decades old. “If you know anything about electrical engineering, uh, you cannot hook up copper into glass,” he added. In a weekend appearance on CNN, Duffy defended Trump’s lack of public involvement in the response, claiming that Trump had directed Stephen Miller to direct the Cabinet to treat this as a “whole government approach” when host Dana Bash pressed him on why Trump didn’t make any public statements despite posting about his irrelevant fixations throughout the afternoon.

Sources indicate that “He was fully engaged,” Duffy insisted. It’s hard to believe when no one in the administration actually seems to have their eye on the ball.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Upgrade, 8:41 p.m.: The Federal Aviation Administration declared it has ended the ground stop.
  • On Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop for all airports in the United States.
  • Industry observers note that there are a number of options for tracking flights, whether you have your flight number or not.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Upgrade, 8:41 p.m.: The Federal Aviation Administration declared it has ended the ground stop.

On Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop for all airports in the United States. If you're planning to fly this afternoon or evening, or you have friends or family doing the same, you're likely concerned about tracking flight statuses. While there's still a lot we don't know, there are tools to help track flights at this time:.

Industry observers note that there are a number of options for tracking flights, whether you have your flight number or not. If you have the flight number, the fastest method is to Google it: Google will display a live tracker of your flight at the top of the results page. You can also head to the airline's official website to track your flight: United Airlines, for example, has a flight tracker where you can either enter your route information or your flight number. Most, if not all, airlines will have a similar tool you can use.

Alternatively, you can use a site or service that tracks all flights. FlightAware is one such site and has a flight tracker that lets you search flights—so long as you know the origin and the destination. If you have the flight number, your iPhone can help: You can enter your flight number into Spotlight search to see a live tracker, or you can text a contact your flight number, then tap the link that appears under the number to see a tracker of the flight.

Industry observers note that at this time, the exact reason isn't totally clear. According to the agency, “The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports following communication issues impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers,” but the FAA hasn't remarked what caused those communications issues or when they expect to lift the grounding. The grounding order comes one day after a massive Microsoft outage that disrupted service for owners of Outlook, Teams, and other Microsoft products. It also comes one day after Ars Technica reported that the FAA was rolling out an AI-powered tool to help manage air traffic across the country.

This is only the third time in U.S. history that the FAA has made such an order—once after 9/11, and again in January of 2023 due to a pilot alert system matter; the latter ground stop lasted around 90 minutes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More than 13 years after Breaking Bad’s heart-pounding finale, “Felina,” drew in a record 10.3 million viewers, Dean Norris, who played DEA agent and Walter White’s brother-in-law Hank Schrader in the hit series, is telling the stories that happened when the cameras weren’t rolling, including a surprising group of actors and other celebrities he watched one big scene with.

Recent findings suggest that in his latest Breaking Bad oral history, Do What You’re Gonna Do, Norris catalogs the show’s entire run through first-person interviews and stories from members of the cast and crew — including Bryan Cranston, Bob Odenkirk, Aaron Paul, Krysten Ritter, Giancarlo Esposito, and the late RJ Mitte. (Spoilers ahead: It’s been 13 years, people. Move it or lose it!).

Sources indicate that when Breaking Bad premiered in 2008, the gritty crime series about a cancer-ridden high school science teacher making crystal meth to pay his debts didn’t just captivate viewers. It became a cultural juggernaut. Throughout five seasons and 62 episodes, viewers watched as the Albuquerque, New Mexico, everyman Walter White — played by Bryan Cranston — transformed into a bald, pork-pie-hat-wearing drug kingpin named Heisenberg. The series won 16 Emmy Awards during its run, including four Cranston wins for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series. Norris calls this book the “definitive” oral history of Breaking Bad, a side of the hit show and its leading stars that fans might never have heard before.

In one chapter, Norris describes watching his character’s jaw-dropping death in the series’ penultimate episode, “Ozymandias.” After filming the episode, Norris did not watch the entire thing until it aired — when he was invited to actress Kate Hudson’s Pacific Palisades home.

“This was not the sort of event where I would have been welcomed a few years earlier, but now I was Hank Schrader, the dogged cop on Heisenberg’s heels,” Norris writes. “I was one of the leading players on television’s hottest show, and with that status came a steady stream of invitations to a world I had never known, nor even been particularly interested in visiting. But I must admit, it was pretty cool.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

According to Norris, it was a surreal experience to watch a group of people who had no idea what was coming see the episode. And the venue, a popular celeb’s house, also meant the inclusion of a few unexpected guests.

It has been revealed that “When Hank took a bullet to the head, the whole room let out a collective gasp. Someone hit pause on the DVR remote, and everyone —­ Kate Hudson, Bruce Willis, Goldie Hawn and Kurt Russell, Elon Musk (!?), just to name a few —­ turned to stare at me,” he writes. “I almost felt like I was supposed to take a bow. Instead, I just smiled, as if to say, It’s OK. I’m all right.”.

Elsewhere in the book, Norris talks about the kismet nature of how key cast members found their way to the show. When talking about Mitte — who died in October at age 34 — Norris reveals that Mitte was the last member of the White family cast. While the choice to have Walter White Jr. have cerebral palsy was made in order to make Cranston’s character seem more sympathetic to viewers, Norris notes that Mitte “crafted a fully formed portrait of an adolescent at the center of a family storm; one whose disability may have helped shape him but did not define who he was.”  Trending Stories Raye, Rosalía, and Ella Langley Lead 2027 Grammy Nominees Jennifer Lopez Teases New Music on ‘Fallon’: ‘This Does Feel Like a Happy Era’ Robert Pattinson Is the Next James Bond Watch Buffalo Springfield Come Together for the First Time in Many Years.

When interviewed about his role, Mitte said he often channeled his own experiences with family and responsibility to make Walter White Jr. as strong of a character as possible — including spending five seasons building up to a final showdown standing up to his father.

Industry observers note that “A lot of the decisions I made for Junior were based on my own experiences as a young adult. At the time, I was still a child, but I utilized those moments from my own life of having to stand my ground and make that decision —­ realizing who I am and what I need to do to take care and provide for my family,” Mitte says in the book. “In the show, Walt was no longer doing that. He was actually creating more danger for his family. I think it’s very powerful that Walt Jr. had the ability to stand his ground and to put those boundaries in place: ‘You’re out. This is my family now, and you’re not a part of it.’”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that dolly Parton nostalgia sure seemed to be running high with Grammy voters. The country music icon, who died in August at 80, received three posthumous nods when nominees for the 69th awards were announced Monday morning. And since Parton scored two nominations in the category of Best Country/Duo Group Performance, that Dolly glow also helped secure nods for artists like Zac Brown, Lainey Wilson, and even Queen Latifah.

In a recent development, to celebrate her 80th birthday, Parton assembled a cast of all-stars to rerecord her song “Light of a Clear Blue Morning,” which originally appeared on her 1977 LP, New Harvest … First Gathering. Wilson, Parton’s goddaughter Miley Cyrus, Reba McEntire, and Queen Latifah (scoring her first country-music Grammy nomination) all sing with the Country Music Hall of Famer on the recording, released as a charity single to raise funds for pediatric cancer research at Monroe Carell Jr. Children’s Hospital at Vanderbilt in Nashville.

Brown and his eponymous Zac Brown Band, meanwhile, are nominated for Best Country/Duo Group Performance for their Parton collab “Butterfly.” An inspirational ballad meant to guide Brown’s children through life, the song was featured as a duet with Parton on his 2025 album, Love & Fear. Brown performed it during the recent Parton tribute special, and has been making the song, with Parton’s recorded vocals, part of his live shows. “Getting to be friends with her and getting to make music with her and just be around her, the example she set as a human being: loving everyone,” Brown mentioned during an August concert just a few days after Parton’s death. “One of the most talented, funny, beautiful human beings I’ve ever met in my life.”  Trending Stories Raye, Rosalía, and Ella Langley Lead 2027 Grammy Nominees Jennifer Lopez Teases Newly introduced Music on ‘Fallon’: ‘This Does Feel Like a Happy Era’ Robert Pattinson Is the Next James Bond Cynthia Erivo, Travis Barker Honor Phil Collins With Significant Vocals, Big Drums at Rock Hall Ceremony.

Parton’s final Grammy nomination this year is all her: She’s in contention for Best Audio Book, Narration, and Storytelling Recording for the reading of her 2025 memoir, Star of the Show: My Life On Stage.

In total, Parton has 58 Grammy nominations over the course of her career and 10 wins. Her most recent came in 2021, when “There Was Jesus” was named Best Contemporary Christian Music Performance/Song. This is a particularly exciting year for country music at the Grammy Awards, as Ella Langley secured seven nominations, including in the Big Four categories; Miranda Lambert earned a Producer of the Year, Non-Classical nod; and women dominated the Best Contemporary Country Album field.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that dividend stocks remain a popular choice for investors seeking steady income and higher portfolio returns. However, with thousands of dividend-paying companies to choose from, identifying the right stocks can be challenging.

In this regard, recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can provide useful insights and help identify dividend stocks backed by solid fundamentals and with attractive upside potential.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

According to recent reports, independent oil and natural gas company Permian Resources (PR) is this week's first dividend stock. The company recently paid a quarterly base cash dividend of 16 cents per share. At an annualized dividend of 64 cents per share, PR offers a dividend yield of 3.5%.

Sources indicate that recently, Evercore analyst Chris Baker initiated coverage of Permian Resources stock with a price target of $25. The analyst believes that the company is well positioned to benefit from improving U.S. shale demand after the Iran conflict, thanks to its low-breakeven inventory that can boost free cash flow growth. Baker also noted PR's disciplined consolidation in the Permian Basin.

Furthermore, the 5-star analyst highlighted the tech giant's focus on a single basin and management's efficient capital allocations across expansion efforts, strategic acquisitions, and share buybacks. Baker noted that management focuses investments on the higher-return Northern Delaware Basin, helping boost profitability.

"The key piece of our work here, and the reason we think PR deserves a higher multiple relative to more finite or less flexible shale stories, is that PR runs an acquire and exploit model," said Baker.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Massachusetts judge announced on Monday that a new trial would begin on March 29 to determine whether Lindsay Clancy murdered her three children in 2023. Clancy was tried this past summer, but in September, the jury announced it was deadlocked and ended the proceeding in a mistrial. Prosecutors have not yet indicated whether they would try Clancy, whose previous trial lasted six weeks and was a cause célèbre, for first-degree murder charges, lesser counts, or at all, according to The New York Times, despite Judge William Sullivan’s announcement.

That mentioned, prosecutors’ agreement to another trial suggests they will pursue first-degree murder charges since, the Times reports, a judge could have ruled on second-degree murder or manslaughter charges without a trial.

Sources indicate that the previous trial ended with 11 jurors wanting to acquit Clancy for the deaths of her children — Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and 8-month-old Callan — and one man, Michael P. Desronvil, insisting she was guilty. Another juror described him as “very arrogant” and claimed he had admitted he had reasonable doubts about her guilt. He disagreed with that claim. “Based on all the physical evidence, key witnesses and what the prosecution presented, I thought it was enough proof that she knew exactly what she was doing and planned,” he said in a September statement. Recent findings suggest that since the mistrial, a GoFundMe campaign benefiting Clancy’s parents quickly raised more than $1.1 million since their lives were “put on hold.” Clancy’s lawyer, Kevin Reddington, also petitioned President Trump to pardon his client. Reddington, who sees another trial as double jeopardy, has said he feels it’s cruel to put Clancy through another trial.

Clancy remains in custody at a state hospital, according to the Times. Her lawyer had argued that she was experiencing postpartum depression and had hallucinated a voice that told her to strangle her children and kill herself. The case’s next hearing is scheduled for Dec. 30.

#4089. Google Killed Its Dark Web Report, but You Can Still Monitor Data Breaches

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (775 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Google Killed Its Dark Web Report, but You Can Still Monitor Data Breaches

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (775 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google’s Dark Web Report used to be the only consumer-focused platform that let users scan major data breaches, dark web marketplaces, and private forums to see if their personal information had ended up in the hands of hackers.
  • Sources indicate that google says it sunsetted Dark Web Report because, although the information it provided was generally useful, the service failed to provide “helpful next steps” for owners whose data was found on the dark web.
  • Sources indicate that dark Web Report may not have been perfect, but it was the only early warning system of its kind that was available for personal use and let people run scans free of cost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google’s Dark Web Report used to be the only consumer-focused platform that let users scan major data breaches, dark web marketplaces, and private forums to see if their personal information had ended up in the hands of hackers. But the firm discontinued the service at the start of 2026, with newly introduced scans stopping on Jan. 15 and all accounts deleted on Feb. 16.

Sources indicate that google says it sunsetted Dark Web Report because, although the information it provided was generally useful, the service failed to provide “helpful next steps” for owners whose data was found on the dark web. Google promised a fresh service that would provide more actionable intel, but that service has yet to materialize, and there haven’t been any further announcements about it yet.

Sources indicate that dark Web Report may not have been perfect, but it was the only early warning system of its kind that was available for personal use and let people run scans free of cost. Now that it’s gone, however, there are plenty of other services that offer the same service at varying costs and levels of effectiveness. Let’s talk through the nature of the insight that Google's reports offered, how it collected that information in the first place, and what options exist in the market to replace it.

Google debuted the Dark Web Report in March 2023 as a premium feature available to Google One people, but later extended it for free to anyone with a Google account and moved it to the "Results about you" dashboard.

You'd set up a monitoring profile with your name, date of birth, physical address, phone number, emails, and Social Security Number if you lived in the U.S. After that, you could head to the dashboard anytime you wanted to run a free scan across dark web forums and marketplaces, publicly disclosed corporate data breaches, and other hidden online spaces to see if any of your personal information had shown up there. It was easy to use—but not a lot of people knew it existed in the first place.

Recent findings suggest that it’s unclear what prompted the internal decision at Google, but in the absence of concrete next steps, it is reasonable to think the reports could create panic for the uninitiated. There’s no way to remove your information from the dark web once it’s already in circulation there. Still, having an early warning so you could reset 2FA or self-lock your SSN isn’t without merit.

But perhaps more importantly, most people with Google accounts didn’t know and hadn’t heard of the Dark Web Report’s existence. Google has likely taken it as a hint that people want more active remediation tools than simple alerts, which is why it’s now directing users to the Password Manager, Passkeys, and “Results about you” dashboard instead—though, again, the tech giant hasn't followed through on a direct replacement for Dark Web Report, despite teasing such a feature.

Many of the top dark web scanners draw from the same well of information, scanning against major data breaches and dark web spaces. Several also offer breach notifications that send you email alerts when your details show up in a periodic scan. However, none of that is worth paying for because Have I Been Pwned or Mozilla Monitor cover those features quite well for free. Even the default password managers from Google and Apple come with some ability to monitor leaked credentials.

Sources indicate that there isn’t an easy way to scrub your information from the dark web once it ends up getting leaked. But you can take steps to protect sensitive information or financial data once you know there’s been a leak. If a password has been compromised, reset it immediately. Also, enable 2FA on the affected account for added security. Even better, switch to a passkey if that account supports it. If not, authenticator apps are a safer way to receive 2FA codes than standard SMS.

Industry observers note that if your Social Security number has been leaked, freeze your credit with Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion. You can do this by contacting each agency separately. Freezing your credit will prevent unauthorized credit withdrawals and protect your credit score from abuse by attackers. If one of your credit or debit card numbers has ended up in a breach, call your bank to freeze transactions on that card immediately.

Finally, get in the habit of using email aliases instead of sharing your actual email address with every platform and service provider. Addy.io and Proton’s SimpleLogin are both popular services that let you generate temporary email aliases that point to your inbox.

Industry News: The Grammy Nominations Blanked Harry Styles. What Happened?
