💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Grammy nominations today are full of surprises — but the big shocker is the name that isn’t there.
  • Industry observers note that you can practically hear fans around the world asking the Grammys: What kind of pills are you on?
  • It has been revealed that it can’t be overstated how weird this is.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Grammy nominations today are full of surprises — but the big shocker is the name that isn’t there. Harry Styles got zero nods for his acclaimed album Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally. The last time he dropped an album, Harry’s House, it won Album of the Year, while his single “As It Was” got nominated for Song and Record of the Year. In January, he released KissCo, a deeply personal and experimental statement — but also a wildly successful hit, debuting at Number One and spawning the chart-topping “Aperture.” Yet it got no Grammy nominations at all. How did this happen?

Industry observers note that you can practically hear fans around the world asking the Grammys: What kind of pills are you on? (Not the good ones, that’s for sure.).

It has been revealed that it can’t be overstated how weird this is. Michael J. Fox got a Grammy nomination. Shaggy got one. So did Fred Armisen, Michelle Obama, Frank Zappa, Tim Curry. There’s Queen Latifah and the Pixies’ Black Francis — in the country category. But not Harry Styles. Hell, even Kanye West got nominated for Best Rap Album — who thinks West had a more successful year making music than Styles? The Recording Academy, that’s who.

The album was submitted in the major pop categories, including Album of the Year and Pop Vocal Album. “Aperture” was submitted for Record, Song, Pop Solo Performance, Music Video—all categories where he’s been nominated before. “Coming Up Roses” was submitted for Best Arrangement; the Netflix special One Night in Manchester for Best Music Film. (KissCo was also submitted for Album Cover, but this year’s nominees are tough to explain — Charli XCX and Slayyyter got shut out too.) Where Styles didn’t submit was the Dance Pop categories, or even Rock, which might have been easier going.

Recent findings suggest that but this is just a drastic break with Grammy history. In the past 50 years, when any artist wins Album of the Year, they get nominated for their next album, in some category or another. It’s almost unheard-of for them to get shut out next time. It’s only happened 3 times: Mumford & Sons won AOTY in 2013 (for Babel), Steely Dan in 2001 (for Two Against Nature), Toto in 1983 (for Toto IV). They all soon released follow-ups that got zero Grammy noms. But these follow-ups weren’t really comparable to KissCo—none of them hit Number One, or included a Number One hit. So there’s no real precedent for this. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

In a recent development, every other Album of the Year winner got thrown a bone for their next studio album, with a nomination or two. That means Christopher Cross, Phil Collins, Natalie Cole, Tony Bennett, Norah Jones, George Michael, Celine Dion, Bob Dylan, Santana, OutKast, Herbie Hancock, Arcade Fire, Kacey Musgraves, Jon Batiste. But not Styles. (Obviously, there’s a few Best Album winners where there wasn’t a follow-up, when the artist dies or quits or is Lauryn Hill.).

It has been revealed that the Grammys tend to be legacy-minded, by definition — once the Academy decides you’re a Grammy type of artist, you remain a Grammy type of artist. There’s a certain “incumbent advantage.” Grammy voters are old, old, old, and they’d always rather vote for someone they’ve already voted for. His one-time opening act Kacey Musgraves won AOTY for Golden Hour, then put out a follow-up that nobody liked much, Star-Crossed — but still snagged a couple of country nominations for the song “Camera Roll.” That’s how it usually works. Not this time.

According to recent reports, it’s even stranger since Harry has been a key part of the Grammy ceremony in recent years—at this year’s show, when Bad Bunny won Album of the Year, Harry was the one who handed it to him. It was the big dramatic climax of the night — who can forget Bad Bunny breaking down in tears at his table, after hearing Harry read the name?

But it was hardly the first show-stealing turn for Styles, as in his “Watermelon Sugar” that kicked off the 2022 ceremony. He had to fight an uphill battle getting Grammy recognition, since he started out as the Academy’s absolute least favorite kind of artist — a singer in a boy band, a British one no less, who formed on TV for a reality show, tsk-tsk. But the Academy eventually caught on to what the audience already knew, recognizing him with his first Grammy for “Watermelon Sugar.” He became one of the first winners in history to give his acceptance speech wearing a feather boa — a very Harry touch. According to recent reports, kiss All the Time has been acclaimed as one of the year’s boldest and best albums, moving way out of the Harry’s House comfort zone where he easily could have stayed. It’s not a universal pop crowd-pleaser like Harry’s House, without any undeniable radio blockbuster like “As It Was” or “Adore You” or “Watermelon Sugar.” It got plenty of bewildered first-week reviews, largely from people confused by the moody electroclash club sounds, misinterpreting the title to think this was the straight-up disco record it plainly wasn’t. So for many people, the music took time to appreciate. But it holds up to nine months of heavy listening, with bangers like “Dance No More” and “Ready, Steady, Go” as well as intimate ballads like “Coming Up Roses” and “The Waiting Game.”.

Industry observers note that styles chose not make the safe follow-up he could have cranked out in his sleep. He made sure nobody could mistake KissCo for Harry’s House Part 2: Better Homes and Gardens. That’s never been how he operates as an artist. He’s the guy who blew up in One Direction, yet made his solo move with a totally uncommercial and eccentric singer-songwriter statement, inspired by the Laurel Canyon 1970s. His debut solo single was “Sign of the Times,” a glam-rock piano epic about death, building for almost six minutes, conceding nothing to trends or the radio. A bold and brazen statement—but it proved him as an artist who was determined to go his own way, rather than chase anybody else’s idea of pop success.

That mindset has worked out for Harry, to say the least, after the astounding year he’s had in 2026. He’s been packing stadiums around the planet for his Together, Together tour, with the innovation of playing multi-night residencies in a few cities. (He hasn’t made it to L.A. yet — is that why the Recording Academy didn’t notice?).

It has been revealed that his 30-night run at Madison Square Garden — by this tour’s standards, the tiniest and most intimate of venues. —was a career highlight, even when he wasn’t busting out the slutty shorts. But he’s kept the show evolving and changing as it travels, with so many ambitious peaks—in London, his orchestral performance with “Bridge Over Troubled Water,” or in Latest York, his indie-sleaze electro-punk detonation of “Kiwi.” He also had an unforgettable moment in the year’s biggest and best movies, Project Hail Mary, where the “Sign of the Times” karaoke scene is one of the year’s most poignant music moments.

If there’s anything we know about Styles, deeply private though he is, it’s that he’s just not interested in celebrity cliches. He’s not the kind of pop star who chases red carpets and award demonstrates. Remember, last year on Oscar Night, he not only failed to show up, he spent the day running the Tokyo Marathon without telling anyone he was doing it. (He did even better at the Berlin Marathon.) When he was in New York for his 10-week run at Madison Square Garden, he wouldn’t have been caught dead at a fancy club or party or gala. Instead, he simply walked to work every day, prowling the city streets with no handlers or entourage, just his trusty “Techno Is My Boyfriend” baseball cap. On the final night, the Garden gave him a banner to commemorate his record-breaking run of sold-out shows, presented by the Knicks’ Jalen Bruton. For this historic occasion, Harry was dressed as a pizza rat. Sources indicate that the KissCo snub already looks like one of the great comic gaffes in Grammy history. But if winning Grammys were the kind of thing that interested Harry Styles, he’d be a very different kind of artist. But nearly ten years into his solo career, he’s kept proving it over and over again — he’s a headstrong boy who does exactly what he wants, not what he thinks an audience will expect. He works with people he knows and trusts, not the buzziest pros, and he only releases music when he’s passionate about it, like his hero Thom Yorke. As he told Yorke this summer, in their Rolling Stone Musicians on Musicians cover story, “You have to just be, ‘What do I want to listen to at this time in my life? What is it that I feel like I want to do, say, make?’ And the fact that people are going to hear it — that realization happens later.”.

According to recent reports, that’s why he does everything from the heart — and that’s exactly why the audience has responded. It’s truly baffling that the Grammys missed out on a chance to be part of the KissCo story.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that google has given its AI-powered "Ask Maps" feature a major upgrade, adding tools for trip planning, real-time route guidance, appointment finding, and saved-list search. The updates begin rolling out today on Android and iOS.

Sources indicate that google launched Ask Maps last March as an AI assistant designed to handle questions and requests more complicated than simply searching the word "bar" or "groceries." Instead of performing simple keyword searches, the idea behind Ask Maps is that you can describe several specific requirements at once, and Maps will find places that match them all. For example, you could ask for a restaurant with outdoor seating for a certain number of people, and "Ask Maps" will factor in your past searches and give you results. Of course, AI assistants have a habit of making things up, so even with today's roll-out, you'll want to double-check your sources before you drive an hour to the wrong restaurant.

Recent findings suggest that to me, this is the most useful latest feature launching today. Whether you're planning a day trip for holiday shopping or something more ambitious, like a three-day road trip with coastal hikes and oceanfront dining, Ask Maps will put together a day-by-day schedule. Each plan includes insider tips and numbered map pins for every stop, so you can see the whole route at a glance. Once you're happy with the plan, you can share it with friends and family or export it to Google Docs on desktop.

According to recent reports, when it's time to head out, you can ask Maps to pull up your itinerary, or look for the "itinerary" badge in your chat history. You'll see real-time details such as live traffic conditions, whether a place is currently open, and even the vibe at your next stop.

Plans can change on the fly, too. Ask Maps to add a scenic viewpoint or a lunch spot along the way, then tap to get directions to your next stop straight from the itinerary.

Here's what else you can use Ask Maps to do, starting today.

Industry observers note that pulling up directions now surfaces "Know Before You Go" tips for your route. These include where to park or charge your car, along with real-time conditions like weather, potential delays, and tolls.

Ask Maps is also gaining some agentic capabilities. Allegedly, you can just ask, “Find me a 4 p.m. nail appointment near me,” and Ask Maps will show you open slots across nearby businesses. In addition to finding appointments, Google says this agent will be able to call local businesses on your behalf—stay tuned while I wait for the upgrade and test this one out myself.

If you keep lists of saved places, Ask Maps can now search them for you. Ask something like, "Which spots saved in my lists have availability for 5 in the next 30 minutes?" Ask Maps looks across your lists and checks live availability, so you can pick a place and go.

It has been revealed that these updates start rolling out today on Android and iOS. Travel itineraries and saved-list search are available everywhere Ask Maps is offered. "Know Before You Go" route tips and appointment finding are launching first in the U.S., with more regions coming soon.

#4085. Breaking: Inside the Wild Nights of Martin Scorsese and Robbie Robertson’s 1970s L.A. Adventure

Breaking: Inside the Wild Nights of Martin Scorsese and Robbie Robertson’s 1970s L.A. Adventure

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 18 min read (3577 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollingstone

⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, jonathan Taplin reached out during the summer of 1976, 10 days into the shooting of Latest York, New York.
  • Recent findings suggest that not long after, Taplin recalled, he and Robbie Robertson visited Marty at his office on the MGM lot.
  • In a recent development, later, Robbie met with Marty over dinner at the Mandarin, an upscale Chinese restaurant in Beverly Hills, at the time a novelty.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, jonathan Taplin reached out during the summer of 1976, 10 days into the shooting of Latest York, New York. He’d reconnected with the Band. The guys were planning an all-star farewell concert on Thanksgiving at the Winterland Ballroom, the promoter Bill Graham’s San Francisco venue. Marty had obviously moved well beyond the concert-documentary phase of his career, but might he consider filming the proceedings?

Recent findings suggest that not long after, Taplin recalled, he and Robbie Robertson visited Marty at his office on the MGM lot. “He was living a very crazy existence,” Taplin remarked. “First off, he was having an affair with Liza Minnelli. And yet his wife, Julia Cameron, was around on the set all the time. So he was constantly ducking out. He had a dressing room on the MGM lot that had a daybed in it. It was very, very weird. It was insane. And they were all doing so much coke.” Steve Prince (“a kind of hangout guy, driver, bodyguard, and coke dealer”) had firmly become “part of the entourage” by that point, Taplin added. “He was the guy who would stand outside of Marty’s trailer on the set of Newly introduced York, New York and bar the door.”.

In a recent development, later, Robbie met with Marty over dinner at the Mandarin, an upscale Chinese restaurant in Beverly Hills, at the time a novelty. In an auspice of their future partnership-in-crime, each man brought along his wife and girlfriend, in Marty’s case, Julia and Liza, in Robbie’s, his wife, Dominique Bourgeois, a Québécois journalist, and her friend Geneviève Bujold, the actress. Marty, the music fanatic, held Robbie somewhat in awe: They were the same age, but Robbie had joined the Band at 16 and had been woodshedding with Dylan when Marty was still an anonymous film student struggling to complete his second short. Robbie took note of Marty’s intense gaze that night, given a slightly devilish cast by his dark Vandyke beard. Later he would say, of possible directors, that Marty “was the only person that knew enough about the fucking music and grew up on it just like me, and was basically just as much a punk as the rest of us. He could relate to the whole fucking thing.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

In a recent development, after dinner, they hit On the Rox, an after-hours bar on Sunset Boulevard, upstairs from the Roxy nightclub, which had become a clubhouse and discreet drug spot for hard-partying celebrities like John Lennon, Jack Nicholson, and Harry Nilsson. They started talking about documenting the concert “on a small level, maybe just video or 16mm,” Robbie said. Marty knew United Artists and the producers of New York, New York would never allow him to moonlight on another film, even a documentary, simultaneously. Then again, hadn’t John Huston managed to sneak off for massive-game safaris during the filming of The African Queen? Couldn’t Marty slip away with a film crew over Thanksgiving weekend, when the New York, New York production would be on holiday anyway, not to shoot an elephant but a simple rock concert? As Robbie revealed the guests he’d invited to perform — Dylan, Muddy Waters, Van Morrison, Joni Mitchell, Neil Young — Marty stopped pretending to fight. What the hell would the studio do, fire him?

Seeds of the pair’s drug buddydom were also sown that night. Robbie and Marty had been “sneaking in and out of the bathroom as if we all had weak bladders,” Robbie noted. “Trying to be very proper.” At a certain point, Marty, who seemed to have a nasty cold, asked if anyone had nasal spray. Robbie gave him a look, unsure if he was cool or not, then decided to risk it. “This might help clear it up,” he said, producing a vial of coke a friend had just palmed him. Marty shook his head. “I’ve got that. I just need some Afrin or something.” He’d actually meant nasal spray. Neither man would be so basic as to quote the ending of Casablanca, but come on. The beginnings of beautiful friendships aren’t so common they should pass unnoted.

In a recent development, production paused for Thanksgiving break, and as planned, Marty went up to San Francisco to film the Band’s Last Waltz concert. A director in a more reasonable frame of mind (unclouded by cocaine megalomania) might have thought, Okay, I’m already contractually bound to complete the biggest feature film of my career, and I’m technically sneaking off to work on this other dubious project, so I should probably keep things relatively low-key. Robbie had initially suggested simply shooting in 16mm, after all. Instead, Marty storyboarded the entire production in advance based on the set list (timing shots down to specific lyrics and instrumental passages), convinced set designer Boris Leven to dress up the Winterland Ballroom with props from the San Francisco Opera, and brought along seven cinematographers (including László Kovács, Michael Chapman, and Vilmos Zsigmond, who would go on to DP Michael Cimino’s The Deer Hunter) to film the entire thing in 35mm, which had been Kovács’ idea. “Can the cameras even shoot that long?” Marty had asked. “You won’t know unless you try,” Kovács noted. Related Content Charli XCX to Cameo in Martin Scorsese’s New Horror Film With Leonardo DiCaprio, Jennifer Lawrence Amy Helm Allegedly Caused $2 Million in Damages to Levon Helm Studios, Lawsuit Claims 50 Years Ago Today: The Band Warm Up for ‘The Last Waltz’ in Asbury Park Levon Helm’s Family Embroiled in Dispute Over His Famed Woodstock Venue.

It has been revealed that during much of the postproduction of New York, New York, Marty had also begun crafting a cut of The Last Waltz. Everyone involved agreed the 35mm footage of the show looked amazing, in this case Marty’s substantial swing had paid off, they had something, and he glimpsed a shot at redemption for having been fired from Woodstock all those years ago — he would make the greatest concert film of all time! They had too much, in fact, the concert having lasted over six hours — multiply that by seven cameras — but also, somehow, not enough: Robbie Robertson realized the concert had failed to represent a pair of key influences on the Band, country music and gospel. (The original concert had been “too lily-white,” the Band’s Levon Helm later said.) So the same week in May that Star Wars came out, Marty and the musicians reassembled on an MGM soundstage to record additional material with the Staple Singers and Emmylou Harris. Marty also filmed interviews with the members of the Band at Shangri-La, their studio in Malibu.

During a production meeting at the house on Mulholland Drive, Robbie and Marty discovered their personal lives happened to be falling apart in tandem. “You know, my wife threw me out, she left me, I have nowhere to go,” Robbie blurted out, admitting that he’d been crashing at hotels and occasionally at Shangri-La. In his posthumous memoir, he described the spontaneous confession as “embarrassing,” given that Marty “came from a certain place and culture where you didn’t reveal personal things.” But Marty surprised him. “‘You could stay here if you want!’ He leaned in, speaking more quietly. ‘Julia just moved out. She’s gone. It’s just Steve and me.’”.

A Hollywood bachelor pad! There was plenty of room, and such proximity would be useful for any questions that might arise during The Last Waltz edit and sound mix. A splendid arrangement. How could it possibly go sideways? “It didn’t take but a day or two to fall into this process,” Robbie remarked, with his Canadian accent pronouncing the “pro” like someone talking sports. “We were like animals sniffing around for the trail, and hit it real quick, and it went into this thing kind of automatically. Those other voids that had been there in our lives were totally consumed. You couldn’t think of anything else but what was going on. It was very urgent, boom boom boom, one after the other, in, out, people in, people out, this movie, this studio, music, film, just full steam ahead.”.

Full steam ahead. He’s being intentional in his vagueness because so much of their friendship revolved around things friends knew better than to discuss outside the inner circle, because in real life Marty and Robbie had become more than friends, they’d become drug buddies, which is a different kind of friendship, it’s a conspiracy — you and your mate versus the straight world, constantly on the make, constantly trying to figure out where to cop and who has what and where you might be able to duck into a toilet stall or back room or secluded corner table, and it all becomes incredibly serious and important-seeming, but also? It’s pretty funny. So many squares wandering around with no fucking clue what you and your drug buddy are getting up to. You’re pulling one over on the world! And every so often, if someone does seem to have your number, there’s a pleasing bit of frisson, an unspoken moment of comity. Oh, you get it too?

The great drug-buddy duo of literature, drawn from real life and embellished in a way that felt hilarious and true to anyone who has ever been one, remains Raoul Duke and Dr. Gonzo — Hunter S. Thompson and Oscar Zeta Acosta — in Thompson’s Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas. Describing a work of art as being like “____ on acid” has been a tired formulation for at least three decades, but in this case it’s literal and straightforward: Duke and Gonzo were Laurel and Hardy, Abbott and Costello — choose your favorite slapstick pairing — on acid. Thompson fashioned his adventures in the mode of a classic comedy team, and Robbie and Marty, who had seen those pictures and almost certainly read Thompson, Marty having at one point considered directing a Fear and Loathing script by Larry McMurtry, carried on the tradition, only in their case they were Hope and Crosby on coke and Quaaludes.

Robbie soon began calling Marty “Maestro,” lovingly fucking with him, with his self-conception of his work as within the tradition of the Great Directors. But he also meant it.

According to recent reports, in his memoir, Robbie dated the fateful production meeting to February 1977, about five months before Julia described retrieving her typewriter from the house she “shared with Martin” in her own book. Given the degree of drug and alcohol consumption in their respective scenes, neither narrator can necessarily claim the mantle of greater reliability. The public record, with its numerous examples of the Scorseses appearing together as a couple throughout the period in question, would seem to support Julia’s timeline. But given the history of Hollywood publicity machines manufacturing happy facades, it’s certainly not dispositive, what with so much riding on the success of Newly introduced York, New York and the likelihood of studio preference for minimal drama surrounding the director of an already troubled production.

Another record of this period, previously undiscovered, comes via [longtime Scorsese collaborator] Mardik Martin, who spent a fair amount of time at the Mulholland house and, with the initial cooperation of Marty, Robbie, and other witnesses and active participants, later began work on a script about that mysterious nocturnal period of their lives, one in which Marty, most of all, descended into what can only be described as a kind of madness — engaging in multiple overlapping love affairs, consuming heroic amounts of cocaine, rarely sleeping, harboring (literal) messianic delusions, and in the end very nearly dying. Mardik’s unfilmed script (dated April 15, 1985) and notes capture those lost years in granular and intimate fullness. His writing practice incorporated extensive research, which for this script meant recording and transcribing hours of interviews with the cast of characters, including Marty, Robbie, Steve Prince, and Isabella Rossellini, who became Marty’s lover and eventual third wife. Famous people employ publicists to quash these sorts of stories, and Mardik’s fealty to reality in his scénario à clef ultimately contributed to the project’s demise. And so he filed his tapes and pages away, where they remained unseen until several years after his death in 2019. The material called back to seedy Hollywood tales of the past, this time with mountains of blow and a rock and roll soundtrack.

The unmade film had the perfect title: Mardik called his script Insomnia.

Sources indicate that in the script for Insomnia, Mardik described the Mulholland house as “a large, unpretentiously luxurious dwelling, sparsely but tastefully furnished. Rare and beautiful movie posters dominate wall spaces.” Robbie had been touched by the spontaneity and kindness in Marty’s offer of a bed and soon enough settled into the screening room, a converted garage with a screen, projector, convertible sofa, and poster of Fritz Lang’s M. As roommates, he and Marty would eventually fall into a routine consumed by working and partying, the lines often blurry in a manner familiar to a touring musician like Robertson and more novel for an overscheduled motion-picture director, though Marty would prove a quick study. He was spending his days editing The Last Waltz at a production office at United Artists — they’d sold the film before its completion based on the quality of the concert footage — while Robbie bounced around various music studios handling production work on the soundtrack album and writing and recording a upcoming suite for the film.

Marty being Marty, their parties on Mulholland involved not only drugs and women but marathon movie screenings. Home video had just come on the market, but Marty preferred to pick up film prints. At the studio, Robbie might receive a call from his new housemate excitedly detailing the double or triple feature he’d programmed for the evening, and, oh, by the way, what time did Robbie think he’d be home? An hour, an hour and a half, something like that? An hour later, on the dot, the phone would ring again. Where are you? The food is ready! They’d both just ditched their families, but Marty had become the wife in a Forties domestic comedy.

Not that Robbie felt henpecked. He adored what he took to calling their Odd Couple routine and looked forward to the nightly master classes.

Sources indicate that eventually, they hung a sheet of paper in the kitchen for the jotting of titles to screen, their version of a chore list. Sometimes Marty would insist upon slogging through a trashy B-picture to reach a single extraordinary scene. Robbie’s tastes ran more toward the classical art film, surrealists, and gloomy Swedes: Bergman, Buñuel, Jean Cocteau. Later, they would laugh, Marty told Mardik, about “how I’d invite girls to my house to watch movies and bore them to tears with endless conversation about films.”.

To keep the dawn at bay for as long as possible, the vampires had Steve Prince, their Renfield, install special blackout blinds in the projection room and eventually throughout the entire house, a task Robbie said Steve approached as seriously as if he’d been placed in charge of the Manhattan Project. “From that point on,” Robertson wrote in his memoir, “most of our lives were lived in darkness.” If a movie was playing, no matter the time of day, the only light came from the screen. Geneviève Bujold told Women’s Wear Daily in December 1977 that she’d recently become acquainted with Marty through “a friend” and had been attending some of the late-night screenings, mentioning a double feature of The Uninvited (Lewis Allen, 1944), a ghost story, and Dodsworth (William Wyler, 1936), an adaptation of the Sinclair Lewis novel. The old projector made “so much noise even the neighbors can hear it squeaking,” Bujold said, and Marty would run “two or three films a night, one on top of another, whoosh.”.

Whoosh! The drug scene at the Mulholland house “was more than you normally would see,” acknowledged Taplin, who wasn’t exactly naive, having worked with the Band when three of its five members had serious heroin addictions. “I mean, there were a lot of people taking a lot of cocaine at that time. That was the drug of choice at that point. It made people feel like they were the most genius people in the world. It was around. But Marty and Robbie’s situation was unusual.”.

It has been revealed that there may have been “a little tinge of an educational thing” for Marty as well, Robbie said, Robbie who’d been on the road since he was sixteen, at the tail end of the rockabilly era, when he started playing for Ronnie Hawkins, the Ontario-by-way-of-Arkansas wild man who told Robbie and the other future members of the Band he couldn’t offer much in the way of salary but promised they’d “get more pussy than Frank Sinatra.” Because they took drugs and grew out their hair and beards, the boys’ club of New Hollywood directors found themselves routinely portrayed as something akin to their musical heroes, but for the most part they were solitary, film-obsessed nerds. Disposable income and the license of quasi-bohemian artistry allowed them to inhabit a rock star–adjacent space. But it would take an actual rock star like Robbie to edify a relative novice like Marty when it came to the problems of fame, the privileges of celebrity, and how one might discreetly inhabit a life of excess without pushing away the spotlight. “He was always uptight,” Robbie said of his friend. “He couldn’t relax with the thing.” Robertson could speak in mobster code better than Marty himself.

By the time they moved in together, Robbie had recorded one of the great face-melting guitar solos of the 1950s (on Hawkins’s cover of Bo Diddley’s “Who Do You Love,” which Greil Marcus called “possibly the most menacing piece of rock ’n’ roll ever made”). He’d played guitar on Blonde on Blonde and been onstage with Dylan on the U.K. tour when the crowd yelled “Judas!” He’d drunk corn liquor with Sonny Boy Williamson and played in Jack Ruby’s Dallas nightclub in 1963 (alongside a one-armed go-go dancer) a month before the Kennedy assassination. And he had already written “Up on Cripple Creek,” “The Night They Drove Old Dixie Down,” “Chest Fever,” “The Shape I’m In,” “Caledonia Mission,” “The Weight” —.

He just grinned and shook my hand. “No” was all he said.

— songs that spoke to his generation while also sounding haunted and outside of time.

It has been revealed that in the opening interview section of The Last Waltz, Marty sits stiffly in a sports coat and trim beard, asking questions he already knows the answers to and coaxing Robbie to speak in clippable sound bites. Robertson, meanwhile, in his brown leather jacket and unbuttoned canteloupe-colored shirt, comes across as relaxed and louche and doesn’t seem to take the exercise very seriously. Though in reality, of course, he’d been the driving force behind the concert and film. “Ask me that again,” he tells Marty at one point, leaning forward in his chair. As Marty repeats himself, Robbie’s eyes wander, and before the question is finished, he’s snatched a fly from the air, or pretended to.

Cool Robbie always marveled at the passionate intensity Marty seemed incapable of not bringing to every relationship. In general, Robbie, his latest date on his arm, was never sure what he might find back on Mulholland. Marty the mad Sicilian might be having a wild screaming match with one of his girlfriends. Robertson, per a transcript of one of his interviews with Mardik: “There will be glass flying and breaking and loud, crazy arguments. (Makes me think of so many, but let him tell you about them.)” In any case, Robbie dedicated himself to giving his friend, as he put it, “an education of the road,” a primer in “how to deal with all of that and let the good times roll.”.

According to recent reports, but he also understood that for Marty, the evening could not properly begin until he got home, so eventually feelings of guilt about working so late would creep into his consciousness and he would begin making excuses to people in the studio before heading back up to the Hollywood Hills. “The food is ready” almost always meant pizza from Two Guys from Sicily had arrived, their best delivery option, substandard for New York but passable for Los Angeles. (“Disgusting,” Robbie noted.) The movies might not start until two or three in the morning, Marty being, as Robbie once said, a believer in “the same thing Napoleon believes, that anyone who sleeps more than three hours a night is a fool.” An important caveat to the movie start time being everything had to wrap before the sun came up, for dawn had become “a scary thing” to the Maestro, it meant something ominous. “Ask him what,” Robbie told Mardik.Dawn coming up, Marty said, “meant death.” Trending Stories Raye, Rosalía, and Ella Langley Lead 2027 Grammy Nominees Jennifer Lopez Teases New Music on ‘Fallon’: ‘This Does Feel Like a Happy Era’ Robert Pattinson Is the Next James Bond Watch Buffalo Springfield Come Together for the First Time in Many Years.

To Robbie it just meant he better get some sleep.

Industry observers note that sharon Horgan had a string of British hits (including a couple we'll talk about here), before scoring stated successes with Divorce, Shining Vale, and Bad Sisters. She's rapidly rising in the ranks of TV super-producers, the acerbically funny HBO Max rom-com Youth (in which she also stars) being just the latest.

Sources indicate that this earlier series created by and starring Sharon Horgan is a family sitcom that feels far more believable than most, seeing Irish primary school teacher Sharon (Horgan) hooking up with American ad exec Rob (Rob Delaney) over the course of a week, only to discover that she's pregnant once he returns home. They don't really have feelings for each other, but decide to give it a go at being a couple, eventually falling into marriage just before the birth of their child. There are lots of jokes and plenty of acerbic dialogue, but this isn't Married... with Children. Sharon and Rob can be a bit nasty to each other and to their sloppy friend group, but there's also something rather sweet in the show's conviction that having someone to be a mess with can be one of life's great joys. Stream Catastrophe on Prime Video.

In a recent development, A little more of a high-concept here, but nevertheless an effective show about reimagining yourself in middle age. Younger follows Liza Miller (Sutton Foster), a recently divorced woman in her 40s who finds that age is a barrier to reentering the publishing industry she left years earlier. After a compliment convinces her that she could pass for a younger woman (poor thing), she manages to convince the right people that she's just 26 in order to land an entry-level job. Seven seasons of misadventures ensue, but much of the show revolves around the twisty-turny relationship between Liza and Josh (Nico Tortorella), a tattoo artist in his twenties. Stream Younger on Netflix.

Bridget Everett stars as Sam Miller, who struggles to find her latest direction after moving back to her hometown to care for her dying sister. (Don't worry: There's plenty of comedy in the drama, and it's not as heavy as it sounds.) She's solidly middle-aged and starting over, kinda—making new friends in a familiar environment where she has to confront the past and the future alike. Luckily, her love of singing—and a community of goofy oddballs—are there to help. It's another story of a person of a certain age, trying to rebuild their life following an upheaval. Stream Somebody Somewhere on HBO Max.

Sources indicate that when all else fails: Start a punk band. This drama from Sally Wainwright (Gentleman Jack) sees five women start a punk band as a lark, just a fun way to kill some time by entering a local talent context. The women realize very quickly, though, that they're very, very pissed off—about the workplace for women, menopause, a diminished dating pool, caring for aging parents and grown children—all of it tied up in the ways in which we treat women, and particularly middle-aged women. The band is a way to reclaim their voices, which doesn't erase or negate any of their problems nor drama (and there's plenty here), but gives them a platform with which to make some noise about it. Stream Riot Women on Britbox.

More of a traditional sitcom, not that there's anything wrong with that, this one builds a lot of goodwill with the performance of Leanne Morgan, its lead and co-creator (alongside Susan McMartin and Chuck Lorre). She plays the show's lead: a Knoxville, Tennessee wife and mom, who finds herself suddenly single in her 50s after her husband of 33 years leaves her. It's a genial, old-school hang-out show with a phenomenal veteran supporting cast that includes Kristen Johnston, Ryan Stiles, and Tim Daly. Stream Leanne on Netflix.

As she says more than once, she's going to take on the fashion world with a "body-positive attitude, cute v-neck, and some lip-gloss." Stream Survival of the Thickest on Netflix.

It has been revealed that certainly the goofiest take here on the idea of starting over in mid-life, this is very much a traditional three-camera sitcom, albeit one with a stacked cast of TV legends. Writer Melanie (Valerie Bertinelli), beautician Joy (Jane Leeves), and soap diva Victoria (Wendie Malick) wind up spending a wild night in Cleveland after a plane to Paris is diverted, discovering in the process that, while they're seen as over-the-hill back in Los Angeles, they're all Ohio 10s—though the sassy caretaker of their house, Elka (Betty White), might not agree. Stream Hot in Cleveland on Paramount+.

She'a s hair younger than Alex, but Fleabag (she's only ever referred to as "Fleabag") is trying to rebuild her life after a bad breakup, with extremely mixed results. Phoebe Waller-Bridge won separate Emmys as the star, creator, and writer of the series. Stream Fleabag on Prime Video.

Inspired by the real-life careers of comedians like Totie Fields and Joan Rivers, the show is warm and welcoming, with great performances and dialogue; it also achieves something rare in being a show about comedy that’s actually funny. Stream The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel on Prime Video.

The substantial life change in this earlier Sharon Horgan hit is a little different: Julia Johnstone's mother had been a big help in taking care of Julia's children, but she's not going to do it anymore, leaving this working mom (Anna Maxwell Martin) to take the full brunt of childcare for the first time (her husband in the picture, but not much use). She joins up with other working moms involved with a local support group, including shallow Amanda (Lucy Punch), star of her own ongoing spin-off. Stream Motherland on Prime Video and Britbox.

Mikel Arteta states he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

According to recent reports, but that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the fresh season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he mentioned.

Industry observers note that “We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”.

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he stated: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”.

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

According to recent reports, the importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Recent findings suggest that only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” stated Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

“We did the first one quite well in a lot of moments but the compete part – especially in and around our box – was not to the standards to win a football match against a good side. It’s better to give them [the goals away] in a friendly match than an official match. It’s always good when you lose a match in pre-season because it creates a bit more fire in the belly.”.

Sources indicate that kepa Arrizabalaga will not want to watch Betis’s first goal back in a hurry. The Arsenal goalkeeper may have got a slight nudge as he came for the ball at a corner but he was all over the place and never looked even in the vaguest control of the situation. Rodrigo Riquelme scored at the far post after the ball sailed over the keeper. Arteta called it a “really sloppy goal”. With former Leeds goalkeeper Illan Meslier having arrived on a free transfer as back-up to Raya, Kepa faces an uncertain future at Arsenal. Moments like this will not help his cause.

In a recent development, he did not feature much last season but is probably best remembered for his torrid showing in the Carabao Cup final defeat by Manchester City in March. He looked as unconvincing here as he did then, as the former Chelsea goalkeeper also sliced a clearance in the build up to Betis’s third goal. Before then, Kai Havertz had turned over possession cheaply from which Nelson Deossa set up former West Ham midfielder Pablo Fornals to score.

Arsenal need more creativity and firepower in attack, hence the interest in Vinícius and Atlético Madrid’s Julián Alvarez. Viktor Gyokeres again looked rather limited here and the likes of Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze are also still to report back. Yet one of the few, brighter aspects of Arsenal’s performances was the sight of the regal looking Riccardo Calafiori marauding forward from a very nominal left-back role.

If Arsenal are going to play more adventurously this season and try to ratchet up things in the entertainment stakes then Calafiori could have a significant role to play, as long as Arteta can keep him fit. He can be a potent weapon galloping forward and there were clear glimpses of that here. Harnessing that talent while not compromising too much defensive security may be one of the manager’s challenges.

Sources indicate that louie Copley had only been on the pitch for nine minutes – a half-time substitute for Ben White – when the 19-year-old midfielder went down largely unchallenged with what looked like a troubling knee injury. Arteta admitted afterwards that the way the teenager fell to the ground was a concern and he looked in visible pain and distress as he was treated by the medical staff before being helped off the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that the fear will be of some kind of ligament damage and Arteta confirmed Copley would be scanned on Thursday. “Quite worried to be fair for the kid because the mechanism doesn’t look very positive and the symptoms that he already has,” the manager stated. “So we are going to have to wait and see for tomorrow’s scan. Touch wood that is not a bad one.”.

It has been revealed that premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Spanish side Real Betis at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin, with this being the first-ever meeting between the two sides. This is the first time Arsenal have played a pre-season game in Dublin since August 2018, when they drew 1-1 with London rivals Chelsea, with Arsenal winning on penalties.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 in their opening game of pre-season, with new signing Christos Tzolis on the scoresheet in his first appearance for the club. After today, Arsenal have three more games, including the Community Shield, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry on opening night of the new season. They are closing in on a deal for Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes, who is set to become one of Arsenal’s most expensive signings. Mikel Arteta’s side have been dealt a blow ahead of the season with the news that France centre-back William Saliba will miss an extended period due to a back injury. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Real Betis, under the management of former Manchester City boss Manuel Pellegrini, finished fifth in La Liga last season and have therefore qualified for this coming season’s Champions League after a 20-year absence from the competition. Pellegrini has led Betis into European competitions for five consecutive seasons, which includes losing the 2025 Europa Conference League final to Chelsea. They have been busy in pre-season action already having played five games up to this point. They have won four of the five, including a 4-0 victory over Lyon, with just one defeat coming against Granada.

They have a number of former Premier League players in their ranks, including Antony, Giovani Lo Celso, Pablo Fornals and former Arsenal man Hector Bellerin. Real Betis have already played a number of friendlies as they build up to the start of their season, which begins on August 21 when they take on Real Sociedad.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that like Snapchat messages, WhatsApp's "View Once" feature is a great way to send things you don't want living on your friends' devices.
  • It has been revealed that that's now changing.
  • Industry observers note that as WABetaInfo highlights, the first time you use this feature, WhatsApp will present a pop-up explaining the feature, how "View Once text gives you more privacy," and that when you send the message, it'll disappear from the chat after the recipient opens it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that like Snapchat messages, WhatsApp's "View Once" feature is a great way to send things you don't want living on your friends' devices. You can send voice messages, photos, and videos that will "self-destruct" after they're opened, limiting (if not eliminating) the risk of your friends keeping them forever. However, View Once has a major limitation: While WhatsApp will let you send voice memos and images that way, you can't use it to send texts, meaning every one you send will live on (unless you unsend it yourself).

It has been revealed that that's now changing. As reported by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is now beta testing View Once for text messages, too. Soon enough, you'll be able to send voice memos, photos, videos, and texts as one-time-only messages. That way, you can send sensitive information via text—say, a password or an notable account number—without worrying about it persisting. Here's how it works: You craft your text message as you usually do, but rather than tap the send button, you hold it. You'll see the usual "Schedule message" option, but once the feature rolls out, you'll also find a new "View Once" option as well.

Industry observers note that as WABetaInfo highlights, the first time you use this feature, WhatsApp will present a pop-up explaining the feature, how "View Once text gives you more privacy," and that when you send the message, it'll disappear from the chat after the recipient opens it. WhatsApp also explains that recipients cannot share, forward, save, or take screenshots of View Once text messages. Recipients won't see the text appear in the usual chat interface, either; instead, your recipient will need to open the message in a separate window. Once they close this page, the message disappears.

According to recent reports, as mentioned above, this feature is right now in testing, so it's only available to WhatsApp beta testers. What's more, only the Android version of the beta has access at the moment, so iOS beta testers are out of luck. (That said, the WhatsApp iOS beta is perpetually full, so there's not much you could do even if WhatsApp made this test available on iPhone.).

Recent findings suggest that if you have an Android device, you can enroll in the WhatsApp beta to try out "View Once" text messages today. According to WABetaInfo, the feature is live as of WhatsApp version 2.26.45.6. To enroll, open the WhatsApp beta page on the Google Play store and enroll your account in the beta. If you don't have WhatsApp on your phone already, download it here; if you do, reload the page and install the latest patch. This will update your existing WhatsApp app to the latest beta version.

If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Rolling Stone may receive an affiliate commission.

They say mother knows best, and when it comes to gift-giving, mine really does. My mom has always had a flair for whimsy. She’s the kind of woman who would lay an entire tarp across our backyard on the last day of school and stage a food fight, or build a Christmas countdown calendar from scratch, then fill every little compartment with surprises.

It has been revealed that she’s also the reason I learned that the best gifts aren’t necessarily the ones people ask for, but the ones they didn’t even know they needed. Turns out, that lesson would come in handy when I made gift-giving my career.

My mom is truly the best human on the planet. Don’t worry, I’m sure yours is, too. Which is why I want to help you find a present she’ll love when the holidays roll around.

It has been revealed that so, where do you start shopping? I’d steer clear of the obvious. Sure, a robe is nice. A scarf will keep her warm. Another water bottle? She probably has six. You can do better! This is the woman who taught you how to make the most out of life, after all. She deserves something as one-of-a-kind as your relationship. Maybe that’s a cuckoo clock you can build together or a custom garden gnome with her face on it. Whatever fills her cup, there’s something here that’ll make her smile.

I also kept budgets, interests, and personalities in mind, because no two moms — or gift-givers — are alike. According to recent reports, global stock markets have been under pressure as geopolitical tensions have resurfaced in the Middle East. Moreover, investors remain concerned about the sustainability of AI-driven demand and infrastructure spending.

Nonetheless, those looking for attractive stock picks amid the ongoing volatility can gain key insights by tracking the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts. These experts assign ratings after in-depth analysis of a firm's fundamentals, growth opportunities, and risks.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

E-commerce and cloud computing giant Amazon (AMZN) is this week's first pick. Heading into the company's second-quarter earnings, TD Cowen analyst John Blackledge reiterated a buy rating on AMZN stock, citing strength in the Amazon Web Services cloud unit as well as the e-commerce and advertising businesses. The analyst lowered his price target on AMZN stock to $340 from $350 as he revised his estimates and slightly raised his capex projections.

Specifically, Blackledge expects Amazon to report revenue of $200.1 billion, 2% above the Street's consensus, driven by acceleration in AWS and advertising revenue. He also expects the tech giant's e-commerce business to reflect the shifting of Prime Day in the U.S. and other key markets to the second quarter this year, compared with third quarter of last year.

In particular, Blackledge expects AWS revenue to grow 35.5% year-over-year in Q2 2026, marking an acceleration from 28.4% in the prior-year quarter and 3.4% above the Street's expectations. The 5-star analyst expects revenue to be driven by rising generative AI workloads as the manufacturer's significant AI infrastructure spending helps to ease supply constraints.

Regarding third-quarter outlook, Blackledge mentioned, "Our rev and Op Income estimates are 0.3% and 3.2% above consensus, driven by further AWS revenue growth acceleration led by AI demand.".

Blackledge ranks No. 771 among more than 12,300 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 55% of the time, delivering an average return of 11.2%. See Amazon Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

According to recent reports, moving on to semiconductor tech giant Marvell Technology (MRVL). Following several meetings with management, RBC Capital analyst Srini Pajjuri reiterated a buy rating on MRVL stock with a price target of $360.

"Overall, the meetings reinforced our conviction that MRVL can sustain 40%+ growth for the next 3 years, driven by strong AI demand, optical connectivity leadership, and expanding Custom pipeline," stated Pajjuri.

The 5-star analyst added that robust demand and limited supply are giving greater revenue visibility. Pajjuri noted that Marvell's data center business is on track to deliver more than 50% growth this year and next. Also, the growth in the company's networking business is outpacing compute, driven by agentic AI and inferencing workloads.

Meanwhile, Pajjuri noted that optical product lead times have extended to more than six months, while XPU customers are placing purchase orders 12 months in advance. While the analyst kept his estimates unchanged, he sees the possibility of upside for the second half of 2026 from the Optical business, with more significant upside potential for 2027 and 2028 estimates.

Industry observers note that furthermore, Pajjuri noted that Marvell's scale-across offering is emerging as an additional growth catalyst for 2027, while scale-up networking is expected to present a multibillion-dollar greenfield serviceable addressable market. Also, management is upbeat about Marvell's custom business, with the organization targeting more than $10 billion in revenue for 2028, driven by existing programs with Amazon's AWS and Microsoft and multiple XPU attach wins.

Pajjuri ranks No. 88 among more than 12,300 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 75% of the time, delivering an average return of 51.5%. See Marvell Options Activity on TipRanks.

Ahead of second-quarter earnings, Wells Fargo analyst Aaron Rakers reaffirmed a buy rating on AMD stock and raised his price target to $615 from $505, citing "increasing focus on path to +$20/sh. EPS in CY28." The analyst expects AMD to reiterate its confidence in the MI450 series and Helios ramp beginning in the third quarter of 2026.

Recent findings suggest that the 5-star analyst increased his estimates for AMD server CPU revenue to $16.0 billion (up 68% year-over-year), $20.5 billion (up 28%), and $25.0 billion (up 22%) for 2026, 2027, 2028, respectively. Rakers noted that in the previous quarter, AMD increased its server CPU total addressable market estimates to $120 billion by 2030, representing a more than 35% compound annual growth rate.

Rakers expects AMD to comment on an additional rise in server CPU demand since its first-quarter results. #4078. I Tested Pangram to See If It Can Really Detect AI-Generated Content Like It Claims

I Tested Pangram to See If It Can Really Detect AI-Generated Content Like It Claims

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1028 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that we know it can be difficult for human beings to spot AI-generated content, but can detection software fare any better?
  • You'll find arguments on both sides of the debate as to whether or not Pangram's claims stand up.
  • According to recent reports, proponents of Pangram would point to an ongoing reward offer—currently at $3,950—available to anyone who can find a pre-2019 (and pre-LLM) piece of writing that Pangram falsely flags as being AI-written.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that we know it can be difficult for human beings to spot AI-generated content, but can detection software fare any better? Pangram is one of the leaders in the field, promising a "near-zero false positive rate" by looking at "subtle cues" in the writing, based on a training and feedback model comparing human-made content with the AI equivalent.

You'll find arguments on both sides of the debate as to whether or not Pangram's claims stand up. After a short story was flagged by Pangram and then judged to be free from AI, the detection engine has been accused of bias against text from minority writers.

According to recent reports, proponents of Pangram would point to an ongoing reward offer—currently at $3,950—available to anyone who can find a pre-2019 (and pre-LLM) piece of writing that Pangram falsely flags as being AI-written. So far, the reward is unclaimed.

It has been revealed that as the AI detector has recently added AI image and video detection to its capabilities, it seemed a good time to put Pangram's analysis skills to the test for myself. Here's how it performed in the three different content types.

On the human side, I picked out 10 of my most recent articles for Lifehacker, known to be written by a person because I personally wrote them—in the traditional way, I fretted over word choices, went back and changed sentences, and accidentally left in a variety of typos that editors thankfully fixed.

For the AI content, I rotated between ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, and got the LLMs to write 10 articles with the same headlines and the same approximate number of words, for a tech-savvy audience. I even asked the AI apps to vary their language use, so that the output would "read less like an LLM has written it.".

Pangram's AI text detector lets you upload files, but to make the task a little harder, I copied and pasted all of the text into the online article, so it wouldn't be able to rely on any metadata included in the file. The scans got the correct result each and every time: Human-written text came back as 100% human, and AI-written text came back as 100% AI.

Industry observers note that what's more, Pangram was certain about its results. All of the human writing was marked as highly likely to be human, and the vast majority of the AI writing was marked as highly likely to have come from an LLM. There were only a handful of phrases or sentences across thousands of AI words that got a "medium" rather than a "high" ranking for AI.

According to recent reports, now, there have been some edge cases where Pangram has got it wrong—like a poem repeating the same six words thousands of times—but as far as this sample goes, it can't be faulted. Clearly, my writing is too idiosyncratic and too clunky to be confused for the smooth sheen of AI-produced prose.

Industry observers note that to be fair, I do have another advantage over AI: I can actually test out devices and apps in a way that LLM bots can't. ChatGPT can't experiment with One UI 9 (at least not yet), though it can scrape the web for various experiments and tests that real people have done.

According to recent reports, however, I was able to fool Pangram to some extent by alternating AI paragraphs with human-written paragraphs. The text was flagged as AI, but the percentage estimate was typically lower (20-25%) than what it actually was (around 50%). If you're offloading some but not all of your writing to AI, some of it might slip though as real.

In a recent development, image and video detection is the newly introduced string to Pangram's bow, so I sifted through my phone's photo and video library for some pieces of content to test the AI on. Again, I used copy and paste to get the files into Pangram rather than uploading them, to limit how much information the AI detector could get from metadata.

In a recent development, again, all the human-made content was recognized as such, with a very high level of certainty—whether it was complicated crowd shots or simpler images of natural scenes. Presumably, there are even more signals to go off than there are with writing, including camera movements, colors, style, consistency, and composition.

Sources indicate that next up, I generated a few images and videos in Google Gemini and ChatGPT, requesting results that would look as photorealistic and "non-AI" as possible—the resulting files covered people, animals, and buildings. As before, I used copy, paste, and a few screengrabs to try and limit the metadata Pangram had access to.

Here, too, the AI identification was spot on, with all of the artificial content recognized as such, to a high level of confidence. This is perhaps not surprising: I think AI images and especially AI video still have more "tells" than AI writing, especially if you've seen a lot of it, so I wasn't expecting Pangram to fail here.

According to recent reports, I did try experimenting with real photos that had a little bit of AI in them, what with tools like Gemini and ChatGPT now so good at image editing, as well as creating pictures from scratch. These were marked as "unsure" by Pangram, though to cut it some slack, only a small amount of the images were altered.

As with the text, the best way to beat Pangram's detection systems seems to be to include some AI embedded in human-made content. It will most likely still fail the "100% human" test, but the tests I ran demonstrated that Pangram is less certain in these cases, or underestimates the amount of AI there actually is.

Sources indicate that increase the level of AI, and the detection gets more reliable—but if you're only using AI for a small part of whatever it is you're making, it's less worthwhile using AI tools anyway. As far as these tests go, Pangram's claims about accuracy check out, making it a useful tool if you need to ensure something is AI-free.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Recording Academy doesn’t always get it right when it comes to Latin music, but lately they’ve been trying. Last year, voters from the Latin Recording Academy were able to cast ballots in the standard edition, making for a more diverse voting pool. It’s a move that’s already paid off. Earlier this year, at the 2026 awards, Bad Bunny made history with the first Album of the Year win for a full Spanish-language album. Now, with the 2027 Grammy nominations, one of the biggest genres in the U.S. is still front and center — even if some of the nods are perplexing. Let’s take a look at all of the Latin music highlights from this year’s nominations.

Rosalía just made history at the Latin Grammys when she became the first woman to win Album of the Year three times. Now, the Spanish singer is the second-most-decorated nominee for the 2027 Grammys, and she could follow Bad Bunny’s lead with another historic AOTY win. If Rosalía’s Lux snags the highest honor of the night, she would become the first woman to win in the category with a Spanish-language project.

There were a handful of Latin music first-time nominees across categories. Ryan Castro secured two nods in the Best Música Urbana Album, one for his solo LP Hopi Sendé and another for his collaborative album with J Balvin, Omerta. Meanwhile, Argentine musician Milo J earned recognition in the Best Latin Song and Best Latin Rock or Alternative Album categories for his Latin Grammy-winning project La vida era Más Corta. Venezuelan American singer Elena Rose also received her first-ever Grammy nod, in the Best Latin Pop Album category. About that….

… Rose’s nomination leads us to the unfortunate catch-all that the Best Latin Pop Album category became this year. As we stated, the Academy doesn’t always get it right when it comes to Latin music. Nowhere is that more blatant than this category, which is jam-packed with an array of popular Latin artists who make distinct music from each other. Karol G’s alternative album No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto makes some sense here, as does Mon Laferte’s Femme Fatale — but Carín León’s Muda runs the gamut of genres from norteño to salsa and soul. It makes no sense here, and Rawayana’s and Elena Rose’s genre-bending albums don’t really, either. Rather than find a way to honor these impressive works and the widely varied Latin genres they’re pushing forward, the Academy seems to be stuffing them under one confusing umbrella. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

Recent findings suggest that drake is up for Best Latin Song. Yes, you read that right: The rap superstar has received a nod for his Spanish-language feature on Karol G’s “Ahí.” It’s surprising in many ways, but especially considering Drake’s longstanding differences with the Academy; the last time he won a Grammy for one of his own songs, in 2019, he gave a speech about how little the awards mean to him, and he’s chosen not to submit his own work since then. The fact that the Academy nominated “Ahí” rather than Karol’s Bruno Mars collaboration “Still” is also a bit of a head-scratcher. But now Champagne Papi will go up against acts like Ca7riel & Paco Amoroso, Rosalía, Milo J, and Jorge Drexler. Trending Stories Raye, Rosalía, and Ella Langley Lead 2027 Grammy Nominees Jennifer Lopez Teases Latest Music on ‘Fallon’: ‘This Does Feel Like a Happy Era’ Robert Pattinson Is the Next James Bond Watch Buffalo Springfield Come Together for the First Time in Many Years.

One of Latin music’s most sought-after collaborators is being recognized by the Academy once more. Edgar Barrera nabbed a third consecutive nod for Songwriter of the Year, Non-Classical. He’s up against a field that includes Amy Allen and Theron Thomas, both of whom previously beat him. But after working on some of the year’s biggest Latin music projects and writing for Gracie Abrams, could this finally be the year the Recording Academy honors Barrera’s songwriting power?

There’s no denying Latin music’s worldwide takeover — just look at what Shakira and Anitta are doing. Both stars submitted their music beyond the Latin music categories, and they were recognized for continuing to expand their reach. Anitta’s latest album, Equilibrivm, received a nod for Best Global Music Album, while Shakira’s World Cup hit “Dai Dai” was nominated for Best Global Music Performance.

Tech Report: Eight Hacks Every Tidal User Should Know

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1389 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that I recently switched from Apple Music to Tidal, and I'm happy I made the change.
  • Download your playlist as a .txt file.
  • According to recent reports, install Python on your system.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that I recently switched from Apple Music to Tidal, and I'm happy I made the change. The main reason is AI-made music: Tidal has stricter AI filtering than any other major streamer. The second reason is audio quality. While all major music streaming services do basically the same thing, Tidal's focus has always been on streaming music at the highest possible quality. While other streaming services have more or less "caught up" in terms of pure sonic fidelity, Tidal still is better at getting that quality to your speakers, if you know a few tricks.

Download your playlist as a .txt file. You can do this directly from Apple Music under File>Library>Export Playlist. You can't from Spotify, but the free site Exportify will download any of your playlists as a spreadsheet file you can save.

According to recent reports, install Python on your system. Double click "install certificates" in the folder that opens after installation.

It has been revealed that download this script. Save it in the same file as your playlist.

It has been revealed that run the script: (For Mac, open Terminal. For Windows, go to the Command prompt. Type python3 on a Mac or py on Windows.) Drag the script into the terminal window and press enter. It should ask you to drag your downloaded playlist into the window next.

In a recent development, sign in to Tidal. Hit "Approve" to give permission for Tidal to run the script.

Have a banana. The script is going to search for all the songs on your playlist and match them to Tidal's library, so it can take a little while. I tested it with a playlist from Apple Music with 2,397 songs. It took about 20 minutes and found 2,362 of my tracks, a 99% success rate.

Fix the leftovers: The program creates two separate text files for "orphans." One is songs it couldn't find and one is songs it might be worth double-checking manually.

If everything goes well, your large playlist should be available on Tidal.

Note: The script uses a community-created library to talk to Tidal, so it could stop working if Tidal changes things up.

Sources indicate that like most streaming services, Tidal has a "heart" button called "add to my collection." You can click on any track, album, or playlist to "like" and saved it. But Tidal also has a separate, somewhat mysterious "Save for Later" option that puts songs, albums, and playlists into a separate collection. There are a couple reasons for this. First, it keeps a running list of new-to-you music waiting for you on a rainy day, and secondly, it (presumably) affects your recommendation algorithm differently. While Tidal isn't open about every detail of its recommendation algorithm, I assume "save for later" has less weight (if any) on your future recommendations than "add to my collection.".

Recent findings suggest that on Tidal, tracks that are 100% AI-generated get an "AI" badge, earn no royalties, and are never placed on a Tidal-curated playlist. People can flip a switch in Settings to either allow or disallow AI content, too. Simple, but there's a bit of nuance that goes beyond the on/off switch. You have to set the AI-toggle separately on each device you use Tidal on, even if it's the same account. I guess this is so I can listen to AI music in my car but not at my desk? Sadly, AI detection is not a science, so some AI-made, and partly AI-made, tracks may still get through.

If you're streaming music from a music app through Bluetooth, the output is automatically compressed to a lower quality, and your phone stays in charge, so a phone call or a notification can interrupt your music. But Tidal's Tidal Connect feature skips the middleman. Music streams directly from your wifi to your speaker and your phone becomes a remote control, so you can take a call, go for a walk, and even run out of phone battery and the music will keep playing.

Have an external device with Tidal Connect compatibility.

Make sure your speaker or other output device and phone or computer are on the same wifi network.

Pick your speaker on your wifi network.

Click the icon again to switch back to your phone.

It has been revealed that plenty of wifi speakers don’t support Tidal Connect, so check before you buy. Tidal keeps the full list of supported devices on its site. There's everything there from WiiM Mini—a $99 small box that adds Tidal Connect to speakers you already own—to dCS components that cost more than a car.

Industry observers note that tidal Connect isn't the only way to get the highest quality audio from Tidal. You can go for an old school, wired path like I have. I play audio from my desktop and route it directly to a mixer via USB. Here's the set-up:.

Settings > Streaming > Audio Quality: Max.

Sound Output: choose your mixer as the output device instead of your computer’s speakers.

It has been revealed that exclusive Mode: On. It’s under Sound Output > More Settings. Tidal sends audio straight to the mixer at each track’s native sample rate, without your computer resampling it or mixing in system sounds.

Force Volume. It's in the desktop app next to Exclusive Mode, under Settings > Streaming > Sound Output > More Settings. Force Volume means Tidal will always output at the highest volume. You'll be controlling the actual volume from your mixer.

Set your levels with the mixer’s faders.

To check what your mixer can handle, look at its maximum sample rate:.

According to recent reports, mac: Open Audio MIDI Setup (in Applications > Utilities), click your mixer, and open the Format menu. The highest number listed is your ceiling.

Windows: Go to Settings > System > Sound, click your mixer, and look under Output settings > Format.

Industry observers note that my cheap-ass mixer tops out a 16-bit/48kHz which is CD quality, but not Tidal's top of 24-bit/192kHz, but at least I can control the EQ. Speaking of...

It's much cooler to turn dials than mess with computer settings. Tidal doesn’t have an equalizer, so if you’re using Tidal Connect or a wired connection, you'll need something to shape the sound. Here are some options:.

Industry observers note that your computer: System-wide EQ apps, like Equalizer APO on Windows or SoundSource on Mac, can adjust Tidal’s output. They don’t work with Tidal Connect though, which bypasses your computer’s audio processing.

Your speaker’s app: If you use a Tidal Connect speaker or streamer, it probably has a companion app for EQ.

A mixer or audio interface: Channel EQ knobs let you adjust bass, mids, and treble by hand, in real time.

Your speakers: Many powered speakers and studio monitors have low and high controls on the back.

A stereo receiver or amp: Old-school bass and treble knobs still work in 2026.

Most of Tidal's catalog streams as "better-than-CD quality" FLAC files at every subscription tier, so you might be inclined to click "play music at highest quality on everything." but settings are only as good as the gear you're using, and there are times when lower quality is the right choice. Here's when to turn down the settings:.

When you're in your car: CarPlay and Bluetooth cut audio down to CD quality or less before it reaches your speaker, and with road noises, it usually doesn't matter anyway, so turn the streaming down to "High" instead of "Max." Or download your playlist before you leave, if you must have "as good as possible" audio.

You have a data cap and are off wifi. Top quality audio requires huge file transfer, so set your mobile data to High or Low and save Max for wifi.

Your connection is spotty: To avoid buffering, a lower setting keeps the music playing.

According to recent reports, this isn't a universal hack, but some Android phones have microSD card slots, which can save you a lot of hassle if you're downloading a lot of audio files—an album at high quality might top 1GB, so having an external source will save you a ton of hassle. If your phone has a microSD card slot, go to Tidal's settings, find "download destination" and choose the memory card.
